zh_title: PreForceVision：基于物理引导的光学螺栓头形变预紧力估计方法
translation: 螺栓预紧力是螺栓连接中决定性的功能量，因为它决定了外部载荷是通过摩擦夹紧还是直接通过螺栓传递。现有的预紧力测量技术，包括应变片螺栓、力垫圈、超声波方法和螺栓长度测量，在某些应用中很有效，但需要额外的硬件、耦合、校准或连接修改。这限制了其在大规模标准紧固件中的可扩展性，并促使人们寻求非接触式光学方法。本文提出了PreForceVision，一个基于物理引导的光学框架，用于从螺栓头正面的预紧力诱导表面形变中估计螺栓预紧力。该方法将预紧力估计视为一个逆形变-力问题，其中从参考-加载图像对中提取光学可访问的螺栓头表面形变，并将其与内部预紧力状态相关联。对M16强度等级8.8螺栓的初步结果表明，在90千牛顿（\SI{90}{\kilo\newton}）下，模拟的头部表面压陷约为12微米（\SI{12}{\micro\meter}），应变片测量值具有相当的量级，光学3D测量的中心压陷约为10到20微米（\SIrange{10}{20}{\micro\meter}）。其贡献在于一种基于物理引导的光学方法论，结合了受控图像对采集、基于DIC或光流的形变提取、多模态验证以及用于受控条件下粗略预紧力估计的不确定性感知的回归。
tldr: 提出了一种名为PreForceVision的非接触式光学方法，通过捕捉螺栓头表面的微小形变来估计螺栓预紧力。
ai_comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的基于物理引导的光学螺栓预紧力估计方法，通过螺栓头表面的微小形变实现非接触式测量，克服了传统方法需要额外硬件和改装的局限性，在工业结构健康监测中具有较大的应用潜力。
motivation: 现有的螺栓预紧力测量技术（如应变片螺栓、力垫圈、超声波方法和螺栓长度测量等）虽然在某些应用中有效，但需要额外的硬件、耦合、校准或接头改造，限制了其在大量标准紧固件中的可扩展性，因此需要一种非接触式光学方法。
method: 提出PreForceVision框架，将预紧力估计视为逆形变-力问题，利用参考-负载图像对通过DIC或光流法提取可光学访问的螺栓头表面形变，结合多模态验证和不确定性感知的回归进行预紧力估计。
results: 对M16强度等级8.8的螺栓进行的初步结果显示，在90 kN时模拟的头部正面压陷约为12微米，应变计测量值与其量级相当，光学3D测量的中心压陷约为10到20微米。
conclusion: PreForceVision通过将光学形变测量与物理引导回归相结合，为螺栓预紧力的非接触式估计提供了一条可行的新途径。

title: Pangenome Peeling: Decomposing Weighted Adjacencies into Path-Forest Genomes
authors: Alitzel López Sánchez, Jiazhen Leng, Natasha Ivanova, Lingling Jin, David Sankoff
abstract:
One aspect of pangenome analysis that has received little attention is the recovery of the individual genomes that gave rise to a pangenome graph. While substantial effort has focused on constructing pangenomes from collections of genomes, the inverse problem remains largely unexplored: given a pangenome represented as a set of weighted adjacencies, can we reconstruct the constituent linear genomes that underlie it?
  Thus we introduce the pangenome peeling problem, which seeks to decompose a weighted adjacency graph into a collection of linear genomes whose combined adjacencies reproduce the observed edge weights. This problem is particularly relevant when considering ancestral pangenomes, where the graph structure may be known or inferred, but the underlying genomes are not.
  As a first step toward addressing this problem, we formally define pangenome peeling and derive a lower bound on the minimum number of genomes required to explain a given weighted adjacency graph. We then present two reconstruction methods: one based on the sequential addition of edges and a second based on extracting maximum-spanning-tree structures. Both methods produce genome collections that exactly explain the input adjacency data.
  To evaluate the recovered sets of genomes, we compare them to the set of input genomes using a maximum-weight matching framework based on the double-cut-and-join distance with indels. Here the maximum-spanning tree approach is superior, producing sets of constituent genomes close to the simulations while the sequential addition of edges approach yields constituent genomes increasingly divergent from the input as genomes sizes increase.
comment: This is an extended version of the article of the same name submitted to the RECOMB 2027 conference
zh_title: 泛基因组剥离：将加权邻接分解为路径森林基因组
translation:
泛基因组分析中较少受到关注的一个方面是恢复产生泛基因组图的个体基因组。虽然大量工作集中于从基因组集合构建泛基因组，但逆问题仍大多未被探索：给定表示为一组加权邻接的泛基因组，我们能否重构支撑它的组成线性基因组？
因此，我们引入了泛基因组剥离问题，旨在将加权邻接图分解为一组线性基因组，其组合邻接能够重现观察到的边权重。当考虑祖先泛基因组时，这个问题尤其相关，此时图结构可能是已知或推断的，但底层的基因组未知。
作为解决该问题的首要步骤，我们正式定义了泛基因组剥离，并推导了解释给定加权邻接图所需的最小基因组数量的下界。随后，我们提出了两种重构方法：一种基于边的顺序添加，另一种基于提取最大生成树结构。这两种方法都能产生准确解释输入邻接数据的基因组集合。
为了评估恢复的基因组集，我们使用基于带有插入缺失的双切连接与插入缺失距离的最大权重匹配框架，将其与输入基因组集进行比较。结果表明最大生成树方法更优，产生的组成基因组接近模拟数据，而边的顺序添加方法随着基因组大小的增加，生成的组成基因组与输入的偏离越来越大。
tldr: 本文研究了从泛基因组图恢复原始线性基因组的逆问题，提出了泛基因组剥离问题，并证明基于最大生成树的方法能有效重构底层基因组。
ai_comments: 该论文首次探讨了从泛基因组图中恢复原始个体线性基因组的逆问题，提出了“泛基因组剥离（Pangenome Peeling）”问题，并开发了基于最大生成树的方法，在模拟实验中表现优异，对祖先泛基因组推断具有重要意义。
motivation: 尽管构建泛基因组的研究较多，但从泛基因组图恢复其构成的个体线性基因组这一逆问题（尤其是祖先泛基因组）受到的关注较少，缺乏有效方法。
method: 正式定义了泛基因组剥离问题，推导了解释给定加权邻接图所需的最小基因组数量下界，并提出了两种重构方法：基于边顺序添加的方法和基于提取最大生成树结构的方法。利用基于双切连接与插入缺失距离的最大权重匹配框架进行评估。
results: 基于最大生成树的方法表现更优，能够产生与模拟数据接近的组成基因组集合，而基于边顺序添加的方法生成的基因组随基因组大小增加而偏离输入。
conclusion: 论文提出了泛基因组剥离问题及相关重构方法，其中基于最大生成树的方法在恢复底层线性基因组方面表现出优越性。

title: Multimodal Training with Knowledge Traction for Video Anomaly Detection
authors: Xiao Tan
abstract: The task of weakly supervised video anomaly detection is challenging. Existing approaches mainly model video frame features and determine whether anomalies are present based on their magnitudes. In this work, we propose a novel method that incorporates external knowledge into training to improve model performance, robustness, and generalization. We leverage textual prompts and a large language model (LLM) to establish prior information for the specific task, and employ dictionary learning to normalize and compress this information. Moreover, during experiments, we observed inconsistencies in the textual descriptions extracted from similar video frames by image caption models. To address this, we devise a method that leverages an LLM and auxiliary information to ensure consistency in the textual descriptions of similar frames within a video. Finally, we introduce a feature processing approach that incorporates prior knowledge and cross-modal attention mechanisms. This approach learns the relationships and characteristics among different modalities to construct more accurate and reliable feature representations, thereby improving the accuracy and stability of downstream tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our method surpasses other state-of-the-art approaches.
zh_title: 基于知识牵引的多模态视频异常检测训练方法
translation: 弱监督视频异常检测任务极具挑战性。现有方法主要对视频帧特征进行建模，并根据其幅度大小来判断异常的出现。在这项工作中，我们提出了一种新颖的方法，将外部知识融入训练中，以提高模型的性能、鲁棒性和泛化能力。我们利用文本提示和一个大语言模型（LLM）来为特定任务建立先验信息，并采用字典学习对这些信息进行归一化和压缩。此外，在实验过程中，我们观察到图像描述模型从相似视频帧中提取的文本描述存在不一致性。为了解决这个问题，我们设计了一种方法，利用大语言模型和辅助信息来确保视频中相似帧文本描述的一致性。最后，我们引入了一种结合先验知识和跨模态注意力机制的特征处理方法。该方法学习不同模态之间的关系和特征，以构建更准确、更可靠的特征表示，从而提高下游任务的准确性和稳定性。实验结果表明，我们的方法超越了其他先进的方法。
tldr: 本文提出了一种利用大语言模型提供先验知识和跨模态注意力的视频异常检测方法，显著超越了现有技术。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地将外部知识（大语言模型和文本提示）引入弱监督视频异常检测中，并通过字典学习和跨模态注意力机制增强了模型的鲁棒性与泛化能力，展现出优于现有方法的性能。
motivation: 现有的弱监督视频异常检测方法主要对视频帧特征建模并依据幅度判断异常，缺乏外部知识的辅助，导致模型在鲁棒性和泛化能力上面临挑战。
method: 利用文本提示和大语言模型建立任务先验信息，采用字典学习对其归一化和压缩；设计方法确保相似帧文本描述的一致性；提出结合先验知识与跨模态注意力机制的特征处理方法构建精确的特征表示。
results: 实验结果表明，该方法超越了其他先进的同类方法，有效提升了下游任务的准确性和稳定性。
conclusion: 通过引入大语言模型构建先验知识、解决文本描述不一致性问题以及采用跨模态注意力机制，本文提出的方法显著提升了弱监督视频异常检测的准确性和稳定性，优于当前主流方法。

title: Marginal-Nonuniform Multiclass Learning
authors: Nataly Brukhim, Steve Hanneke, Amirreza Shaeiri, Maximilian Thiessen
abstract: We study the problem of multiclass classification within the framework of marginal-nonuniform learning, where the constants in the learning rate may depend on the unknown marginal distribution generating the unlabeled data, but not on the target concept. This notion naturally lies between classical PAC learning, where the constants are independent of both the marginal distribution and the target concept, and more recent universal learning, where the constants may depend on both. We give a complete characterization of the optimal marginal-nonuniform learning rates, establishing a fundamental trichotomy: exponential, linear, and arbitrarily slow rates. This characterization is witnessed by a new combinatorial dimension, termed the uncentered DS-eluder dimension. A key ingredient in the upper-bound proofs is a set of new distributional exhaustion lemmas that exploit the sequential nature of this dimension and may be of independent interest.
zh_title: 边际非均匀多分类学习
translation: 我们研究了边际非均匀学习框架下的多分类分类问题。在该框架中，学习速率中的常数可以依赖于生成未标记数据的未知边际分布，但不依赖于目标概念。这一概念自然地介于经典PAC学习（其中常数与边际分布和目标概念均无关）与近期的通用学习（其中常数可以同时依赖于两者）之间。我们对最优边际非均匀学习速率给出了完整的刻画，确立了一个基本的三分法：指数速率、线性速率和任意缓慢的速率。这种刻画由一个被称为“去中心化DS-eluder维度”的新组合维度所证实。上界证明的一个关键要素是一组利用该维度序列性质的新分布引理，这些引理可能具有独立的学术价值。
tldr: 论文在多分类学习中提出了边际非均匀学习框架，通过全新的去中心化DS-eluder维度，完整刻画了指数、线性及任意缓慢的最优学习速率三分法。
ai_comments: 该论文在多分类学习框架下引入了边际非均匀学习的概念，介于经典PAC学习与通用学习之间，通过引入“去中心化DS-eluder维度”实现了对最优学习速率的完全刻画，具有很高的理论价值。
motivation: 为了在独立于目标概念但依赖边际分布的边际非均匀学习框架下，研究多分类分类问题，并填补经典PAC学习与现代通用学习之间的理论空白。
method: 通过引入一种名为“去中心化DS-eluder维度”的新组合维度，并利用一组能够利用该维度序列性质的新分布耗尽引理来证明上界。
results: 建立了边际非均匀多分类学习速率的基本三分法（指数级、线性级和任意缓慢级），并给出了最优学习速率的完全刻画。
conclusion: 论文成功刻画了边际非均匀多分类学习的最优学习速率，揭示了指数级、线性级和任意缓慢级的三分法，并引入了新的组合维度和分布耗尽引理。

title: CoMoFlow: Controllable Protein Conformational Ensemble Generation via Explicit Collective-Mode Modeling
authors: Yusong Wang, Zheyuan Gu, Ailiang Lin, Minghao Shao, Yicheng Xu, Jiang Cai, Prayag Tiwari, Mingkun Xu
abstract: Protein conformational ensemble generation aims to efficiently characterize the structural variations accessible to a protein beyond a single static structure. Recent flow-based methods efficiently generate conformational ensembles, but they model coordinated structural variation implicitly, which can limit ensemble fidelity and hinder direct control. To address this limitation, we propose CoMoFlow, a controllable framework for generating protein backbone conformational ensembles by explicitly modeling collective variation. CoMoFlow constructs protein-specific collective modes from the equilibrium structure, learns the distribution of their coefficients across the molecular dynamics (MD) ensemble, and uses sampled collective variations to guide SE(3) flow matching through feature conditioning and prior recentering. Experiments on ATLAS and de novo proteins show that CoMoFlow improves reconstruction of MD conformational distributions and coordinated structural variation relative to strong flow-based baselines, while enabling direct control over targeted conformational changes.
zh_title: CoMoFlow：通过显式集体模式建模实现可控蛋白质构象系综生成
translation: 蛋白质构象系综生成旨在高效表征蛋白质除了单一静态结构之外可及的结构变异。最近基于流的方法能够高效生成构象系综，但它们对协同结构变异进行隐式建模，这可能限制系综保真度并阻碍直接控制。为了解决这一局限性，我们提出了CoMoFlow，一个通过显式建模集体变异来生成蛋白质骨架构象系综的可控框架。CoMoFlow从平衡结构构建蛋白质特异性的集体模式，学习它们在分子动力学（MD）系综中的系数分布，并利用采样得到的集体变异通过特征条件化和先验重新中心化来引导SE(3)流匹配。在ATLAS和从头设计蛋白质上的实验表明，与强大的流基线相比，CoMoFlow改善了MD构象分布和协同结构变异的重建，同时实现了对目标构象变化的直接控制。
tldr: 提出了一种名为CoMoFlow的新框架，通过显式建模集体模式并结合SE(3)流匹配，实现了高保真且可控的蛋白质构象系综生成。
ai_comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的基于显式集体模式建模的蛋白质构象系综生成框架（CoMoFlow），有效解决了现有基于流的方法无法显式控制协同结构变化的局限性，在模拟MD构象分布和直接控制目标构象变化方面展现出显著优势。
motivation: 现有的基于流的方法在生成蛋白质构象系综时隐式地对协同结构变异进行建模，这限制了系综的保真度，并阻碍了对其的直接控制。
method: 从平衡结构构建蛋白质特异性集体模式，学习其在分子动力学（MD）系综中的系数分布，并通过特征条件化和先验重新中心化，利用采样得到的集体变异来指导SE(3)流匹配。
results: 在ATLAS和从头设计（de novo）蛋白质上的实验表明，CoMoFlow相比强大的流基线方法，在重建MD构象分布和协同结构变异方面均有所改善，同时能够直接控制目标构象的变化。
conclusion: CoMoFlow通过显式建模集体模式并结合SE(3)流匹配，成功实现了高保真的蛋白质构象系综生成与直接调控。

title: CID: Measuring Cognitive Work Through Semantic State Change
authors: Ron Fulbright
abstract: Traditional information theory provides powerful tools for analyzing statistical properties of information but offers limited insight into meaning and semantic transformation. It has never been possible to quantify the meaning of an arbitrary piece of information. Large language models represent information as vectors embedded within high-dimensional semantic spaces, enabling meaning to be analyzed geometrically. This paper defines semantic state as the vector representation of information within a model's semantic space and defines cognitive work as the transformation between semantic states, movement through semantic space. To quantify this transformation, we introduce the Contextual Information Differential (CID), a covariance-aware metric based on Mahalanobis distance measuring semantic displacement relative to the structure of the embedding manifold. By treating meaning as a geometric property of semantic space, CID provides a practical method for measuring semantic change, cognitive transformation, and information processing. This framework establishes a foundation for analyzing cognitive processing, learning, reasoning, knowledge generation, synthetic expertise, and human/AI collaboration through implementation-independent measurement of semantic state change in both human and artificial systems.
zh_title: CID：通过语义状态变化测量认知工作
translation: 传统信息理论为分析信息的统计特性提供了强大的工具，但对意义和语义转换的洞察有限。它从未能对任意一条信息的意义进行量化。大型语言模型将信息表示为嵌入高维语义空间中的向量，从而使意义能够被几何分析。本文将语义状态定义为信息在模型语义空间中的向量表示，并将认知工作定义为语义状态之间的转换，即在语义空间中的移动。为了量化这种转换，我们引入了上下文信息差分（Contextual Information Differential, CID），这是一种基于马哈拉诺比斯距离的协方差感知度量，用于测量相对于嵌入流形结构的语义位移。通过将意义视为语义空间的一种几何属性，CID提供了一种测量语义变化、认知转换和信息处理的实用方法。这个框架为通过对人类和人工智能系统中语义状态变化的独立于实现的测量，分析认知处理、学习、推理、知识生成、合成专业知识以及人机协作奠定了基础。
tldr: 本文引入了CID，一种基于大型语言模型语义空间中马哈拉诺比斯距离的度量，用于量化语义状态变化，从而衡量认知工作和信息处理。
ai_comments: 这篇论文的创新之处在于它弥补了传统信息理论在处理语义方面的局限性与现代大型语言模型几何表示之间的鸿沟。CID提供了一种可量化的方式来测量“意义变化”或“认知工作”，这对于理解人工智能和人类认知可能具有深远的影响。其重要性在于为分析复杂的认知过程提供了一个基础框架。
motivation: 传统信息理论在分析信息统计特性方面功能强大，但对意义和语义转换的洞察有限，无法量化任意信息的意义。大型语言模型将信息表示为高维语义空间中的向量，使得意义可以被几何分析。
method: 该论文将语义状态定义为信息在模型语义空间中的向量表示，并将认知工作定义为语义状态之间的转换（即在语义空间中的移动）。为量化这种转换，引入了上下文信息差分（Contextual Information Differential, CID），这是一种基于马哈拉诺比斯距离的协方差感知度量，用于测量相对于嵌入流形结构的语义位移。
results: 通过将意义视为语义空间的一种几何属性，CID提供了一种测量语义变化、认知转换和信息处理的实用方法。
conclusion: 该框架通过对人类和人工智能系统中语义状态变化的独立于实现的测量，为分析认知处理、学习、推理、知识生成、合成专业知识以及人机协作奠定了基础。

title: Query-Guided RoPE Modulation for Lost-in-the-Middle Mitigation in Long-Context LLMs
authors: Peiyu Zhang, Heng Ping, Shinibali Bhattacharyya, Anwesan Pal, Nikos Kanakaris, Kevin Cheang, Shixuan Li, Wei Yang, Paul Bogdan
abstract: Long-context language models often neglect information in the middle of the input, a phenomenon known as "lost-in-the-middle". Part of this gap may stem from the long-range decay of rotary position embedding (RoPE), which weakens the positional signal between distant tokens. Existing input compression deletes low-importance tokens, and attention reweighting acts only after RoPE has weakened this signal. RoPE-level methods modify positions directly but apply the same remapping to every query. To address these limitations, we propose QGPM (Query-Guided Positional Modulation), a training-free method that reshapes RoPE positions using query relevance from the model's own attention heads. QGPM builds a broad relevance map for lower layers and a sharp one for upper layers. Low-relevance tokens advance by less than one position on fast-rotating planes, pulling relevant evidence toward the query. Slow-rotating planes keep the original layout, with every token in place. Experiments on NoLiMa and RULER with multiple context lengths show that QGPM improves over base models and strong baselines, with the largest gains on retrieval tasks, and generalizes across multiple backbones. Our code is available at https://github.com/iZHpy/QGPM.

title: Optimal Regret for Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade
authors: Matteo Castiglioni, Anna Lunghi, Alberto Marchesi
abstract: Learning to profit from trade requires learning both sides of a market: what a seller is willing to accept and what a buyer is willing to pay. We study repeated bilateral trade, where an intermediary posts a purchase price to a seller and a sale price to a buyer whose valuations are drawn from an unknown joint distribution. Trade occurs only if both parties accept their respective prices, in which case the intermediary earns the difference between the two prices. The intermediary observes only whether trade occurs, without observing either valuation. We show that learning both sides of the market is no harder, in terms of regret, than learning just one. Specifically, we design an algorithm achieving regret $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{2/3})$ against the best fixed pair of prices, matching, up to logarithmic factors, the classical lower bound for one-dimensional dynamic pricing. Our result shows that the classical one-dimensional regret rate survives the transition to two dimensions, raising the question of whether this absence of a curse of dimensionality extends to arbitrarily high dimensions.

title: Towards Sustainable Federated Learning via Carbon-Aware Client Selection
authors: Wentao Gao, Omid Tavallaie, Albert Y. Zomaya
abstract: The Information/Communication Technology (ICT) industry is severely challenging the global environment due to the sharply rising carbon emissions generated by machine learning (ML) workloads. Federated Learning (FL) is one of the prominent distributed ML systems used in applications with billions of client devices, such as Google Gboard and Apple Siri. Nearly half of the total carbon footprint in FL originates from client-side computation during local training. However, existing client selection strategies in FL primarily focus on minimizing energy consumption rather than carbon emissions, despite the fact that carbon impact depends not only on computational load but also on the underlying carbon intensity of the energy source. In this paper, we address this gap by proposing a carbon-aware fair client selection strategy (CA-FCS) designed to minimize the carbon emissions associated with model training on client devices. In contrast to existing approaches for reducing carbon emissions in FL, we incorporate hourly carbon intensity and a realistic energy consumption model developed using empirical measurements from Google Pixel smartphones to estimate client-side carbon emissions in FL. Since repeatedly selecting low-carbon clients may reduce data diversity and degrade global model performance, particularly under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data settings, CA-FCS incorporates fairness into client selection to mitigate this issue. We conduct extensive experiments under realistic FL settings for mobile devices, where client participation is constrained by device availability conditions, such as charging status and Wi-Fi connectivity. The results demonstrate that our method reduces client-side carbon emissions by up to 46% while maintaining competitive model accuracy.
zh_title: 通过碳感知客户端选择迈向可持续的联邦学习
translation: 信息与通信技术（ICT）行业由于机器学习（ML）工作负载产生的碳排放急剧上升，对全球环境构成了严峻挑战。联邦学习（FL）是诸如谷歌Gboard和苹果Siri等拥有数十亿客户端设备的应用程序中所使用的重要分布式ML系统之一。联邦学习中近一半的总碳足迹源于本地训练期间的客户端计算。然而，现有的联邦学习客户端选择策略主要集中于最小化能耗而非碳排放，尽管事实是碳影响不仅取决于计算负载，还取决于能源底层的基础碳强度。在本文中，我们提出了一种碳感知公平客户端选择策略（CA-FCS），旨在最小化与客户端设备模型训练相关的碳排放，从而填补这一研究空白。与现有的减少联邦学习碳排放的方法不同，我们结合了每小时碳强度以及使用谷歌Pixel智能手机实测数据开发的真实能耗模型来估计联邦学习中的客户端碳排放。由于重复选择低碳客户端可能会降低数据多样性并退化全局模型性能，特别是在非独立同分布（non-IID）数据设置下，CA-FCS在客户端选择中融入了公平性以缓解该问题。我们在移动设备的真实FL设置下进行了广泛的实验，其中客户端参与受到设备可用性条件（如充电状态和Wi-Fi连接）的限制。结果表明，我们的方法在保持具有竞争力的模型准确率的同时，将客户端碳排放减少了高达46%。
tldr: 本文提出了一种碳感知且兼顾公平性的联邦学习客户端选择策略（CA-FCS），通过利用实时碳强度和真实设备能耗模型，在维持模型精度的同时将客户端碳排放最高减少了46%。
ai_comments: 该论文切中当前绿色人工智能（Green AI）的热点，将碳感知（Carbon-awareness）引入联邦学习的客户端选择中，不仅考虑了碳强度的时间动态性，还兼顾了非独立同分布（non-IID）数据下的公平性，具有较高的实用价值和创新性。
motivation: 尽管联邦学习中约有一半的碳足迹来自客户端的本地训练计算，但现有的客户端选择策略大多关注最小化能耗而非碳排放，且忽视了能源碳强度的时空波动性以及过度偏好低碳客户端导致的模型性能下降和公平性问题。
method: 提出了一种名为CA-FCS的碳感知公平客户端选择策略，结合了每小时碳强度、基于Google Pixel智能手机实测数据的真实能耗模型，并在客户端选择中引入公平性机制以应对non-IID数据带来的挑战。
results: 在移动设备的真实联邦学习设置下进行的广泛实验表明，该方法在保持具有竞争力的模型准确率的同时，最多可减少46%的客户端侧碳排放。
conclusion: 本文提出的碳感知公平客户端选择策略（CA-FCS）有效解决了联邦学习中客户端计算带来的碳排放问题，在大幅度减少碳排放的同时确保了模型性能和训练公平性。

title: Solver-Free Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Edge Selection
authors: Xinda Zheng, Frits de Nijs, Edward Lam
abstract: Decision-focused learning trains prediction models to improve downstream decisions, but many methods require costly solver calls or optimal-solution labels. We propose a solver-free decision-focused learning framework for NP-hard edge-selection problems with uncertain parameters in the objective, the constraints, or both. A neural optimization layer is first trained without solution labels, using problem objectives and constraint penalties. Graph-informed edge scoring and iterative refinement encourage concentrated and structurally consistent continuous decisions. The layer is then frozen, and a prediction model is trained through its continuous output using a problem-specific loss evaluated under observed parameters. At deployment, the predictor, optimization layer, and a lightweight decoder produce decisions without solving the original NP-hard problem. Experiments on the asymmetric traveling salesperson and endpoint-free orienteering problems show consistently better decision quality than prediction-focused learning and improvements over most evaluated decision-focused baselines. Our framework requires less training time than the evaluated decision-focused baselines, even when optimization-layer pretraining is included. Neural deployment also produces decisions faster than solver-based deployment, offering a better quality-efficiency trade-off. The layer also reduces training cost in existing decision-focused methods when used as an approximate optimization oracle.

title: Deliberate Pacing for Human Oversight in Agentic Software Development
authors: Tobias Reichel, Michèle Stassen, Anamaria Mojica-Hanke, Maria Teresa Baldassarre, Sebastian Baltes, Alexander Serebrenik, Steffen Herbold
abstract: Agentic AI increasingly enables software development activities to proceed without continuous human involvement. While this autonomy may accelerate development, it also raises questions about when developers can meaningfully oversee software development done by agents. We propose deliberate pacing: intentionally adjusting when and how autonomous development proceeds to preserve opportunities for meaningful oversight. Drawing on an exploratory multivocal literature review of 20 sources, we identify three factors motivating this vision: changing relative costs of human involvement, the timing of oversight opportunities, and interdependencies between pacing decisions across the software development life cycle. We argue that neither uninterrupted autonomy nor frequent human intervention is universal. Instead, pacing should balance opportunities to understand and influence consequential decisions against costs in human attention, development time, and rework. We outline a research agenda to investigate when deliberate pacing is beneficial, how intervention timing affects oversight, and how pacing decisions interact across development activities.
zh_title: 为 Agentic 软件开发中的人工监督而进行的刻意调速
translation: Agentic AI 越来越多地使软件开发活动能够在没有持续人工介入的情况下进行。虽然这种自主性可能会加速开发，但它也引发了关于开发人员何时能够有意义地监督代理进行的软件开发的问题。我们提出了刻意调速：有意调整自主开发何时以及如何进行，以保留有意义监督的机会。借鉴对 20 份文献进行的一次探索性多方文献回顾，我们确定了促成这一愿景的三个因素：人工介入相对成本的变化、监督机会的时机以及贯穿软件开发生命周期的调速决策之间的相互依赖性。我们认为，不间断的自主性或频繁的人工干预都不是普遍适用的。相反，调速应在理解和影响关键决策的机会与人力、开发时间以及返工成本之间取得平衡。我们概述了一项研究议程，以调查何时进行刻意调速是有益的，干预时机如何影响监督，以及调速决策如何在开发活动中相互作用。
tldr: Agentic AI 正在加速软件开发，但缺乏人类的持续监督。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了“刻意调速”——一种通过调整自主开发的时机和方式来保留有意义的监督机会的方法。研究表明，应该平衡监督机会和开发成本，而不是不间断的自主或频繁的人工干预。未来研究将集中于确定刻意调速的益处、干预时机的影响以及跨开发活动的调速决策的相互作用。
ai_comments: 这项研究提出了一个新颖且重要的方法来解决 Agentic AI 在软件开发中的监督挑战。通过“刻意调速”的概念，研究强调了在自主开发过程中策略性地整合人工监督的重要性，这与完全自主或频繁干预的极端做法不同。多方文献回顾的方法增加了研究的广度和深度。然而，实际应用中的具体调控机制和量化评估仍有待进一步研究。
motivation: 随着 Agentic AI 在软件开发中的应用日益广泛，如何在代理进行开发时保留有意义的人工监督是一个关键问题。研究动机在于，完全自主或过于频繁的人工干预都可能不是最优解，需要一种新的方法来平衡开发效率和监督质量。
method: 通过对 20 份文献进行探索性的多方文献回顾，识别出影响该愿景的三个关键因素：人工参与成本的变化、监督机会的时机以及软件开发生命周期中不同调速决策之间的相互依赖性。
results: 研究结果表明，不应采用不间断的自主开发或频繁的人工干预。相反，调速应在理解和影响关键决策的机会与人力、开发时间和返工成本之间取得平衡。
conclusion: 为了在 Agentic AI 驱动的软件开发中实现有效的人工监督，需要采用“刻意调速”的方法，该方法能够平衡监督机会与开发成本。未来的研究应进一步探索这种方法的具体实施和影响。

title: Lightweight Path-Aware Frontier Re-ranking for LiDAR-Based UAV Exploration
authors: Duc Manh Do, Thanh Nguyen Canh, Ngoc Minh Do, Mai Thanh Thai, Xiem HoangVan
abstract: Autonomous 3D exploration with UAVs requires efficient target selection under limited flight time and onboard computation. In conventional Euclidean-distance-based frontier pipelines, geometric distance may poorly represent the actual collision-free travel cost in cluttered environments, leading to inefficient frontier choices. This paper presents a lightweight path-aware frontier re-ranking method for LiDAR-based UAV exploration. The method first retains a small top-N set of promising frontier candidates using a lightweight utility function and then applies time-bounded RRT* planning to estimate their feasible path costs for re-ranking. The path generated for the selected frontier is further reused for navigation to reduce redundant global planning. Experiments in three warehouse-like environments show that the proposed method consistently produces shorter exploration trajectories than conventional frontier baselines, with traveled-distance reductions of up to 14.1%, while reducing exploration time by up to 9.5% in two environments and remaining competitive in the third. The method maintains map detail comparable to the conventional OctoMap-based baseline, demonstrating an effective trade-off between exploration efficiency and mapping quality.
comment: Accepted for presentation at RIVF 2026 (20th International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies)

title: Performance Bottlenecks in Computing ZK Proofs on a GPU
authors: Victor Carolino, Caleb Geren, Michael Kaufman, Maximilian Nussbaum, William Scott, Henry F. Korth
abstract:
Zero-knowledge proofs allow one party to prove the correctness of a statement or execution of a computation while revealing no more than the statement of correctness itself. Recent use cases, such as AI datasets, suggest the need for faster proof generation over increasingly large constraint sets. This paper explores efforts in optimizing zero-knowledge proof generation, specifically PlonK, using GPUs, for applications that are not amenable to solution via incrementally verifiable computing (IVC).
  Our intention with this work is to improve ZK performance by introducing fundamental changes in the low-level architectural structure of proof generation. These changes affect performance curves for most current proof
  generation algorithms. In particular, this paper explores the trade-offs between increased parallelization on GPUs and the resultant memory management problems that occur due to this parallelization. We implement a parallelized PlonK in order to analyze these trade-offs and make arguments concerning the nature of data flows within the proving protocol. Our results lead us to consider multi-GPU environments to maximize performance for large circuit sizes. Such environments introduce issues of communication, efficient hardware management, data partition, and data
  transfers. This paper further discusses the use cases that motivate multi-GPU implementations, their cost models, and the use of remote direct memory access (RDMA) for data transfer among GPUs.

title: Alignment by Confident Debate: Preference Learning from Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Nikhil Verma, Dingxian Wang, Mohammad Reza Rezaei, Andrew Rabinovich, Zhao Chen
abstract: Post-training language models for reasoning typically rely on gold answers, task-specific verifiers, or learned reward models, limiting scalability when such signals are scarce. Multi-agent debate offers a self-supervised alternative, but converting debate into reliable training supervision remains challenging: majority voting weights agreeing responses equally, lacks a principled tie-breaking rule, and is ill-defined for open-ended tasks without a canonical answer; likelihood-based scoring can conflate fluency with correctness; and homogeneous committees may reinforce correlated errors. We introduce Alignment by Confident Debate (AbCD), which converts debate traces into preference data without gold answer labels. A sampling-diverse committee debates each problem, after which final answers are clustered by task-level semantic equivalence. We use verifiable tasks (mathematical reasoning, multiple-choice quantitative QA, and executable code-generation) as a controlled test bed: their answer keys or executable checkers let us evaluate the quality of debate-derived supervision against ground truth, even though the oracle itself never uses gold labels. Post-training on the resulting preferences outperforms inference-only ensembling and debate, as well as SFT on the same traces, across five model families spanning 1B to 8B parameters and four datasets, improving consensus accuracy, with a maximum gain of $21.5_{pp}$. Ablations show that the approach transfers to a larger model and to code generation, while also revealing limitations of heterogeneous committees and agreement-based weighting. Overall, the results suggest that debate traces can yield useful preference supervision when answer equivalence is combined with confidence-weighted disagreement.

title: Symmetric Zassenhaus splittings for bounded and unbounded operators
authors: Paul Bergold, Arieh Iserles, Karolina Kropielnicka
abstract: We establish rigorous local-error bounds for the entire family of symmetric Zassenhaus splittings for possibly unbounded operators, under explicit assumptions on commutator bounds, regularity-preserving flows, and conjugation identities. Truncated symmetric Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansions yield an explicit coefficient formula for the Zassenhaus exponents and identify vanishing commutator expressions. In order to extend these cancellations to the realm of unbounded operators, we prove a general theorem on finite expansions of multiple operator conjugations with controlled integral remainders. For splittings of order 2n, our argument gives the sufficient commutator-length bound 4n-1, revealing regularity requirements that are not apparent from the formal order calculation. Using the Schrödinger equation with a quadratic potential as an example, we show that the order-dependent regularity requirements can reduce to one fixed weighted Sobolev space for all splitting orders.

title: Video Stitching from Multiple Moving Cameras
authors: Shira Ifergane, Roy Amoyal, Shahar Benishay, Oren Freifeld
abstract: We address geometric video alignment for the same scene captured by multiple freely moving cameras. Existing methods, which are based on image stitching or video stabilization, are typically limited to two cameras or must assume the restrictive setting of a fixed linear ordering of the cameras. We propose MViS, a lightweight test-time optimization framework for joint multi-view alignment with temporal consistency. MViS uses a spatial-transformer-inspired net to jointly process frames from all views within a short temporal window and predict per-view, per-time homographies. Optimization proceeds in two stages: geometry-guided alignment followed by appearance-based refinement, with both stages enforcing multi-view and temporal consistency across the sequence. The method requires no scene-specific hyperparameter tuning, handles arbitrary and time-varying view-intersection graphs, and remains robust under rapid camera motion. On a standard two-view video benchmark, MViS matches or surpasses the state of the art. To facilitate evaluation in more complex scenarios, we introduce an annotated dataset with more than two freely moving cameras and establish the first benchmark for this setting. Project page: https://bgu-cs-vil.github.io/MViS-project/ .

title: An Empirical Evaluation of a Weighted PALU Model for Internet Traffic Networks
authors: Wood Moore, Hayden Jananthan, Jeremy Kepner
abstract: The PALU model is a hybrid power law generative framework that decomposes Internet traffic graphs into three structural components: a preferential attachment core, degree one leaf nodes, and disconnected satellite clusters. Although the original PALU formulation provided a theoretical basis for this decomposition, it was never validated against real traffic data and was restricted to unweighted networks. This work presents the first empirical evaluation of PALU against real Internet traffic, using packet traces from the MAWI WIDE samplepoint F dataset. We introduce a weighted extension of the model incorporating strength degree scaling, and develop a packet-to-graph pipeline for parameter estimation across multiple observation window sizes. Results show that the power law degree exponent $α\approx 2.0$ remains stable across observation scales from $10^5$ to $3 \times 10^6$ packets, consistent with the PALU structural prediction. However, the satellite cluster parameter $λ$ and the weighted scaling parameter $θ$ exhibit systematic dependence on observation scale, and the Poisson star assumption for unattached components is formally rejected at all tested window sizes. These results indicate that PALU captures important aspects of Internet traffic structure but requires an explicit observation model to fully account for finite sampling effects.

title: Bayesian Inverse Problems for EUV reflectometry with regularized JKO scheme
authors: Vitalii Aksenov, Oliver Henze
abstract: We study a Bayesian inverse problem in EUV reflectometry, where optical constants and layer thicknesses are inferred from angle- and wavelength-resolved reflection measurements. The physical process is modeled and evaluated using an efficient forward model based on the transfer matrix method. As an alternative to computationally expensive sampling-based inference, we employ an Eulerian, entropically regularized Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme that minimizes the Kullback--Leibler divergence via proximal steps in the Wasserstein space. Using the Benamou--Brenier dynamic formulation and a Hopf-Cole transform, each JKO step is reformulated as a pair of heat equations coupled only through their initial and terminal conditions, enabling an efficient fixed-point solver. The resulting high-dimensional densities are discretized on tensor-product grids and represented in tensor-train format, exploiting Kronecker structure for scalable computation. Preconditioning based on estimated posterior moments further improves tractability. We test the method with numerical experiments on EUV reflectometry data for a ruthenium--silicon ($\ce{Ru}$ on $\ce{Si}$) specimen and compare the learned tensor-train posterior to ensemble Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) reference samples. We demonstrate a use case in which we are able to reuse the tensor-train posterior to obtain samples for shifted target distributions with less computational effort than a comparable MCMC method.

title: MSR-ABC: Complementary Feature Fusion for Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification
authors: Yuan Liang, Sourav Bhattacharjee, Abraham Campbell
abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) classification from computed tomography (CT) may benefit from representations that capture different aspects of tumour phenotype. However, simply concatenating reconstruction-derived features, image--text embeddings, and radiomic descriptors may not fully exploit their complementary information. We propose MSR-ABC, a global--local framework integrating MedVAE, MedSigLIP, and radiomics. Spatially matched local image descriptors interact through cross-representation attention, while radiomic auxiliary supervision encourages the pooled local representation to retain quantitative tumour attributes. A gated residual mechanism integrates local information with global summaries. Area-aware pooling and visual and soft-text prompting complete the framework. We evaluate discrimination using a patient-level split of 396 KiTS23 cases and an external cohort of 111 TCGA/TCIA cases, reporting mean AUROC over three training seeds with 95% patient-bootstrap confidence intervals. MSR-ABC achieves mean AUROCs of 0.806 internally and 0.879 externally. Internally, it exceeds global MedVAE--radiomics and three-source concatenation by 3.35 and 3.61 AUROC percentage points, respectively. Removing any source lowers mean AUROC in both cohorts, with the largest decreases following radiomics removal. Individual removal of cross-representation attention, auxiliary supervision, or gated fusion also lowers internal mean AUROC. These findings are consistent with complementary contributions within the integrated architecture and support further investigation of structured representation fusion for non-invasive renal tumour characterisation.

title: Extended Model-Based Learned Inertial Odometry
authors: Sasanka Kuruppu Arachchige, Joni-Kristian Kämäräinen
abstract: Inertial odometry is a compelling approach to state estimation for agile quadrotor flight due to its affordability, low weight, and robustness to perceptual degradation. However, relying only on integrated inertial measurements is impractical, as sensor errors and time-varying biases lead to significant pose drift. Although recent advances have enabled inertial odometry for drone racing, existing approaches show limited generalization to trajectories not seen during training. This work improves generalization by adopting a body-frame representation and incorporating body-frame torque dynamics into the learning pipeline. The learned model predicts short-horizon relative displacements, which are fused with IMU measurements in an Extended Kalman Filter. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the previous state-of-the-art learned inertial odometry approach for quadrotor pose estimation on unseen trajectories. An additional evaluation on four public quadrotor datasets, with whole trajectory shapes held out of training, confirms a lower velocity error on every held-out set and shows that the torque input is most informative when it is derived from the rotor signals. Code, data pipeline and trained models are publicly available.

title: Dual-Number Associative Arrays for One-Pass Provenance and Sensitivity
authors: Timothy Habashy, Hayden Jananthan, Jeremy Kepner
abstract: Associative arrays and GraphBLAS express sparse computations as matrix operations over a chosen semiring, but the result normally contains only the ordinary value. We define a dual-number extension $D_k(S)=S\ltimes S^k$ that carries this value together with $k$ independent auxiliary channels in the same computation. We prove that the construction is a split square-zero extension of any commutative semiring. Over min-plus, the auxiliary value is the weight of the shortest walk constrained to use the corresponding edge, excluding the weight of that edge. This gives an exact shortest-path membership test for that edge, although ties return the union of the edges on all optimal paths. We implement the min-plus construction using sparse \texttt{python-graphblas} operations, with a fixpoint test that checks the value and auxiliary components together. We validate the implementation across 18,692 checks, including 2,825 tied target pairs. On random graphs with 100,000 vertices and 32 seed edges, the dual method is $3.39\times$ faster than the sequential algorithm but $1.50\times$ slower than a min-plus-specific batched method. This difference is largely explained by the dual method requiring $1.55\times$ as many sweeps. Thus, the main contribution is a general algebraic approach with competitive sparse performance, rather than information that specialized min-plus algorithms cannot already compute.

title: Scalable Full-Horizon SFC Deployment over Predictable SAGIN Topologies via Configurable Column Generation Framework
authors: Hang Li, Hao Huang, Yihu Xu, Zixuan Kong, Yanling Jin
abstract: Space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs) integrate heterogeneous communication and computing resources to support ubiquitous services. Service function chains (SFCs) enable complex services to be composed of ordered functions and executed collaboratively across these resources. Mobility continuously reshapes connectivity throughout service execution, yet much of the resulting topology evolution is predictable. Decisions based only on isolated topology snapshots may therefore overlook valuable future connectivity. We formulate an admission-first, cost-aware model on a time-expanded graph for SFC deployment. Our key observation is that temporal feasibility is request-specific, whereas global coupling arises mainly from shared-resource competition. We therefore develop a configurable column-generation framework in which complete request deployments form columns and a restricted master problem coordinates admission and resources. SAGINFE, a fast constructive heuristic built on per-flow embedding (PFE), supplies a standalone feasible solution and initial columns. Configurable pricing schedules combine early-terminated and stricter searches, supplemented by selective PFE candidates. Candidates undergo feasibility and exact reduced-cost checks. Request-wise pricing can run in parallel, followed by finite-pool integer selection. The default configuration improves the admission-first objective over initialization on all 120 main instances. Four pricing workers achieve up to a 2.69-fold median pricing-stage speedup while preserving admitted request counts in the tested cases.

title: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Coarse-to-Fine Finite Element Solver for Heterogeneous Darcy Flow
authors: Kapil Chawla, Sanghyun Lee, Jonathan Valyou
abstract:
Quantum linear system algorithms offer theoretical potential for solving large sparse systems from PDE discretizations. However, applying them directly to fine-scale problems remains impractical on near-term hardware because of limited qubits, restricted circuit depth, and noise. They also prepare a quantum state rather than solution coefficients, whose recovery requires measurement and reconstruction.
  In this work, we develop a hybrid quantum-classical coarse-to-fine finite element framework for heterogeneous Darcy flow. We investigate whether a measured quantum coarse solution improves fine-grid initialization and reduces subsequent classical solver work. Rather than solve the full fine-scale system on a quantum device, we apply a method inspired by the Variational Quantum Linear Solver (VQLS) to the Galerkin coarse system. We reconstruct the approximate coarse solution from measurements, prolongate it to the fine grid, and use it to initialize a classical preconditioned iterative solve.} Numerical experiments on steady heterogeneous Darcy flow and a time-dependent SPE10-based problem show that measured quantum coarse solutions can improve fine-grid initialization, while classical correction recovers accurate pressure fields. The effect on classical solver iterations depends on the problem. All quantum computations were simulated using Qiskit Aer.

title: RuACT: Recovering Inactive Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers
authors: Yijun Li, Zhengxi Lu, Zhipiao Liu, Jinzheng Yu, Xutao Weng, Jian Shao, Yongliang Shen
abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) extends RL with verifiable rewards to open-ended tasks by scoring each response against query-specific rubrics. Under group-relative optimization, however, a rubric that every sampled response fails (unreachable) or passes (saturated) gives all responses the same outcome and no learning signal; in Qwen3-4B medical training, 60.88% of query-rubric observations are inactive. We find that the two states lack different supervision: stating an unreachable rubric in the prompt raises its satisfaction from 1.13% to 91.25%, whereas responses that all pass a saturated rubric still differ in quality. We therefore propose RuACT (Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers), which assigns each inactive rubric the role that supplies what it lacks. Rubric as Teacher uses unreachable rubrics as privileged information for reward-gated on-policy self-distillation, and Rubric as Critic decomposes saturated rubrics into child rubrics that separate current responses while sharing the parent's weight. RuACT outperforms GRPO, rubric reweighting, and rubric-guided exploration on all four medical and scientific benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and achieves the best average with Qwen3-1.7B. On initially unreachable rubrics, unguided recovery rises from 35.02% to 42.86%, while child refinement improves reward-quality alignment on independent rollouts from 57.74% to 60.77%. Code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/RuACT.

title: Coordinatewise Epsilon for Adam under Heavy-Tailed Noise
authors: Jeonseong Kim, Chenglin Fan
abstract: Adam estimates second moments coordinatewise, but typically adds the same scalar $\varepsilon$ to every denominator. We study how this shared $\varepsilon$ affects convergence when noise and curvature vary across coordinates. Under coordinatewise finite-$p$ noise moments, $p\in(1,2]$, choosing $\varepsilon_i$ from the noise and curvature bounds for each coordinate attains the heavy-tailed $\ell_1$-stationarity benchmark $O(T^{-\frac{p-1}{3p-2}})$, matching the known optimal time exponent for smooth nonconvex stochastic optimization. For $1<p<2$, Adam with a shared $\varepsilon_t$ admits a lower bound of order $Ω(T^{-\frac{p-1}{2p}})$. This lower bound holds for every predictable scalar choice of $η_t$, $β_{1,t}$, $β_{2,t}$, and $\varepsilon_t$, precluding a dimension-uniform benchmark rate for this class.

title: Dual-Region Slice Aggregation for CT-Based Renal Tumor Classification
authors: Yuan Liang, Sourav Bhattacharjee, Abraham Campbell
abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most common kidney cancer in adults. We present a region-aware architecture for CT-based ccRCC classification. Tumor and 0--10 mm peritumoral context are pooled separately from shared frozen DINOv3 feature maps. A shared position-aware slice aggregator precedes fixed training-only principal component analysis (PCA). The resulting representations are fused with radiomics using two scalar feature gates. Evaluation on KiTS23 and 111 external cases yields internal test and external AUCs of 0.8078\pm0.0154 and 0.9094\pm0.0015. Compared with matched single-tumor readout, mean AUC increases by 1.50 and 2.34 percentage points, respectively. Early-PCA and reconstruction controls yield lower internal mean AUCs, while external AUC is similar for early and late PCA. These findings highlight the joint role of regional readout and slice aggregation in adapting frozen visual features to renal CT.

title: Transformer-FSQ: Discrete Latents for Extreme KV-Cache Compression
authors: Andras Szecsenyi, Thomas L. Lee, Vaisakh Shaj, Elliot J. Crowley, Amos Storkey
abstract: Private, personalised language models must run on local consumer devices, where large, frontier models cannot fit, and retaining long contexts is non-trivial. Sequential memory---the key-value (KV) cache---grows linearly with context length, quickly dwarfing the model itself: for Qwen3-1.7B-Base, 200,000 retained entries require 21 GiB, 6.6 times more than the model weights. Yet the KV-cache compression methods we measured fail beyond moderate compression ratios. We introduce Transformer-FSQ, addressing extreme KV-cache compression by replacing standard key and value projections with a finite scalar quantisation bottleneck. Our cache stores a packed vector of discrete integer codes per token, with no per-token quantisation metadata. Converting a pretrained transformer trains only these projections on 0.25 tokens per original parameter. We evaluate Transformer-FSQ against five baseline families on models from 0.6B to 8B parameters. On long-context retrieval (RULER), from 12$\times$ to 97.5$\times$ Transformer-FSQ is the most accurate method we evaluate, across scales. A fused Triton kernel decodes directly from the integer codes; with baselines given their authors' kernels where available, it decodes at $1.01\times$ (95% interval $0.98$--$1.05$) the throughput of native SDPA attention on the uncompressed Qwen3-8B-Base at $32\times$ and $1.54\times$ at $97.5\times$. Extreme KV-cache compression is therefore a practical way to extend how much context a fixed device can hold.

title: Coresets for Capacitated Clustering via Dual Concentration
authors: Milind Prabhu, Chris Schwiegelshohn, Sudarshan Shyam, Erik Waingarten
abstract:
We study coresets for clustering problems, focusing on the classical $k$-median and $k$-means objectives. A coreset is a small weighted summary of the input data that approximately preserves the clustering cost for every choice of centers. Such summaries are a central tool for scaling clustering algorithms to large datasets.
  In this work, we consider the capacitated setting, where the clustering is subject not only to choosing centers but also to respecting prescribed cluster-size constraints. This model is a natural generalization of standard clustering and has been widely studied, but its coreset complexity is less well understood. For finite metric spaces, we obtain optimal-size coresets; surprisingly, these match the best-known bounds for unconstrained clustering. We also give improved coreset bounds in Euclidean space, notably the first coresets with near-linear dependence in $k$ while being independent of the dimension and input size.
  The main new technical ingredients are concentration bounds for the dual solutions of min-cost flow problems, which allow for both significantly simpler and tighter analyses of the underlying sampling distribution used in the coreset construction.

title: A Fast and Accurate Algorithm for the $p \to q$ Norm of Sparse Non-Negative Matrices
authors: Marco Pirazzini, Daniel A. Spielman
abstract:
We present an algorithm that computes the $p \to q$ norm of a non-negative matrix with $s$ nonzero entries to accuracy $\varepsilon$ in time $\widetilde{O}(s^{3/2} \log (1/\varepsilon))$, for any $p \ge q \ge 1$. The fastest algorithm previously designed for this problem has running time $\widetilde{O}(s / \varepsilon)$ (Objois and Vladu, 2026), which is slower when high accuracy solutions are desired.
  Our algorithm employs a surprising application of Laplacian solvers inside an Interior Point Method (IPM). We formulate the problem as a linear optimization problem over a product of power cones, and show that the Newton updates of the IPM can be computed by solving a Laplacian system in a Schur complement after subtracting a rank-2 matrix.
  We also discuss an implementation of our algorithm, showing that it is practical and it outperforms optimized solvers such as MOSEK by factors of up to $20\times$ on a variety of tasks.

title: ReplayAudit: Auditing Outsourced LLM Fine-Tuning via Sealed Records and Selective Replay
authors: Yihan Xia, Wenxin Xu, Taotao Wang
abstract: Auditing outsourced LLM fine-tuning requires checking an untrusted provider's training while controlling verification cost. Uniform sampling ignores training-time signals, while checking a suspicious record can require replaying several preceding steps. We present ReplayAudit, a telemetry-guided auditing system that seals training records before challenges and independently replays sampled intervals from sealed checkpoints. Loss changes and parameter-update norms guide stratified random sampling; replay determines whether the selected computation agrees with its records. We relate sampling probabilities to replay work and evaluate the system on real LoRA training. A 7B BF16 prototype rejects a false update-norm report during a random audit; targeted checks also reject false loss reports and skipped updates. We calibrate sampling budgets offline to at least a 90% probability of directly selecting an injected step. For two learning-rate deviation settings, executing these budgets on the same honest 1.5B trajectory reduces median complete-audit wall time by 49% and 67% relative to uniform sampling. When skipped updates evade the high-anomaly stratum, the corresponding audit instead costs 38% more. These results show how deviation capture and actual replay work jointly determine the cost of telemetry-guided auditing.

title: DKWBC: Decoupling Motion Tracking and Balancing for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
authors: Dingkun Wei, Zehong Shen, Huaijin Pi, Xueyang Wang, Xing Zhu, Hujun Bao, Yujun Shen, Xiaowei Zhou
abstract: Humanoid whole-body control requires a robot to track diverse reference motions while maintaining balance under gravity, torque limits, contact switching, and external disturbances. Existing reinforcement-learning-based trackers typically learn control outputs that jointly address motion tracking and balance. However, similar reference poses can correspond to substantially different dynamic demands, requiring a unified policy to learn motion-dependent control requirements alongside balance corrections. This can complicate learning and lead to high-frequency fluctuations in control outputs. We propose DKWBC, a dynamics-informed whole-body control framework that combines explicit model-based tracking with a learned balancing residual. Inspired by the model-based and environmental-wrench contributions to joint torques in floating-base dynamics, DKWBC uses inverse-dynamics feedforward and joint PD feedback to supply tracking torques, while a residual policy learns additional joint-torque corrections for balanced execution. By explicitly accounting for motion-dependent torque demands, this structure simplifies the policy's learning task. Experiments in simulation and on real hardware demonstrate that a single learned balancing policy generalizes across motion datasets while maintaining accurate motion tracking and balance across ground support, attached payloads, and physical interaction. Project page: https://robbyant-research.github.io/DKWBC/.

title: Not Your Diary, Just Your Topic: Grading the Wrong-User Control
authors: Karina Romanova, Igor Kiselev, Vladimir Platonov, Viliana Devbunova, Gregory Leleytner, Adeliya Leleytner, Lina Veltman, Aleksandr Nikolich
abstract: A common test of personalization replaces a user's history with someone else's and measures the drop in accuracy. But this swap also changes the topics in the history, so the drop may reflect topic mismatch. We examine this problem with a frozen language model on LaMP-2 news categorization, using histories from similar users and synthetic histories assembled from other users' articles. The user's own history improves accuracy by 2.3 percentage points over a model trained without history. Removing history only at evaluation makes this gain appear larger, at 4.8 points. Category labels alone reproduce 86% of the accuracy gap between the user's own history and a random user's history. With synthetic histories matched on labels and text similarity, the gap falls to 0.9 points. Across two user splits and three training seeds, the advantage over a similar user's history is 3.2 points for users seen during training and 0.65 points for unseen users, where the evidence for an advantage remains inconclusive. A small movie-tagging experiment with one training seed also finds no advantage over other users' histories. These findings show why personalization should be evaluated on unseen users, with histories of similar content and a model trained without history as comparisons. We also find that adding gated cross-attention improves on a prefix-only model under our training setup; whether this holds more broadly remains open.
comment: 21 pages. NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Personalized, Aligned, Long-Term Memory for AI Systems (PALM)

title: Know What You Need: Efficient Activation Checkpointing
authors: Danyal Ahmed, Edouard Oyallon
abstract: Large Language Model training is increasingly constrained by memory capacity. Activation Checkpointing reduces activation memory by avoiding storing selected activations during the forward pass and rematerializing them during backpropagation, thereby trading memory savings for additional computation. Although this technique is essential for scaling model training, rematerialization can be prohibitively expensive, particularly for Transformer linear layers. Approximate computation could reduce this overhead, but conventional approaches either introduce errors that accumulate over the backward pass or fail to exploit information available from the initial forward pass. We introduce a novel approximate rematerialization method that can yield unbiased gradient estimates: using information collected during the initial forward pass, the method selectively recomputes only the most important layer components, either through greedy selection or randomized sketching. Ablation studies show that the resulting gradients closely match the exact gradients. When applied to feed-forward layers, attention layers, or both, our method can recompute only two-thirds of the layer components in a Llama-488M model, while increasing perplexity by just 1.7%, 1.2%, and 2.5%, respectively.

title: Contextual Search and Bilateral Trade with a Trace-Square-Root Potential
authors: Romain Cosson, Federico Fusco, Anupam Gupta, Stefano Leonardi, Renato Paes Leme, Matteo Russo
abstract:
We present a unified potential method for contextual search and bilateral trade with one-bit feedback and obtain order-tight algorithms for both problems. Our framework starts from a Bayesian perspective in which the unknown target (for contextual search) and the unknown pair of valuations (for bilateral trade) are sampled from a known prior distribution. In that model, the decision maker bases its prediction on the posterior distribution, obtained by conditioning on feedback received in previous rounds.
  For Bayesian contextual search, we present an algorithm with a total loss bounded by $O(\mathrm{Tr} \sqrt Σ)$, where $Σ$ is the covariance matrix of the target's prior; and for contextual bilateral trade, our algorithm's regret is bounded by $O(\mathrm{Tr} \sqrt{Σ_S}+\mathrm{Tr} \sqrt{Σ_B})$, where $Σ_S$ and $Σ_B$ are the covariance matrices of the seller's and buyer's valuations.
  We then use ideas from this Bayesian setting and adapt a ``dual'' of this trace-square-root potential to the classical worst-case setting, where the target and valuations are chosen adversarially from the unit Euclidean ball. For both contextual search and bilateral trade, we obtain tight $O(\sqrt d)$-regret algorithms. These results match the existing lower bounds up to a constant factor and improve on the previous guarantees of $O(d\log d)$ for contextual search and of $O(d6^d)$ for bilateral trade.

title: Online Timely Bin Packing Revisited: A Simpler Algorithm with Optimality in Special Cases
authors: Pei-Lin Chiang, Wing-Kai Hon, Ying-Chia Huang, Li-Tzu Yang
abstract:
Online Timely Bin Packing is a variant of classical online bin packing in which items arrive over time with sizes and deadlines. Packing an item may be deferred until its deadline, but once a collection of items is packed into a bin, the bin is closed and cannot be used again. The objective is to minimize the total number of bins used. The problem was introduced by Khattar in 2023. In 2025, Aminian proposed Discrete-Greedy, a deterministic online algorithm with a competitive ratio of exactly $2$, which remains the best-known upper bound. Its analysis is particularly simple; however, the algorithm requires maintaining a fractional simulation internally and may leave usable space in some bins unfilled.
  We propose Thrifty-Greedy, a simple deterministic online algorithm that does not require a fractional simulation. We prove that its competitive ratio is exactly $2$, matching the best-known upper bound. At the same time, the algorithm automatically achieves the optimal competitive ratio on two natural classes of inputs: it is $1$-competitive when all items have the same size, and $1.5$-competitive when every item has size in $\{1/3,2/3\}$. In contrast, Discrete-Greedy has a competitive ratio of at least $2$ on both classes.

title: On Positive Computation
authors: Eduardo Skapinakis
abstract: We introduce new notions of reducibility for monotone classes and show that a monotone version of Circuit Satisfiability and the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem are complete for $mNP$, even under positive reductions (which are not the same as monotone reductions). If this holds for all (monotone) $mNP$-complete problems - that they are also so complete for $mNP$ -, then $P\neq NP$. We introduce positive models of relativized computation and show that the separation $posP\subsetneq mNP$ does not relativize, even when oracles are restricted to monotone sets. Yet, there is a (weak) diagonalization proof that $posP\subsetneq mNP$.

title: CRTrack-Cap: A New Benchmark for Cross-View Dense Video Object Captioning
authors: Xiangqun Zhang, Likai Wang, Zekun Qian, Rui Zhou, Ruize Han, Wei Feng
abstract: Dense video object captioning (DVOC) localizes, tracks, and describes object trajectories within a video. Existing methods process each camera view independently, producing separate camera-local tracklets and captions for the same person across cameras. These outputs lack a unified description and leave complementary appearance evidence across views unused. We therefore formulate cross-view DVOC (CVDVOC), which associates these tracklets into scene-level global trajectories and generates one caption for each trajectory from synchronized views. To support this task, we construct CRTrack-Cap from CRTrack by auditing text-identity links and converting usable referring expressions into canonical captions. It retains 425 global trajectories and 838 local tracklets across 13 scenes, with canonical captions for 335 identities. We adapt CHOTA to the cross-view setting as CV-CHOTA to jointly evaluate tracking and caption quality. Our reference framework combines View-Exclusive Cross-Camera Association (VECA) for grouping tracklets with Conflict-Evidence Gating (CEG) for integrating caption evidence using its reliability and disagreement across views. Against three single-view methods adapted with MvMHAT for cross-view association, our framework achieves CV-CHOTA scores of 83.43 and 33.48 on the scene-disjoint in-domain and cross-domain tests, respectively. Together, CRTrack-Cap and our framework provide a benchmark and a strong baseline for describing the same person consistently across camera views.

title: SparseModesNet for coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical system in heterogeneous porous media
authors: Kapil Chawla, Tomoki Koike, Sanghyun Lee, Julie Bessac
abstract: Coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) models describe interactions among displacement, fluid pressure, and temperature in geothermal systems. Fine-mesh simulations over many time steps are costly, particularly with heterogeneous permeability and thermal conductivity or fracture networks that alter fluid and heat transport. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) reduces the number of unknowns but can require many modes because its reconstruction is linear. We apply SparseModesNet to reconstruct coupled THM solutions using a small set of selected modes and a neural-network nonlinear decoder. Starting from a larger collection of candidate modes, SparseModesNet selects modes to reduce reconstruction error rather than simply retaining those with the highest energy. We compare SparseModesNet with POD on three problems: a two-dimensional heterogeneous medium, a two-dimensional connected fracture network, and a three-dimensional geometry based on Utah FORGE fractures. We evaluate reconstructed displacement, pressure, and temperature fields, as well as pressure- and temperature-based quantities of interest. We also test temporal interpolation by training on a subset of snapshots and reconstructing omitted snapshots within the same time interval. For the same reduced dimension, SparseModesNet achieves smaller reconstruction errors than POD and accurately recovers the solution fields and selected geothermal quantities of interest.

title: Entering a New Domain in the Era of Generative AI: An Autoethnography of Solo Game Development as a Bioinformatics Educator
authors: Hannah Kim
abstract: The rapid improvement of generative AI (GenAI) not only increased the efficiency of practice but also empowered individuals with capabilities to explore new domains. However, identity formation in the wake of such empowerment remains understudied. We use an autoethnography to understand identity formation in the context of solo game development as a bioinformatics educator. With the goal of developing a create-your-own-adventure (CYOA) game, we collected data for 73 days through journal entries, interacting with communities of practices. The autoethnographer had continuously reassessed the situation, and closely interacted with communities of practice. Their prior knowledge was used to provide in-game context and to uniquely interpret game development processes. These findings suggest that the autoethnographer made efforts to belong to communities of practice and engaged extensively in sensemaking through the lens of a bioinformatics educator. Although GenAI puts power at hand, attaining a new identity took place at a human pace.

title: TPIC: Energy-Conserving Space Plasma Simulations on GPU Supercomputers
authors: Luca Pennati, Ivy Peng, Stefano Markidis
abstract: Artificial heating and numerical damping affect particle energization in kinetic space plasma simulations, even when the numerical scheme remains stable. Implicit and semi implicit energy conserving Particle-in-Cell (PIC) methods eliminate these errors in the discrete energy balance while relaxing explicit stability constraints. We present TPIC, a massively parallel implementation of the Energy Conserving Semi-Implicit Method (ECSIM) for GPU supercomputers. We extend the exact energy conservation in the ECSIM formulation to closed domains with conducting boundaries by deriving and canceling a spurious term in the discrete Poynting flux theorem. TPIC executes the complete particle and field cycle on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, combining matrix-engine acceleration with asynchronous communication and computation. We validate TPIC in a variety of electrostatic and electrodynamic test cases relevant for space plasma physics applications, including quasineutral plasma expansion, two-stream instability, Whistler waves, Weibel instability, Whistler turbulence, and three-dimensional magnetic reconnection with conducting walls and 12.3 billion particles. We show that in all scenarios, TPIC agrees with the corresponding analytical theory or reference numerical results, and preserves the total system energy to machine precision. On 4,096 AMD GPUs, TPIC advances 1.9 trillion particles with 96.8\% weak scaling efficiency.

title: BiLoGo: Reducing the smoothing of localised responses in Transformer-based neural operators for sheet forming
authors: Yingxue Zhao, Haoran Li, Haosu Zhou, Tobias Pfaff, Nan Li
abstract: Trial-and-error FE simulation of sheet forming could be computationally expensive, neural-network-based learned simulators are used to accelerate design. These simulators should accurately capture localised responses, such as thinning around sharp radii or near ribs, which determine formability. Transformer-based neural operators propagate information efficiently across the mesh but tend to smooth such localised responses. This study develops BiLoGo, a Bipartite Local-Global learned simulator with an FE-guided design that connects local node-element message passing with a Transformer-based neural operator for long-range information exchange. BiLoGo has three modules: a bidirectional node-element GraphSAGE model that learns nodal-elemental coupling on a bipartite graph and predicts each quantity on its native FE entity without interpolation; a dual-stream Transformer-based neural operator that processes blank deformation and tool contact with separate token sets, preventing localised contact information from being averaged with the whole-blank state; and a fusion and element update module that combines global and local features via gated residual fusion and updates element features conditioned on element-node kinematics. Evaluated on a dome-shaped cold forming case and two corner-shaped hot stamping cases (one with ribs), BiLoGo achieves the lowest positional and threshold-based thinning errors on all three cases compared with single-level and hierarchical graph-based models and Transformer-based neural operators. Near the ribs, the smoothing index of predicted thinning increases from 0.41-0.56 for Transformer-based neural operators to 0.94 for BiLoGo-U. Compared with the hierarchical graph network CAtt-BiUGNN, BiLoGo-T reduces mean positional error by 15.5% on the Corner case and BiLoGo-U by 8.3% on the Corner+Rib case, with 66-69% less training memory.
zh_title: BiLoGo：减少基于Transformer的板料成形神经算子中局部响应的平滑现象
translation: 板料成形的试错有限元模拟计算成本高昂，因此常使用基于神经网络的学习模拟器来加速设计。这些模拟器应准确捕捉局部响应，如尖锐半径或筋条周围的变薄，这决定了成形性。基于Transformer的神经算子能够在网格间高效传播信息，但往往会平滑此类局部响应。本研究开发了BiLoGo，这是一种具有有限元引导设计的二分局域-全局学习模拟器，它将局部的节点-元素消息传递与用于长距离信息交换的基于Transformer的神经算子连接起来。BiLoGo包含三个模块：一个双向节点-元素GraphSAGE模型，它在二分图上学习节点-元素耦合，并在其原生的有限元实体上预测每个量而无需插值；一个双流基于Transformer的神经算子，用单独的token集处理毛坯变形和工具接触，防止局部接触信息与整个毛坯状态被平均化；以及一个融合与元素更新模块，通过门控残差融合结合全局和局部特征，并以元素-节点运动学为条件更新元素特征。在穹顶形冷成形案例和两个角形热冲压案例（其中一个带筋）上的评估表明，与单层和分层基于图的模型以及基于Transformer的神经算子相比，BiLoGo在所有三个案例中都实现了最低的位置和基于阈值的变薄误差。在筋条附近，预测变薄的平滑指数从基于Transformer的神经算子的0.41-0.56增加到BiLoGo-U的0.94。与分层图网络CAtt-BiUGNN相比，BiLoGo-T在Corner案例上的平均位置误差降低了15.5%，BiLoGo-U在Corner+Rib案例上的平均位置误差降低了8.3%，同时训练内存减少了66-69%。
tldr: 提出了一种名为BiLoGo的局域-全局学习模拟器，通过结合二分图消息传递与双流Transformer，有效克服了Transformer在板料成形模拟中平滑局部变薄响应的缺点。
ai_comments: 该论文针对基于Transformer的神经算子在模拟板料成形时容易平滑局部响应（如变薄）的痛点，提出了BiLoGo模型。创新性地结合了双向二分图SAGE模型、双流Transformer和门控残差融合模块，既能保持长程信息交换，又能精确捕捉局部特征，具有很高的实用价值。
motivation: 传统的有限元模拟板料成形计算代价高昂，而基于Transformer的神经算子虽然能传播全局信息，但倾向于平滑诸如尖角或筋条周围变薄等局部响应，从而影响成形性评估。本研究旨在减少这种局部响应的平滑现象。
method: 开发了BiLoGo模型，包含三个模块：双向节点-元素GraphSAGE模型、双流Transformer神经算子、融合与元素更新模块（采用门控残差融合）。

title: A Novel Algorithm to Simulate Conductance-based Neuronal Networks
authors: Amir Shahhosseini, Rodolphe Sepulchre
abstract: Conductance-based models are central to neurophysiology and neuromorphic engineering, yet their simulation scales poorly to large networks. We study and analyze an iterative solver that operates in signal space. Each iteration reduces to $N$ decoupled scalar linear time-varying differential equations, one per neuron, which are solved in parallel and in closed form. The solver admits two complementary interpretations: a variable metric forward-backward splitting method, rooted in operator theory, and a waveform relaxation quasi-Newton method, rooted in circuit simulation. We prove uniform and superlinear convergence, with a bound that reflects the conductance structure of the dynamics. The algorithm is illustrated on the classical Hodgkin--Huxley neuron and on networks of up to 5000 neurons.

title: What remains of the planar induced minor conjectures?
authors: Jadwiga Czyżewska, Tomáš Masařík, Marcin Pilipczuk, Paweł Rzążewski
abstract:
Dallard, Milanič, and Štorgel, and independently Gartland and Lokshtanov, conjectured that for every planar graph $H$, Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring are polynomial-time solvable in $H$-induced-minor-free graphs. As a structural explanation, Gartland and Lokshtanov further conjectured that such graphs admit balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices. Bonnet and Chang recently refuted the independent-set part of the algorithmic conjecture, by showing that Maximum Independent Set is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in graphs excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor.
  We revisit both conjectures. We show that the graphs used by Bonnet and Chang exclude much simpler planar graphs, including several $16$-vertex trees, and we introduce a second, independent family of hard instances. We also prove that $3$-Coloring is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in both settings, thus refuting the algorithmic conjecture in full, even in its quasipolynomial version, unless $\mathsf{NP}\subseteq\mathsf{QP}$. On the structural side, we identify planar graphs $H$ for which the structural conjecture holds, while the algorithmic one fails. Thus, constantly dominated balanced separators cannot by themselves explain the tractability of Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring.

title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
authors: Maxime Burchi, Fayaz Ali Dharejo, Radu Timofte
abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) approaches have demonstrated strong performance across diverse domains in recent years, learning accurate world models from agent trajectories. However, despite this progress, current approaches still struggle to surpass human performance on tasks that require long-term memory and planning. In this work, we address the problem of long-term memory in MBRL by moving beyond the commonly studied paradigm of architecture design. We introduce Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL), using gradient descent at test time to encode the memory of episode observations into world model parameters. This enables the agent to learn a distinct world model for each episode, improving memory capabilities compared to traditional approaches that solely rely on contextual memory. We first establish a proof of concept on a simplified two-dimensional variant of the Memory Maze environment, which we refer to as Memory Maze 2D, showing consistent improvements across different world model architectures. We then demonstrate the effectiveness of TT-MBRL in the 3D domain, achieving new state-of-the-art results on the Memory Maze benchmark. Finally, we show that TT-MBRL maintains strong performance on non-memory benchmarks such as DeepMind Control and Atari 100k.

title: Capacity of Generic Symmetric Distributed Linear Computation: The Geometry of Relations
authors: Hua Sun
abstract: In distributed linear computation, $K$ users observe linear functions of common finite-field data and send separate messages to a server that wants another linear function. We characterize the generic capacity $C$, the minimum total number of field symbols sent per computed instance, when all observations and the demand have dimension $ν$, the data have dimension $μ$, and the coefficients of these linear functions are drawn independently and uniformly from the field and stay fixed during coding, with the field size growing through arbitrary prime powers. For fixed $K$, $C/ν$ depends only on $τ=μ/ν$: the curve has finitely many linear pieces for at most three users, infinitely many pieces approaching one value of $τ$ for four users, and a rational part between two sequences of linear pieces for five or more users. The geometry of the relation space, formed by the linear relations among the observations and the demand, determines three things: the shape of the curve, which relations the coding scheme aligns, and the entropy inequalities used in the converse. Generically, the user subspaces of this space are either balanced, where the capacity lies on a single rational curve, or split into two balanced components, a sparse and a dense one, which produces the linear pieces. Achievability uses asymptotic set alignment, in which monomial precoders confine the combined observation differences to a small set. The converse uses the same geometry to lower-bound the sum of the users' remaining observation entropies in terms of the remaining data entropy.

title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
authors: Constantinos Karouzos, Nikolaos Aletras
abstract: Language model deployment often requires different trade-offs between competing objectives as user preferences change, yet standard post-training methods typically produce a single policy for a fixed objective weighting. We introduce LambdaMix, a new parameter efficient method for learning a preference conditioned family of policies with group-relative online reinforcement learning. LambdaMix jointly trains one low-rank adapter per objective over a frozen base model. One preference vector selects the adapter mixture that generates responses and weights the separately normalized rewards used to update the adapters. A single training run supports changing preferences at inference without further optimization. We experiment with four models on helpfulness and harmlessness and on solving math problems while following instructions. We also evaluate the two largest models on rewriting comments to preserve wording while reducing clues about personal attributes. On the first two tasks, LambdaMix achieves higher hypervolume than all evaluated conditioned and policy merging baselines across all four models. LambdaMix uses fewer training completions and stores fewer adapter parameters than a set of GRPO specialist policies. With architecture and initialization fixed, varying adapter mixtures and objective weights together gives wider score ranges and higher coverage than varying either alone.

title: LACART: Lookahead-Augmented Collision Avoidance and Reference Tracking Strategies for Safety-Critical Robots
authors: Pedro Lopes, Amit Shivam, Luis Tiago Paiva
abstract: Autonomous racing provides a demanding testbed for collision avoidance under tight geometric and computational constraints. Building on a recent conference contribution and a master's dissertation, LACART combines lookahead-based control barrier functions (CBFs), a relaxed control Lyapunov function (CLF), and quadratic programming (QP) to modify nominal vehicle commands for obstacle avoidance and reference tracking. The method handles circular obstacles and track boundaries in a common optimisation layer. Comparative simulation results against Huang \emph{et al.} \cite{r9} show similar full-track paths and lower median computation times: 0.31 versus 0.33 ms per step and 0.023 versus 0.025 ms per QP solve. The dissertation further demonstrates a 1:43-scale vehicle with camera-based estimation and wireless actuation at a reported 25 Hz control rate. We identify the conditions linking lookahead-point clearance to body clearance, illustrate hardware limitations, and propose a recorded demonstration of safety intervention and recovery. The contribution targets ground-robot collision avoidance and real-time safety monitoring.

title: Fast and Actionable Classification of HPC I/O Time Series
authors: Maxime Gonthier, Luan Teylo, Francesco Antici, Mihail Popov, Francieli Boito
abstract: Input/output (I/O) is a major bottleneck for highperformance computing (HPC) performance. One of the challenges is the contention between jobs when sharing the parallel file system. However, tackling this issue depends on knowing the temporal behavior of jobs. In this paper, we propose a clusteringbased approach to characterize jobs' temporal I/O behavior. We propose SAGE, a lightweight method that cuts I/O traces into short windows and learns an alphabet from them. The trace then becomes a sequence of symbols, which we call ''genome'', and we use clustering to separate them into classes. We evaluate SAGE and its two-stage variant SAGE-2 on 819,771 real traces from 2 HPC systems. We compare them against other techniques from the state of the art on three metrics, including one we propose. Compared to K-shape, the best baseline available, SAGE-2 lowers the median intra-cluster metrics by 9.1% on average, and achieves this in 2 minutes of clustering time versus 3.8 hours, a 109x speedup. More importantly, clusters created by SAGE and SAGE-2 carry enough information to act on: we evaluate the use of the cluster centroids for I/O scheduling, and show that our approach can decrease I/O stretch by up to 24% compared to the state of the art (round-robin placement).

title: A Separation Principle for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: Lucia Pezzetti, Nicolas Lanzetti, Antonio Terpin, Florian Dörfler, Giorgia Ramponi
abstract: We study cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) problems in which agents evolve under decoupled noisy dynamics but share a population objective. A canonical example is a mobility operator that orchestrates a fleet of vehicles to meet customer demand. The stochastic and time-varying nature of these problems calls for learning approaches, yet existing MARL algorithms do not scale: learning assignment and routing jointly over the full state-action space becomes prohibitive as the number of agents grows. Formulating the problem over the space of probability measures, we prove a separation principle: the population cost-to-go function is upper bounded by an optimal transport problem whose transportation cost is the target-conditioned single-agent cost-to-go function.
