abstract: Concurrent transmissions (CTX) enable an ultra-wideband (UWB) tag to range to, or self-localize from, multiple nodes with a single frame reception, significantly improving update rate and energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches. Prior work demonstrated the concept feasibility via prototypes whose real-world applicability is however hindered by many limitations, notably including their inability to directly execute on UWB tags and to cope with interfering UWB signals. We address these limitations in two ways. First, we redesign the core CTX techniques to enable a fast and efficient execution on resource-constrained MCUs without sacrificing accuracy. Second, we leverage the new features in the IEEE 802.15.4z standard to achieve robustness to interference from other UWB devices and enable tags to dynamically select which anchors to use, two crucial and unexplored capabilities in CTX-based systems. We quantitatively evaluate our approach experimentally in two real-world testbeds with different characteristics. We first analyze our new techniques individually, offering an in-depth discussion of design choices and performance trade-offs. Then, we embed all our techniques into a CTX-based system enabling a tag to self-localize entirely on-device, unlocking gains up to 44% in runtime and 85% in energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches.
comment: Submitted to the IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

title: Where Should Learning Live? Regret Analysis for Text, Parameter, and Joint Adaptation
authors: Jungtaek Kim, Jaden Park, Jongwon Jeong, Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Kangwook Lee
abstract: Language-model systems can select prompts and parameter adapters repeatedly during deployment, using feedback to guide later choices. Earlier choices may change the context or environment inherited by later configurations. We study selection among preconstructed candidates and compare cumulative loss with the best fixed prompt--parameter pair used from the beginning. This excess loss separates into three terms: selection regret within the available family, the gap from restricting that family, and the benefit or harm of the actual deployment history. Selection is evaluated using the history each candidate would have produced if used throughout, which separates candidate quality from the effects of switching. When loss functions are fixed independently of selector randomness, past choices affect loss for only a bounded number of rounds, and every candidate's own-history loss is revealed, limiting switches yields sublinear expected regret within the selected family. We also quantify the costs and additional assumptions of independent probing and deployment-only feedback. Controlled experiments show that fewer switches can either lower or raise deployed loss, depending on whether inherited histories are harmful or helpful. With Qwen3.5-9B on Spider, text-only selection has lower within-family regret than joint selection, yet produces more failures because its candidate family excludes stronger configurations.

title: NAVE: A Normalized, Adaptive Conformer for Antarctic Whale Vocalization Detection
authors: Matthias Nagl, Paul Primus, Gerhard Widmer
abstract: Antarctic whale vocalization detection requires temporally localizing call boundaries in long underwater recordings and classifying them into predefined call types. Training reliable machine learning models for this task is difficult due to the variability and sparsity of whale calls in passive acoustic monitoring datasets. These difficulties are further amplified by time-varying noise that can mask whale calls and by site-specific ambient sound characteristics to which a trained model may not generalize. In this work, we present NAVE, a Conformer-based detector that improves whale-call detection via three components. First, its input representation combines per-bin complex mean subtraction, which suppresses constant site-specific ambient sound characteristics, with an additional per-channel energy normalization (PCEN) channel that adapts to temporal variations in the noise floor. Second, a frequency-dynamic stem processes these noise-aware representations with convolutions that adapt across the characteristic frequency bands of the target call types. Third, we use a Conformer backbone with a convolution kernel matched to the duration of the target calls that adds an inductive bias and improves temporal localization. We evaluate NAVE on BioDCASE 2026 Task 2 using leave-one-site-out cross-validation across the validation sites, which approximates deployment on unseen recording sites. A single NAVE model with a tuned per-class threshold exceeds the stronger WhaleVAD-BPN baseline, using no boundary-proposal network and no search over post-processing parameters. A controlled ablation study shows that the normalized front-end and a duration-matched convolutional kernel each contribute substantially to recovering the D downsweep, the hardest class for previous detectors, with the wide kernel giving the largest aggregate gain.
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Accepted at the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2026 Workshop. Code: https://github.com/TheFruitGuy/NAVE-SED

title: Beyond Segmentation: Enriching ImageCAS with Coronary Ostia Landmarks, Rooted Centerline Graphs, and Open-Weight Localization Models
authors: Matteo Leccardi, Andrea Moglia, Marco Morandini, Michele Brembilla, Alessandro Nicosia, Andrea Penserini, Christian Brandini, Ender Konukoglu, Marco Marcon, Luca Mainardi, Pietro Cerveri
abstract: Coronary ostia and centerlines are key reference points for automated analysis of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), from surgical planning to intraoperative vessel tracking. However, the only public ostium annotations cover 77 non-gated aortic scans, not CCTA, while CAT08 and ASOCA (32 and 40 CCTA scans) mark the ostia only implicitly, as centerline start points. This work enriches ImageCAS, the largest public dataset for coronary artery segmentation, with ostium annotations for its 1000 patients and centerline graphs rooted at these new ostia, making it, to the authors' knowledge, the largest public dataset for ostium localization and the only one with centerlines following the official ImageCAS masks and starting at annotated ostia. Three annotators marked each ostium in the first 500 volumes; in the next 500, the candidates of a model trained on the first batch were corrected (human-in-the-loop). Six 3D localization models, trained on ImageCAS, CAT08 and ASOCA, were benchmarked on 58 held-out volumes (50 ImageCAS, 4 CAT08, 4 ASOCA). SwinUNETR-V2 and nnResUNet localized all ostia without failure (>5 mm error), with median errors of 0.70-0.87 mm. Trained on CAT08 and ASOCA alone, SwinUNETR-V2 fails on 34% of right and 53% of left ostia, whereas adding 250 ImageCAS volumes removes all failures. The centerlines were extracted by a deterministic, quality-controlled minimal-path procedure; on ASOCA, they cover a median of 99.5% of the reference length, with a median per-patient mean distance of 0.22 mm between matched reference points and centerlines. Annotations, centerlines, code, and weights are available at https://hal9000-lab.github.io/.
comment: 52 pages including the appendices. Dataset, centerlines, code and model weights: https://hal9000-lab.github.io/

title: Multiscale Closing Index (MCI) for measuring structural similarity between 2D point sets
authors: Nicolò Zava, Angel Franco-Alvarez, Samy Blusseau, Santiago Velasco-Forero, Maria-Jose Jimenez
abstract: We introduce Multi-scale Closing Index (MCI), a new dissimilarity measure for evaluating the alignment of two 2D point sets. MCI is bounded between 0 and 1 and is based on multiscale mathematical morphology operations, with smaller values indicating greater structural agreement. The measure was motivated by the need to assess the quality of registration between point sets representing cell populations in biological images. To evaluate its behaviour under controlled conditions, we generated synthetic point clouds from Perlin-noise-based spatial structures, following established approaches for simulating biologically plausible spatial organization. We assessed MCI between those point clouds and different transformed versions, obtained by local perturbation, point removal, translation, rotation and addition of impulsive noise. Across these experiments, the dissimilarity MCI increased gradually and consistently with perturbation severity, while showing a clear discontinuity between clouds originating from the same underlying spatial structure and point clouds generated from different structures. We further compared MCI with commonly used point-set distances, including Hausdorff-based measures and Sliced Wasserstein distance. These experiments show the ability of MCI to capture structural agreement and quantify deviations between point sets, highlighting its potential as a complementary metric for evaluating two-dimensional point-set registration.

title: Machine learning for lattice QCD
authors: Gurtej Kanwar, Scott Lawrence, Alessandro Nada, Phiala Shanahan
abstract: Machine learning (ML) methods have been explored as a means of optimizing lattice field theory calculations, with increasing interest in recent years. This chapter gives an introduction and summary to the use of ML methods to optimize lattice field theory without introducing any uncontrolled approximations. We focus on those directions which are clearly established as of late 2025, marking the 50th anniversary of the beginning of the study of lattice gauge theory. This chapter is a contribution to the online book ``Lattice QCD at 50 years,'' (LQCD@50), edited by Tanmoy Bhattacharya, Maarten Golterman, Rajan Gupta, Laurent Lellouch, and Steve Sharpe.

title: On the Order of Privacy and Smoothing in Functional Mean Estimation
authors: Haotian Chen, Yu-Wei Chen, Qifan Song, Jordan Awan
abstract: Differential privacy (DP) is a leading framework for privacy protection, yet privacy mechanisms tailored to functional data analysis (FDA) remain relatively underexplored. For functional mean estimation, we investigate a fundamental question regarding the ordering of privatization and estimation by comparing two canonical pipelines: Fit-Then-Protect (FTP), which smooths trajectories before privatization, and Protect-Then-Fit (PTF), which privatizes observations at discrete time points before smoothing. When data are observed without error, we prove that FTP achieves strictly smaller mean squared error than PTF asymptotically (as the sample size increases) under the same $μ$-Gaussian differential privacy ($μ$-GDP) budget in both finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and infinite-dimensional reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS). Simulation studies support our theory and explore settings with observation error and fitting constraints, demonstrating that FTP outperforms PTF under small observation noise, whereas PTF can become preferable in high-noise settings. In addition to this comparison, we establish a novel GDP guarantee for Gaussian perturbations taking values in a Banach space, extending existing results beyond the RKHS setting.

title: Beyond the $n/2$ Threshold: Quantum Query Complexity for Computing Hamming Weight and Symmetric Functions
authors: Yuan Deng, Zihan Hao, Honghao Lin, Qipeng Liu, Vahab Mirrokni, Jianan Shao, David P. Woodruff
abstract: The oracle-interrogation algorithm [van Dam, FOCS '98] computes every $n$-bit Boolean function with bounded error using $n/2+O(\sqrt n)$ quantum queries. In contrast, parity can be computed exactly using $\lceil n/2\rceil$ queries, but whether an additive overhead beyond $n/2$ is necessary for a single Boolean output has remained open. In this work, we construct an explicit family of symmetric Boolean functions requiring $n/2+Ω(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries at a fixed positive constant error. We also give an algorithm that recovers the exact Hamming weight using $n/2+O(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries with bounded error, and therefore computes every symmetric Boolean function within the same query bound. Together, these results determine the optimal additive order for Hamming weight recovery and for the worst case over symmetric Boolean functions at sufficiently small constant error.

title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
authors: Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Katerina Hristova, George Tsoukalas, Johannes Bausch, Eric Wieser, Francisco J. H. Heras, Nicholas C. Rubin, Guang Hao Low, Sébastien Racanière, Nenad Tomašev, Lei M. Zhang, James Watson, Tanuj Khattar, Aws Albarghouthi, Stavan Jain, Harun Khan, Leopoldo Sarra, Andrew W. Senior, Michael Broughton, Hussain Masoom, Sergio Boixo, Ryan Babbush, Swarat Chaudhuri, Pushmeet Kohli
abstract: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which large language model agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 1.4x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 11x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.

title: Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions
authors: Igor M. L. Pataro, Martina Mammarella, Fabrizio Dabbene, Teodoro Alamo
abstract: This paper presents a deterministic geometric procedure for analysing affine constraints over fixed ellipsoidal regions, motivated by chance-constrained set approximation. Analytical tests classify inequalities as always violated, never violated, or cutting. Pairwise tests determine whether two inequalities can be strictly violated at a common point, yielding a compatibility matrix. The tests follow from quadratic optimisation and the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions, with explicit treatment of tangencies, parallel normals, and degenerate inequalities. The formulation applies in arbitrary finite dimensions and provides geometric information for subsequent bounds on simultaneous sampled violations and safe-region approximation.

title: Super-resolved digital terrain models for GEDI geolocation correction: agreement with airborne LiDAR DTM-based corrections at the beam level, not the footprint level
authors: Natsuki Yuda, Shinichiro Shirota
abstract: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) mission measures three-dimensional forest structure with a LiDAR aboard the International Space Station. GEDI observations have geolocation errors of about 10 m, which cause misalignment with other remote sensing data and reduce the accuracy of downstream tasks. Matching GEDI ground elevations against high-resolution digital terrain models (DTMs) from airborne LiDAR is one way to correct these errors, but such DTMs exist in few regions. To widen this method's applicability, we super-resolved a more widely available low-resolution DTM and used it for the matching. Our question is whether a super-resolved DTM yields the same correction as a 1 m-resolution airborne LiDAR DTM and, if not, why. In steep forests of western Japan, we super-resolved an existing 10 m-resolution DTM to 1 m. Improving its accuracy required fusion with a global 30 m-resolution DTM from a different source. Using the resulting DTM, we corrected GEDI observation positions first by a single shift per ground track, then per observation. For most tracks, the shifts nearly matched those from the airborne LiDAR DTM, likely because DTM errors canceled out across many observations. Per-observation corrections, however, did not match. At a single observation, the error does not cancel out and is too large for the correction. This error likely originates mainly from the input DTM. Therefore, even without a 1 m-resolution DTM, a roughly 10 m-resolution DTM, fused with a global DTM and super-resolved to 1 m, should yield track-wise corrections nearly matching those from a 1 m-resolution DTM.
comment: Appendices will be added in a future version

title: A note on a problem in communication complexity
authors: Henning Wunderlich
abstract: We study bounded-error randomization and majority operators in structural communication complexity. We give a communication-complexity formulation of Tarui's theorem and identify the bounded-error closure of weakly unbounded-error communication with a distributional perturbation of logarithmic margin complexity. Retaining the Boolean guarantee in Tarui's probabilistic polynomials yields the stronger inclusion $\mathsf{PH}^{\mathrm{cc}} \subseteq \mathsf{ZP}\mathbin{\cdot} \mathsf{PP}^{\mathrm{cc}} \subseteq \mathsf{BP}\mathbin{\cdot} \mathsf{PP}^{\mathrm{cc}}$. We also define a majority operator satisfying $\mathsf{PP}\mathbin{\cdot} \mathsf{P}^{\mathrm{cc}} = \mathsf{PP}^{\mathrm{cc}}$ and use Sasaki's majority formula to prove that $\mathord{\oplus}\mathsf{P}^{\mathrm{cc}} \subseteq \mathsf{PP}\mathbin{\cdot} \mathsf{PP}^{\mathrm{cc}}$. For the inner-product function modulo two, both the outer index and each inner protocol have logarithmic cost. Together with Forster's lower bound, this gives an explicit witness to the non-idempotence of the majority operator and to $\mathsf{PP}\mathbin{\cdot} \mathsf{PP}^{\mathrm{cc}} \not\subseteq \mathsf{UPP}^{\mathrm{cc}}$. Both the bounded-error closure and the two-level majority class are contained in $\mathsf{PSPACE}^{\mathrm{cc}}$.

title: The Finite Difference Method, for the heat equation on Sierpiński simplices
authors: Nizare Riane, Claire David
abstract: In the sequel, we extend our previous work on the Minkowski Curve to Sierpiński simplices (Gasket and Tetrahedron), in the case of the heat equation. First, we build the finite difference scheme. Then, we give a theoretical study of the error, compute the scheme error, give stability conditions, and prove the convergence of the scheme. Contrary to existing work, we do not call for approximations of the eigenvalues.
comment: arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:1710.00358

title: AdaptivePnP: Fast Auto-Tuned Plug-and-Play for Deconvolution
authors: Haley Duba-Sullivan, Emma J. Reid, Charles A. Bouman, Gregery T. Buzzard
abstract: Plug-and-play (PnP) methods reconstruct images by alternating a data-fitting step with an image denoiser. Their performance depends on two parameters: the step size $γ$ and the measurement noise level $σ$. In practice, $γ$ is often tuned by grid search over validation images and must be retuned whenever the problem setting changes, and $σ$ is assumed known or estimated separately. We propose AdaptivePnP, a PnP framework that jointly estimates $σ$ and $γ$ at every iteration from the data-fitting residual. To do so, we apply the PnP virtual model to the data-fitting proximal map and show that the residual is zero-mean Gaussian with covariance parameterized by $γ$ and $σ$. However, when one parameter is much larger than the other, the residual carries little information about the smaller one and using the maximum likelihood (ML) estimator can degrade the PnP iterations. We therefore introduce the identifiable maximum likelihood (IML) estimator, which restricts the ML estimator to an identifiable window in which the normalized Cramér--Rao bound of every parameter is bounded by a user-specified tolerance. For the virtual model, this window is an interval of ratios $ρ= γ/σ$, so computing the IML estimate reduces to a one-dimensional search over $ρ$. We apply AdaptivePnP to two standard PnP methods, yielding algorithms that require neither a tuned $γ$ nor a known $σ$. On image deblurring and super-resolution, AdaptivePnP matches or outperforms PnP baselines tuned with the true $σ$. Code is available at https://github.com/hdubasullivan/AdaptivePnP.
comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Computational Imaging

title: Orders between channels and implications for partial information decomposition
authors: André F. C. Gomes, Mário A. T. Figueiredo
abstract: The partial information decomposition (PID) framework is concerned with decomposing the information that a set of random variables has with respect to a target variable into three types of components: redundant, synergistic, and unique. Classical information theory alone does not provide a unique way to decompose information in this manner and additional assumptions have to be made. Recently, Kolchinsky proposed a new general axiomatic approach to obtain measures of redundant information, based on choosing a preorder relation between information sources (equivalently, a preorder between communication channels). In this paper, we exploit this approach to introduce three new measures of redundant information (and the resulting decompositions) based on well-known preorders between channels, thus contributing to the enrichment of the PID landscape. We relate the new decompositions to existing ones, study some of their properties, and provide examples illustrating their novelty. As a side result, we prove that any preorder that satisfies Kolchinsky's axioms yields a decomposition that meets the axioms originally introduced by Williams and Beer when they first propose the PID.
comment: Corrected version of the article published in Entropy 2023, 25, 975 (https://doi.org/10.3390/e25070975). The corrections are described in a correction notice in Entropy. 13 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables

title: Automatic Synthesis of Low-Complexity Translation Operators for the Fast Multipole Method
authors: Isuru Fernando, Chaoqi Lin, Andreas Klöckner
abstract:
The FMM is the leading approach for attaining linear complexity in the evaluation of long-range (e.g. Coulomb) many-body interactions. We demonstrate a new, hybrid symbolic-numerical method for the automatic synthesis of all families of translation operators required for the execution of the Fast Multipole Method (FMM). Our method is dimension-independent (demonstrated in 2D and 3D) and applicable to any translation-invariant kernel. Low complexity in translation operators for the FMM is usually achieved by algorithms specialized for a potential obeying a specific partial differential equation (PDE). Absent a PDE or specialized algorithms, Taylor series based FMMs or kernel-independent FMM have been used, at asymptotically higher expense.
  When symbolically provided with a constant-coefficient elliptic PDE obeyed by the potential, our algorithm can automatically synthesize translation operators requiring $\mathrm{O}(p^d)$ operations, where $p$ is the expansion order and $d$ is dimension, compared with $\mathrm{O}(p^{2d})$ operations in a naive approach carried out on (Cartesian) Taylor expansions. This is achieved by using a compression scheme that asymptotically reduces the number of terms in the Taylor expansion and then operating directly on this "compressed" representation. Judicious exploitation of shared subexpressions permits formation, translation, and evaluation of local and multipole expansions to be performed in $\mathrm{O}(p^d)$ operations, while an FFT-based scheme permits multipole-to-local translations in $\mathrm{O}(p^{d-1}\log(p))$ operations. We demonstrate computational scaling of code generation and evaluation as well as numerical accuracy through numerical experiments on a number of potentials from classical physics.

title: A Blockchain-Based Audit Mechanism for Trust and Integrity in IoT-Fog Environments
authors: Ismael Martinez, Abdelhakim Senhaji Hafid, Michel Gendreau
abstract: The full realization of smart city technology is dependent on the secure and honest collaboration between IoT applications and edge-computing. In particular, resource constrained IoT devices may rely on fog-computing to alleviate the computing load of IoT tasks. Mutual authentication is needed between IoT and fog to preserve IoT data security, and monetization of fog services is needed to promote the fog service ecosystem. However, there is no guarantee that fog nodes will always respond to IoT requests correctly, either intentionally or accidentally. In the public decentralized IoT-fog environment, it is crucial to enforce integrity among fog nodes. In this paper, we propose a blockchain-based system that 1) streamlines the mutual authentication service monetization between IoT and fog, 2) verifies the integrity of fog nodes via service audits, and 3) discourages malicious activity and promotes honesty among fog nodes through incentives and penalties.

title: Stay on the Manifold: Hierarchical Bayesian Trajectory-Family Transfer for Sparse-Target Reconstruction and Sampling
authors: Elvis Han Cui, Yuhan Pan, Xin-Ya Zhang, Bingbin Li, Yanan Li, Donghui Wang, Weng Kee Wong
abstract: Where should reconstructions and new samples lie when a few observations reveal only fragments of a trajectory? We propose hierarchical Bayesian trajectory principal-manifold sampling (HB-TPM), which learns a family of smooth curves from ordered source tasks and adapts it to sparse targets. For unordered vectors, alternating progression assignments and coefficient updates estimate trajectory structure between and beyond the observed shots under the learned source family. Observation-aware extensions connect the trajectory prior to photon arrivals and image-encoded cardiac cycles. Our analysis characterizes the coefficient directions supplied by the prior and bounds sampling error conditional on curve recovery. Across 30 held-out vector tasks, HB-TPM reduces mean sliced-Wasserstein distance by 21.0-41.8% relative to a source-adapted VAE. Prior-strength and sampling ablations identify coefficient shrinkage as the main supported mechanism. On 100 simulated photon records, adaptation lowers mean relative trajectory RMSE by 50.2% versus target-only fitting and 23.6% versus source-mean prediction. Across three training seeds and five folds on 98 cardiac sequences, HB-TPM with latent-MSE training achieves the best mean reconstruction among the tested configurations. Together, the results demonstrate trajectory-family transfer for sparse-target reconstruction and trajectory-centered sampling when source and target tasks share comparable progression structure.
comment: 46 pages, 17 figures. Includes appendices with proofs and additional experimental results

title: HexTiles and Semantic Icons for MAUP-Aware Multivariate Geospatial Visualizations
authors: Yuya Kawakami, Sarah Yuniar, Kwan-Liu Ma
abstract: We introduce HexTiles, a hexagonal-tiling based visual encoding design for multivariate geospatial data. Visualizing several geospatial variables at once is difficult because map position is already reserved for geography, and because variables are often reported on different, irregular spatial units whose aggregation is subject to the Modifiable Areal Unit Problem (MAUP). HexTiles bins data of differing spatial discretizations into hierarchical hexagons and encodes up to three variables per tile in a base color, an inner ring, and semantic icons whose count conveys value, letting the visualization designer guide attention to specific variables and their interactions. To make the effects of MAUP visible, we compute a spatially-weighted variance for each variable within each tile and encode it as a confidence value in every channel, so that the variability hidden by aggregation is not lost. Because interactive maps are increasingly viewed in tilted, 3D perspective, HexTiles encodes quantitative values only in channels that perspective does not distort, namely color and icon count. In a user study comparing HexTiles to Square-glyphs, participants rated HexTiles as significantly less demanding and frustrating, and performed more consistently with it. Domain experts in ecology and hydrology further noted its value for communicating regional patterns, and that the confidence encoding signals where aggregated values should be interpreted with care. Our results suggest that, although 3D is commonly discouraged, it can work for multivariate geospatial visualization when restricted to perspective-robust channels.

title: Domain Adaptive Diabetic Retinopathy Grading with Model Absence and Flowing Data
authors: Wenxin Su, Song Tang, Xiaofeng Liu, Xiaojing Yi, Mao Ye, Chunxiao Zu, Jiahao Li, Xiatian Zhu
abstract: Domain shift (the difference between source and target domains) poses a significant challenge in clinical applications, e.g., Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) grading. Despite considering certain clinical requirements, like source data privacy, conventional transfer methods are predominantly model-centered and often struggle to prevent model-targeted attacks. In this paper, we address a challenging Online Model-aGnostic Domain Adaptation (OMG-DA) setting, driven by the demands of clinical environments. This setting is characterized by the absence of the model and the flow of target data. To tackle the new challenge, we propose a novel approach, Generative Unadversarial ExampleS (GUES), which enables adaptation from a data-centric perspective. Specifically, we first theoretically reformulate conventional perturbation optimization in a generative way--learning a perturbation generation function with a latent input variable. During model instantiation, we leverage a Variational AutoEncoder to express this function. The encoder with the reparameterization trick predicts the latent input, whilst the decoder is responsible for the generation. Furthermore, the saliency map is selected as pseudo-perturbation labels. Because it not only captures potential lesions but also theoretically provides an upper bound on the function input, enabling the identification of the latent variable. Extensive comparative experiments on DR benchmarks with both frozen pre-trained models and trainable models demonstrate the superiority of GUES, showing robustness even with small batch size.
comment: This paper is accepted at CVPR 2025

title: Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching
authors: Chuangtao Ma, Sriom Chakrabarti, Arijit Khan, Bálint Molnár
abstract: Traditional similarity-based schema matching methods fail to resolve semantic ambiguities and conflicts in complex, domain-specific mappings due to a lack of commonsense and domain-specific knowledge. In parallel, large language models (LLMs) without sufficient background knowledge tend to hallucinate, further complicating schema matching. To overcome these limitations, we introduce KG-RAG4SM, a Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching. This method integrates novel retrieval mechanisms, including LLM-based, vector-based, graph traversal-based, and hybrid techniques with advanced reranking schemes to extract the most relevant subgraphs from large external KGs. Our approach achieves superior results without requiring re-training, as evidenced by improvements of 39.79% in precision and 30.56% in F1 score over LLM-based state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods (e.g., Jellyfish-8B) on the MIMIC dataset, and enhancements of 69.20% in precision and 21.99% in F1 score over pre-trained language model (PLM)-based SOTA methods (e.g., SMAT) on the Synthea dataset. Additionally, KG-RAG4SM scales effectively across KGs from commonsense KGs to domain-specific ones, while its instruction-tuning knowledge exclusion component ensures truthful performance in end-to-end schema matching tasks despite the suboptimal relevance of KG context. Our empirical analysis and case studies from real-world scenarios show that the hallucination problem in LLMs for schema matching is well mitigated by our solution.

title: Sketch-MoMa: Teleoperation for Mobile Manipulator via Interpretation of Hand-Drawn Sketches
authors: Kosei Tanada, Yuka Iwanaga, Masayoshi Tsuchinaga, Yuji Nakamura, Takemitsu Mori, Remi Sakai, Takashi Yamamoto
abstract: To use assistive robots in everyday life, a remote control system with common devices, such as 2D devices, is helpful to control the robots anytime and anywhere as intended. Hand-drawn sketches are one of the intuitive ways to control robots with 2D devices. However, since similar sketches have different intentions from scene to scene, existing work needs additional modalities to set the sketches' semantics. This requires complex operations for users and leads to decreasing usability. In this paper, we propose Sketch-MoMa, a teleoperation system using the user-given hand-drawn sketches as instructions to control a robot. We use Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to understand the user-given sketches superimposed on an observation image and infer drawn shapes and low-level tasks of the robot. We utilize the sketches and the generated shapes for recognition and motion planning of the generated low-level tasks for precise and intuitive operations. We validate our approach using state-of-the-art VLMs with 7 tasks and 5 sketch shapes. We also demonstrate that our approach effectively specifies the detailed motions, such as how to grasp and how much to rotate. Moreover, we show the competitive usability of our approach compared with the existing 2D interface through a user experiment with 14 participants.
comment: Accepted to IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2025. Project Page: https://toyotafrc.github.io/SketchMoMa-Proj

title: Evolving Drone Morphologies for Agile Flight
authors: Elijah H. W. Ang, Robin Ferede, Christophe De Wagter, Guido C. H. E. de Croon
abstract: The design of multicopter drones has remained almost the same since their inception. While conventional designs work well in many cases, they may not be optimal in specific tasks. This paper revisits rotary drone design by exploring which body morphologies are best suited for different objectives and constraints. An evolutionary algorithm is used to produce drone morphologies that performs better than standard configurations at thrust-to-weight ratio, maneuverability and size. To generate a range of drones with performance trade-offs between them, the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II is used. The evolved drone bodies outperform a standard multicopters in at least one of the three objectives. The Pareto front extrema show improvement of 489.2%, 23% and 4.8% in maneuverability, thrust-to-weight ratio and size, respectively, when compared to a standard quadcopter. The improvement in maneuverability is attributed to the tilt angles of the motors, while the increase in thrust-to-weight ratio is due to the higher number of propellers. Experiments show that the performance improvement transfers to a real world drone racing task, where the evolved drone outperforms the standard drone in terms of number of gates passed,flight speed and lap times.

title: New Algorithms for Incremental Minimum Spanning Trees and Temporal Graph Applications
authors: Xiangyun Ding, Yan Gu, Yihan Sun
abstract: Processing graphs with temporal information (the temporal graphs) has become increasingly important in the real world. In this paper, we study efficient solutions to temporal graph applications using new algorithms for Incremental Minimum Spanning Trees (MST). The first contribution of this work is to formally discuss how a broad set of setting-problem combinations of temporal graph processing can be solved using incremental MST, along with their theoretical guarantees. Despite the importance of the problem, we observe a gap between theory and practice for efficient incremental MST algorithms. While many classic data structures, such as the link-cut tree, provide strong bounds for incremental MST, their performance is limited in practice. Meanwhile, existing practical solutions used in applications do not have any non-trivial theoretical guarantees. Our second and main contribution includes new algorithms for incremental MST that are efficient both in theory and in practice. Our new data structure, the AM-tree, achieves the same theoretical bound as the link-cut tree for temporal graph processing and shows strong performance in practice. In our experiments, the AM-tree has competitive or better performance than existing practical solutions due to theoretical guarantees, and can be significantly faster than the link-cut tree (7.8-11x in updates and 7.7-13.7x in queries).

title: A structure and asymptotic preserving scheme for the quasineutral limit of the Vlasov-Poisson system
authors: Alain Blaustein, Giacomo Dimarco, Francis Filbet, Marie-Hélène Vignal
abstract: In this work, we propose a new numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system that is both asymptotically consistent and stable in the quasineutral regime, i.e. when the Debye length $λ$ is small compared to the characteristic spatial scale of the physical domain. Our approach consists in reformulating the Vlasov-Poisson system as a hyperbolic problem by applying a spectral expansion in the basis of Hermite functions in the velocity space and in designing a structure-preserving scheme for the time and spatial variables. Through this Hermite formulation, we establish a convergence result for the electric field toward its quasineutral limit together with explicit error estimates in $λ$. Following this path, we then propose a fully discrete numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system, inspired by the approach in arXiv:2306.14605, and rigorously prove that it is uniformly consistent in the quasineutral limit regime. Finally, we present several numerical simulations to illustrate the behavior of the proposed scheme. These results demonstrate the capability of our method to describe quasineutral plasmas, illustrate its stability and confirm its asymptotic preserving property.

title: BNPO: Beta Normalization Policy Optimization
authors: Changyi Xiao, Mengdi Zhang, Yixin Cao
abstract: Reinforcement learning with rule-based, binary-valued reward functions has been shown to significantly enhance the reasoning capabilities of large language models. These models typically rely on REINFORCE-based policy optimization methods, such as REINFORCE with baseline and group relative policy optimization (GRPO). However, a key limitation is that existing methods either ignore reward normalization or use static normalization schemes, which fail to adapt to the evolving policy during training. This mismatch can lead to unstable gradient estimates and hinder training stability. To address this issue, we propose Beta Normalization Policy Optimization (BNPO), a novel method that adaptively normalizes rewards using a Beta distribution with dynamically updated parameters. By aligning normalization with the changing policy distribution, BNPO enables more accurate, lower-variance gradient estimation and promotes stable training dynamics. We provide theoretical analysis showing that BNPO reduces variance and generalizes both REINFORCE and GRPO under binary-valued rewards. In addition, we introduce an advantage decomposition mechanism to extend BNPO to more complex reward settings. Experimental results demonstrate that BNPO achieves state-of-the-art performance among policy optimization methods on reasoning tasks.

title: Inter-Layer Hessian Analysis of Neural Networks with DAG Architectures
authors: Maxim Bolshim, Alexander Kugaevskikh
abstract:
Automatic differentiation computes loss Hessians, while interpreting inter-layer interactions requires an explicit choice of graph-indexed blocks. This paper presents an analytical formalism that decomposes the full Hessian into blocks indexed by the DAG of an architecture. The standard decomposition $H = H^{GN} + H^T$ separates the Gauss-Newton component (positive semidefinite for a convex output loss) from the tensor component (residual curvature). If every node map is locally affine in its parent activations, the tensor component of the input Hessian vanishes on each smooth cell ($H^{T}_{v,w}=0$, $H^f_{v,w}=H^{GN}_{v,w}$); ReLU activations alone do not suffice. The full parametric Hessian contains residual terms that do not reduce to the GGN. Building on this decomposition, we use diagnostic metrics (inter-layer resonance $\mathcal{R}$, geometric coupling $\mathcal{C}$, stable rank $\mathcal{D}$, GN-Gap) with stochastic HVP-based estimates whose cost depends on graph evaluation and the number of probes. The theoretical analysis gives conditional bounds on curvature decay and residual-chain transport; empirical examples span fully connected MLPs (Exp. 1-5) and convolutional architectures (ResNet-18, ${\sim}11$M parameters, Exp. 6). When the architecture reduces to a single node, all definitions collapse to the standard Hessian $\nabla^2_θ\mathcal{L}(θ)\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}$.
  Archival correction. The original general novelty claims are no longer maintained: general DAG-Hessian calculus has prior precedents. This is a corrected archival version.
comment: 45 pages, 9 figures, 17 tables. Submitted to Neural Networks (Elsevier). Code: https://github.com/comiam/dag-hesse

title: Computational Construction and Engineering Evaluation of a Verified Mono-Monostatic Body
authors: Vincent Wesley Couey
abstract: Many engineering failures in orientation-dependent systems are geometric failure modes: changing the material delays the failure; changing the geometry can eliminate it. The mono-monostatic property (exactly one stable equilibrium under gravity) is mathematically proven to exist in convex homogeneous bodies, but, to our knowledge, no verified smooth geometry had been openly published when v1 appeared (April 2026). We introduce an Equilibrium Count Score (ECS) oracle that measures stable equilibria via drainage basin analysis on the center-of-mass height landscape. v2 correction: v1 reported that Sloan's (2023) analytical Gomboc parameterization shows 4-11 local minima "at all published parameter values." That claim is withdrawn. The beta values swept were this work's own grid points, not Sloan's (he states convexity bounds beta <= 0.15 and beta <= 0.17); they lie inside the strictly convex sub-regime beta < ~0.036, where a body at beta = 0.023 was later certified mono-monostatic by interval arithmetic; and the oracle's two stages are biased in opposite directions, so its count can be wrong either way. We construct one strictly convex mono-monostatic body by extending the Sloan phase function with a Fourier term and optimizing via differential evolution, with ECS=1 confirmed across merge thresholds from 0.5% to 10%; two more reach ECS=1 under the oracle but are not strictly convex. Conventional geometries cannot achieve ECS=1 through ballast alone: cylinders and cubes retain multiple stable equilibria even at 30% bottom-weighted mass. Applications: an IMU calibration housing (349x orientation precision improvement), aerial reforestation seed pods (20-67% germination loss from incorrect landing orientation), and marine buoy self-righting. Cross-layer scoring shows the Gomboc is 11.8x worse than the cylinder on contact distribution while optimal on equilibrium stability.
comment: 14 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables. Part III of the Substrate Geometry series. v2 amendment-of-record: withdraws the claim that Sloan's parameterization shows 4-11 local minima at published parameter values; narrows three verified bodies to one strictly convex body (two others are oracle-level only). title: Contrastive Distribution Matching for Amortized Sequential Monte Carlo in Discrete Diffusion
authors: Jaihoon Kim, Taehoon Yoon, Prin Phunyaphibarn, Seungjun Kim, Morteza Mardani, Minhyuk Sung
abstract: Discrete diffusion models have emerged as powerful frameworks for generating structured categorical data. However, efficiently sampling from reward-tilted distributions remains a fundamental challenge. While Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) offers asymptotic exactness for this task, estimating the optimal twist function in discrete state spaces necessitates costly Monte Carlo approximations, resulting a severe computational bottleneck at inference. To overcome this limitation, we introduce Contrastive Distribution Matching (CDM), a novel framework that amortizes the cost of SMC inference by learning a parameterized twist function via positive and negative samples. For efficient training, we reformulate the gradient estimator to leverage the closed-form forward kernels of discrete diffusion models. In practice, evaluating our learned twist function incurs less than 5% additional computational overhead compared to a single forward pass of the base model. Through extensive empirical evaluations, we demonstrate that CDM consistently outperforms existing baselines under matched wall-clock time. We validate the effectiveness and versatility of our approach across a diverse range of applications, including toxic text generation, regulatory DNA sequence design, protein designability, and diffusion large language model alignment.
zh_title: 离散扩散中摊销序列蒙特卡洛的对比分布匹配
translation: 离散扩散模型已成为生成结构化分类数据的强大框架。然而，从奖励倾斜分布中进行高效采样仍然是一个根本性挑战。虽然扭曲序列蒙特卡洛（SMC）为该任务提供了渐近精确性，但在离散状态空间中估计最优扭曲函数需要昂贵的蒙特卡洛近似，导致推理时出现严重的计算瓶颈。为了克服这一限制，我们引入了对比分布匹配（CDM），这是一个新颖的框架，通过使用正负样本学习参数化的扭曲函数来摊销SMC推理的成本。为了实现高效训练，我们重新表述了梯度估计器，以利用离散扩散模型的闭式前向核。在实践中，与基础模型的单次前向传递相比，评估我们学习到的扭曲函数所产生的额外计算开销不到5%。通过广泛的实证评估，我们证明了在匹配的挂钟时间内，CDM始终优于现有的基线。我们在毒性文本生成、调节性DNA序列设计、蛋白质可设计性和扩散大语言模型对齐等广泛的应用中验证了我们方法的有效性和多功能性。
tldr: 提出了一种名为CDM的新框架，通过学习扭曲函数来摊销离散扩散模型中序列蒙特卡洛（SMC）推理的成本，在大幅降低计算开销的同时提升了生成质量。
ai_comments: 该论文针对离散扩散模型中奖励倾斜采样的计算瓶颈，创新性地提出了对比分布匹配（CDM）框架，通过参数化扭曲函数实现了摊销推理，并巧妙利用离散扩散的前向核重构了梯度估计器，具有极高的计算效率和广泛的应用潜力。
motivation: 虽然扭曲序列蒙特卡洛（SMC）能为离散扩散模型中的奖励倾斜分布提供渐近精确的采样，但在离散状态空间中估计最优扭曲函数需要昂贵的蒙特卡洛近似，导致推理时存在严重的计算瓶颈。
method: 引入对比分布匹配（CDM）框架，通过正负样本学习参数化的扭曲函数来摊销SMC推理成本；利用离散扩散模型的闭式前向核重构梯度估计器进行高效训练。

conclusion: 对比分布匹配（CDM）通过学习参数化扭曲函数，有效解决了离散扩散模型中扭曲SMC推理的计算瓶颈，在保证采样质量的同时大幅降低了推理开销，并在多项实际任务中展现出优越性能。

title: Uncertainty-aware neural emulation reveals climate-resilient maize traits at scale
authors: Mojdeh Saadati, Juan Panelo, Gustavo Visentini, Soumik Sarkar, Carlos Messina, Baskar Ganapathysubramanian
abstract: Climate change threatens maize yields worldwide, yet identifying which genetic traits sustain productivity under future conditions requires exploring an enormous space of genotype, soil, and climate combinations that process-based crop models are too costly to simulate at scale. Here we develop an integrated probabilistic emulation framework that transforms a mechanistic crop simulator (APSIM) into a fast, uncertainty-aware discovery engine. Built from two million simulations and coupled to a generative weather model that produces realistic climate sequences, the emulator reproduces thirteen maize growth outputs with high fidelity while returning calibrated confidence for every prediction, at a fraction of the original computational cost. Applying it across 100,000 trait configurations, six locations, and future climate projections extending to the year 2100, we identify 1,114 trait combinations that remain resilient under the 2100 future conditions and a stricter subset of 246 configurations that remain resilient across four future projection periods: 2040, 2060, 2080, and 2100. These resilient configurations occupy a distinct region of trait space, combining high radiation use efficiency with characteristic shifts in developmental and reproductive traits. Trait-importance analysis further identifies radiation use efficiency as the dominant driver of yield under future climate, while projected yields vary widely across locations and climate models, indicating strong spatial heterogeneity in the maize response to climate change.
zh_title: 不确定性感知的神经模拟大规模揭示耐气候玉米性状
translation: 气候变化威胁着全球玉米产量，然而要确定哪些基因特性能够在未来条件下维持生产力，需要探索基因型、土壤和气候组合的巨大空间，而基于过程的作物模型在规模化模拟时成本过高。在这里，我们开发了一个集成的概率模拟框架，将机械作物模拟器（APSIM）转变为一个快速的、具有不确定性感知的发现引擎。该模拟器建立在两百万次模拟的基础上，并与生成现实气候序列的生成天气模型相结合，以极低的计算成本高保真地重现了十三种玉米生长输出，同时为每项预测返回了校准的置信度。将其应用于10万种性状配置、6个地点以及延伸至2100年的未来气候预测中，我们确定了1114种在2100年未来条件下保持弹性的性状组合，以及在四个未来预测时期（2040年、2060年、2080年和2100年）保持弹性的更严格的246种配置。这些具有弹性的配置占据了性状空间的一个独特区域，将高辐射使用效率与发育和生殖性状的特征转变结合起来。性状重要性分析进一步确定辐射使用效率是未来气候下产量的主要驱动力，而预测产量在不同地点和气候模型之间差异很大，表明玉米对气候变化的反应具有强烈的空间异质性。
tldr: 本研究利用不确定感知神经网络模拟器大幅加速作物模型，成功在大规模未来气候情景下筛选出具备高气候韧性的玉米基因型性状组合。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地将概率神经网络模拟与经典的APSIM作物模型相结合，实现了兼顾准确性与不确定性量化的快速作物表型筛选。通过对大规模气候与基因型组合的预测，识别出了未来气候变化下的玉米抗逆性状，对应对全球气候变暖下的粮食安全具有重要意义。
motivation: 气候变化严重威胁全球玉米产量，而通过机理作物模型来大规模探索基因型、土壤和气候组合的巨大空间成本过高，因此需要开发一种快速且能感知不确定性的高效仿真框架来识别耐气候的玉米性状。
method: 开发了一个集成的概率仿真框架，基于200万次模拟数据和一个生成式天气模型，将APSIM机理作物模拟器转化为一个快速的、具不确定性感知能力的发现引擎，并在10万种性状配置、6个地点及未来气候预测中进行应用。
results: 该模拟器能高保真地复现13种玉米生长输出并提供校准后的置信度。研究识别出了在2100年未来条件下保持韧性的1,114种性状组合，以及在2040、2060、2080和2100四个时期均保持韧性的246种更严格的配置；同时发现辐射使用效率是未来气候下产量的决定性驱动因素。
conclusion: 本研究展示了不确定感知神经模拟在高效探索作物基因型-环境相互作用方面的巨大潜力，识别出的耐逆玉米性状和辐射使用效率的关键作用为未来气候适应型作物的育种提供了重要科学依据。

title: Who Speaks Matters: Authority-Aware Multi-View RAG over Italian Parliamentary Proceedings
authors: Mirko Tritella, Riccardo Pozzi, Matteo Palmonari
abstract: Parliamentary proceedings are a primary record of democratic deliberation, yet their volume and fragmentation make multi-perspective access difficult for citizens, journalists, and researchers. Applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to parliamentary transcripts introduces three specific risks: dominance of the most frequent speakers, inability to weight speakers according to topical expertise, and citation misattribution in politically sensitive text. We present ParliamentRAG, a RAG system for the Italian Chamber of Deputies that addresses these risks jointly. Its core contribution is a topic-dependent authority model that estimates each speaker's authority as a function of the current query, combining interpretable components such as profession, education, and previous interventions. Given a user query, the system retrieves relevant speech chunks, identifies topic-relevant experts across parliamentary groups, and generates a summary synthesizing their perspectives, accompanied by supporting quotations. ParliamentRAG is evaluated against Google NotebookLM on 15 policy topics via a two-level protocol combining automated metrics and blind A/B human evaluation by six domain experts. The system achieves higher coverage across political groups (0.97 vs. 0.95), perfect quotation faithfulness (1.00 vs. 0.95), and stronger expert preferences on source-related dimensions, while NotebookLM remains stronger on prose-oriented dimensions.
comment: Accepted at ISWC 2026 In-Use Track. Please cite the ISWC version

title: FlowSim: Rendering-Free Closed-Loop Simulation for Evaluating End-to-End Driving Systems
authors: Hanfeng Wu, Alvaro Marcos-Ramiro, Michael Schmidt, Christoph Stiller
abstract: Closed-loop evaluation of end-to-end (E2E) driving systems typically relies on generating sensor observations and re-processing them through the perception encoder, introducing substantial computational cost and a sim2real gap between simulated and real sensor observations. In this paper, we ask a more fundamental question: is image-space simulation necessary for closed-loop evaluation of E2E driving systems? We propose FlowSim, a rendering-free simulation paradigm that predicts the internal latent representation directly from a previous latent and target-frame symbolic scene conditions. The predicted latent is then processed by the original frozen downstream modules, eliminating image rendering and perception re-encoding. Explicit cross-frame agent association improves latent transition prediction and rollout stability, while variable-horizon simulation enables long-horizon prediction from a common real anchor without accumulating intermediate rollout errors. Experiments on nuScenes and NavSim demonstrate that FlowSim preserves downstream behavior competitively with, and often exceeds image-space simulation in source-to-reference agreement across variable simulation horizons and both dense and sparse latent representations. By predicting the latent directly, both instantiations of FlowSim simulate each step in 0.04--0.06s, substantially faster than the image-space simulation methods they are compared against. These results establish FlowSim as an efficient and practical alternative to conventional image-space simulation methods. Our project page is https://hanfeng-wu.github.io/flowsim_page/.

title: A calculus of types in Isbell nuclei
authors: Juan Luis Gastaldi, Samantha Jarvis, Thomas Seiller, John Terilla
abstract: We identify two constructions from different mathematical traditions. In linear logic and realisability, logical types are generated rather than fixed in advance: one begins with a universe of realisers equipped with execution, uses orthogonality to test their interactions, and takes types to be the biorthogonally closed subsets. In enriched Isbell duality, a quantitative relation induces an adjunction whose fixed points form a category, its nucleus. These constructions proceed by different means; we show that, in the present setting, they produce the same objects. The shared datum is minimal: an associative product, called execution, and a real-valued measurement, with no compatibility assumed between them. The failure of the measurement to be additive is at once the relation defining orthogonality and the quantitative relation whose Isbell nucleus we form, and the types cut out by orthogonality are exactly the fixed points of the associated adjunction. The identification pays off in both directions. The most natural product of types fails to be associative; repairing this failure forces a different notion of type, sensitive to both sides of a composite, on which the induced product is associative and, when execution has units, carries two residuals. What emerges is a noncommutative Lambek calculus, derived directly from execution and orthogonality rather than imposed. In the reverse direction, each such type, read on the categorical side, generates a quantitative relation of its own, and with it a derived adjunction and a further generation of types; these derived types are again types of the original situation, computed by the residuals of the Lambek calculus. We also prove a coherence theorem for the threefold arrangements of this construction and, in the finite-dimensional case, give explicit formulas for the product.

title: Instance-Optimal Estimation with Multiple LLM Judges on a Budget
authors: Junghyun Lee, Sanghwa Kim, Yassir Jedra, Alexandre Proutière, Se-Young Yun
abstract: Evaluating large language models increasingly relies on LLM-as-a-judge protocols, but such evaluations remain costly: different judges have different prices and reliabilities, and the difficulty of each prompt-response pair can vary substantially. This raises a basic allocation question: under a fixed budget, how should one distribute evaluation queries across heterogeneous judges and instances to obtain the most accurate score estimates? We formalize this question as budgeted heteroskedastic multi-judge estimation under independent, unbiased score observations. Given $K$ prompt-response pairs and $J$ judges with known costs but unknown query-judge variances, our goal is to estimate the bounded score vector while minimizing an $\ell_p$-error. Our first contribution is to analyze the inverse-variance weighted estimator (IVWE) and to derive the oracle allocation that minimizes its leading error bound. Since this allocation depends on the unknown variances, we then address the unknown-variance setting by proposing EST-IVWE, an adaptive algorithm that constructs and uses optimistic variance estimates to stabilize the empirical allocation. We prove that EST-IVWE matches the oracle IVWE rate up to lower-order terms in the budget. Our second and central theoretical contribution is a local minimax lower bound matching the leading allocation-dependent rate, establishing asymptotic instance-optimality up to logarithmic factors. An Assouad-type construction based on local, variance-preserving perturbations yields this bound both in expectation and with constant probability. A complementary Fano-type change-of-measure argument captures the logarithmic dependence on the confidence level with a different (suboptimal) allocation geometry. Finally, we numerically validate our approach on synthetic data and resampled HelpSteer2 evaluations, demonstrating improvements over naïve uniform allocation.
comment: 55 pages, 4 figures; the first two authors contributed equally
zh_title: 有预算限制的多LLM评判员实例最优估计
translation: 使用大语言模型作为评判员的协议越来越多地被用于评估大语言模型，但此类评估成本高昂：不同的评判员具有不同的价格和可靠性，并且每个提示词-响应对的难度差异很大。这就引发了一个基本的分配问题：在固定预算下，如何将评估查询分配给异构的评判员和实例，以获得最准确的分数估计？我们将这个问题形式化为在独立、无偏分数观测下的预算异方差多评判员估计。给定 $K$ 个提示词-响应对和 $J$ 个已知成本但查询-评判员方差未知的评判员，我们的目标是估计有界分数向量，同时最小化 $\ell_p$ 误差。我们的第一个贡献是分析了逆方差加权估计量（IVWE），并推导出了最小化其主导误差界的预言机分配（oracle allocation）。由于该分配依赖于未知方差，我们随后通过提出 EST-IVWE 算法来解决未知方差设置，这是一种自适应算法，它构建并使用乐观方差估计来稳定经验分配。我们证明了 EST-IVWE 在预算的低阶项内匹配了预言机 IVWE 的收敛速率。我们的第二个也是核心理论贡献是一个局部极小 minimax 下界，它匹配了主导的分配依赖速率，在对数因子内确立了渐近实例最优性。基于局部方差保持扰动的 Assouad 型构造在期望意义上和以常数概率得到了这个界。互补的 Fano 型测度变换论证用不同的（次优）分配几何捕获了对置信水平的对数依赖。最后，我们在合成数据和重采样的 HelpSteer2 评估上对我们的方法进行了数值验证，证明了其相对于朴素均匀分配的改进。
tldr: 本文研究了如何在固定预算下，通过分配异构的LLM评判员来获得最准确的评估分数，并提出了达到渐近实例最优的自适应算法。
ai_comments: 该论文针对大模型评估中成本高昂的痛点，创新性地提出了多异构LLM评判员在预算限制下的实例最优估计框架，理论与实验结合紧密，具有很高的实用价值和理论深度。
motivation: 现有的LLM作为评判员的评估方法成本高昂，而不同的评判员价格和可靠性各异，提示词对的难度也不同；因此需要在固定预算下，研究如何将评估查询分配给不同的异构评判员和实例，以获得最准确的分数估计。
method: 形式化为预算异方差多评判员估计问题；分析了逆方差加权估计量（IVWE）并推导了理论最优分配；提出自适应算法 EST-IVWE 处理未知方差；通过局部分配下界（Assouad型和Fano型构造）证明了渐近实例最优性。
results: 提出的 EST-IVWE 算法在预算上渐近匹配了最优神谕率（oracle rate）；理论上证明了渐近实例最优性（在对数因子内）；在合成数据和 HelpSteer2 重采样评估上的实验验证了其优于朴素的均匀分配。
conclusion: 论文成功建立了一套多LLM评判员在预算约束下的实例最优估计理论体系，并通过自适应算法和实验验证了其优越性。

title: RoboFQE: Rollout-Free Evaluation of Visual Robot Policies from Offline Trajectories
authors: Yunfu Deng, Sangwoo Shin, Brahma S. Pavse, Josiah P. Hanna
abstract: Evaluating robot policies before deployment typically requires producing new trajectories through real-world execution, simulators, or learned world models. These rollout-based approaches impose infrastructure requirements; simulator and world-model evaluators additionally face prediction errors that can compound over the evaluation horizon. In this paper, we study off-policy evaluation as an alternative to rollout-based robot-policy evaluation methods. Specifically, we introduce RoboFQE, an evaluator that estimates the discounted expected return of a target policy from offline robot trajectories without estimating a behavior-policy density, combining fitted Q-evaluation with a pretrained vision foundation model and learned terminal success annotation to bridge the gap between standard OPE benchmarks and continuous-control visual manipulation. Controlled experiments across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks show that RoboFQE produces accurate discounted-return estimates and preserves policy rankings even on long-horizon manipulation tasks where video world-model evaluators are degraded by autoregressive prediction errors. Ablation experiments show that pretrained vision encoders substantially outperform from-scratch alternatives, particularly on long-horizon tasks, and that learned terminal success annotation enables evaluation without ground-truth reward labels with only slight reduction of accuracy.

title: Dynamic Merging Mutually-Distilled Multi-View Networks for RGB-Event-based Representation Learning
authors: Futian Wang, Fan Zhang, Xiao Wang, Yuhe Ding, Shiao Wang, Jingxi Huang, Jin Tang
abstract: Multi-modal fusion algorithms combining conventional frame-based cameras and event cameras have recently attracted substantial research attention. Typically, existing approaches convert event streams into frames, voxels, or tensors, and then learn the required spatiotemporal information from these transformed event representations for fusion with conventional frame-camera data. Obviously, such paradigms only exploit the limited representational capacity of event data. Moreover, standard training pipelines fail to fully leverage diverse model parameters obtained throughout the learning process. In this paper, we propose a novel mutual distillation method leveraging multi-view teacher network weights to better integrate multiple event representations and achieve model-parameter level fusion. Specifically, we employ multiple encoders to extract different types of event representations and perform mutual knowledge distillation at both the feature-level and logit-level in this process. Afterwards, we perform a dynamic hierarchical model merge strategy on the model parameters from the first stage to yield a unified multi-modal RGB-Event representation model. Experimental results across multiple event-based datasets demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves significant performance improvements.

title: MoRE-GS: Motion-Regime Experts for Future Gaussian Splatting
authors: Shima Salehi, Joshua Peeples
abstract:
Future dynamic novel-view synthesis requires extrapolating multiple motion regimes within the same scene. A single dynamics model may not simultaneously represent stationary regions, coordinated motion, local interactions, and articulated trajectories. We introduce Motion Regime Expert Routing for Gaussian Splatting (MoRE-GS), a causal, render-aware framework for forecasting dynamic 3D Gaussian scenes. MoRE-GS freezes a Gaussian representation reconstructed exclusively from the observed temporal prefix and forecasts its control-keypoint motion using four complementary experts: persistence, a coefficient-space Transformer, a graph convolutional network, and a structured Transformer with rigid and non-rigid motion constraints. A compact routing table assigns expert mixtures across soft motion groups and forecast-horizon bins, while a persistence gate suppresses unreliable extrapolation. Across D-NeRF and HyperNeRF scenes, MoRE-GS achieves improved performance against other methods, and these results demonstrate that renderer-calibrated composition of complementary motion predictors improves causal dynamic Gaussian forecasting across heterogeneous motion regimes.
  Project page: https://advanced-vision-and-learning-lab.github.io/MoRE-GS-website/

title: A Spectral Renormalization-Group View of Learning
authors: Charles H. Martin
abstract: We study how the layers in deep neural networks (NNs) converge, using Wilsonian Renormalization-Group (RG) ideas to organize the spectral picture. During training, these layers often develop heavy-tailed power-law (PL) spectra, and the strongest checkpoints often appear near the PL exponent $α\approx 2$. This pattern raises a simple question: why should this value mark a well-trained layer? The answer is both statistical and physical. Our statistical hypothesis is that $α=2$ marks the boundary between stable if not optimal learning and overfitting via non-self-averaging. The physical answer is that the same value makes the spectral energy gain scale evenly across logarithmic spectral scales, which is the proposed Wilsonian marginal condition. We then apply the ERG trace-log condition, the proposed SETOL theory, which we justify by taking volume-preserving, scale-invariant transformations to remove arbitrary layer scale along the proposed RG flow. The resulting spectral RG flow connects the HTSR and SETOL theories to optimizers such as Muon, and motivates a new optimizer extension, WW-PGD. Together, these results point toward a spectral Renormalization-Group view of learning, in which NNs may approach shared spectral structure in the settings studied here.

title: Behavior Graphs: Unsupervised Graph Structures for Interpreting Robot Deployment Data
authors: Erik Bauer, Jakob Thumm, Christopher Agia, Rohan Sinha, Chen Xu, Haruki Nishimura, Jeannette Bohg, Marco Pavone, Masha Itkina
abstract: Data flywheels promise continuous improvement via insights from deployment data. Understanding how the deployed model succeeds and fails can steer subsequent data collection towards patching failures and reinforcing successes. However, robot deployments create large volumes of high-dimensional rollout data, which is challenging to understand and confidently ground data collection decisions in. To make deployment data easier to analyze and act on, we propose behavior graphs, which compress policy rollouts into a single interpretable, directed graph. We construct the graphs by learning to identify similar behavior modes across rollouts, connecting the behaviors temporally, and finally linking them to outcomes. In a user study on three real-world tasks, where participants analyzed rollouts to choose a data collection strategy, 16 of 18 preferred behavior graphs to rollout videos, reaching comparable conclusions with 40.3% lower perceived temporal demand and 37.6% lower effort. Beyond interpretability for deployment data, behavior graphs are capable progress predictors: across 43 datasets, they improve the rank correlation between predicted progress and true temporal order by 22.9% and reduce mean absolute error by 53.5% relative to the strongest baseline. As the number of deployed robots grows, behavior graphs lend structure to high-dimensional policy rollouts and make deployment data easier to interpret and reason about.
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Project website: https://behavior-graphs.com/

title: A Straight Line Is Not a Camera Pose: Auditing Short-Clip Pose Benchmarks
authors: Xinyi Shi
abstract: The absolute trajectory error (ATE) is the standard measure of camera-motion accuracy, from SLAM to feed-forward 3D reconstruction. On the common Sintel protocol, an image-free constant-velocity line has a lower mean ATE than 10 of 11 recent models re-run with official code and than 85 of 110 published methods. On Lightspeed it beats 5 of 9 models and 10 of 11 published methods, while on TUM, ScanNet, DyCheck and ADT every model beats it. Two properties of ATE's alignment explain this. First, it maps any moving constant-velocity prediction onto the line that best fits the true path, so the line scores the path's regression residual. A residual signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) criterion tells when moving a prediction towards its constant-velocity fit lowers ATE. With the alignment's first-order refit, it accounts for the outcome of all but one of 4010 model-clip evaluations, including all 504 on three benchmarks registered before any model ran. The true path's straightness flags Sintel and Lightspeed. Second, the alignment ignores where cameras look: rotating a trajectory by 30 degrees against its orientations leaves ATE unchanged yet worsens the static-point reprojection of every model on Sintel, TUM and ScanNet, and the line reprojects worst on Sintel by geometric mean. Fitting the alignment's rotation to the predicted orientations gives pose-anchored ATE (PA-ATE), a one-function change at about ATE's cost (37 vs. 34 $μ$s per clip, and 61 vs. 66 $μ$s with the rotation error). It is never below ATE and, as we prove, equals the translational relative pose error over all frame pairs divided by $\sqrt{2}$ when the orientations agree. It ranks every image-free reference below every model on Sintel, follows the reprojection error where ATE does not, and largely preserves the models' order. Its rotation error also exposes Lightspeed ground-truth orientations that the images contradict.

title: CuriousTogether: Implications of Curiosity and Cultural Grounding in Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
authors: Angana Borah, Zoha Hayat Bhatti, Zhijing Jin, Rada Mihalcea
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent settings, exhibiting emergent collective behaviors, yet the role of curiosity as a driver of such dynamics remains understudied. We introduce CuriousTogether, a framework evaluating curiosity-driven multi-agent LLM interactions across three complementary dimensions: novelty-seeking, epistemic and social curiosity. Across eight tasks spanning reasoning, creative generation, and social bias mitigation, curiosity-guided multi-agent settings yield improvements over non-curious ones on seven out of eight tasks, with gains of up to 20.6% in story generation (semantic diversity) and a 14.9 pp reduction in stereotype rates. Furthermore, country-conditioned cultural grounding show benefits for story generation and social tasks, but can hurt precision-oriented reasoning. Finally, we show that inference-time multi-agent curiosity-based approach offers favorable quality-token trade-offs, compared with single-agent baselines. Together, these findings support curiosity-guided interaction as a practical mechanism for improving multi-agent collaboration, with downstream benefits for reasoning, creative, and societal tasks.

title: EPIC: Differentiable Energy-Force Consistent Uncertainty Quantification and Propagation for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
authors: Tianhao Su, Musen Li, Shunbo Hu, Tong-Yi Zhang
abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now rival density functional theory in accuracy and are increasingly used to screen vast crystal databases, yet they can produce unreliable predictions for chemistries outside their training distribution without clear warning. Existing force-level evidential approaches do not inherently define a corresponding uncertainty model over the potential energy surface, limiting the consistent propagation of uncertainty to energy-derived observables. Here we introduce Energy-Propagated Intrinsic Confidence (EPIC), a general energy-centered evidential framework that derives forces as exact gradients of the predicted mean energy, ensuring conservative force fields while providing an analytical estimate of energy uncertainty. Coupled to a MACE backbone trained on the Materials Project trajectory dataset, EPIC propagates uncertainty diagnostics to equations of state, anisotropic structural uncertainty ellipsoids, and phonon dispersions through a Monte Carlo procedure. Applied to 10,966 candidate crystals, the fraction classified as robustly dynamically stable increases from 11\% in the highest-uncertainty quartile to 53\% in the lowest-uncertainty quartile. Furthermore, element-resolved analysis reveals a pronounced chemistry dependence in the relationship between epistemic uncertainty and predicted dynamical stability, highlighting potential limitations in the description of complex bonding environments. EPIC thus provides a physics-aware, chemistry-sensitive uncertainty diagnostic for high-throughput screening and autonomous materials discovery.

title: PROBE: Learned Proxy-Based Execution for Highly Selective Multimodal Semantic Queries
authors: Haikai Zhao, Haisheng Fu, Zhengjie Miao, Zhenman Fang
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) enable semantic queries over unstructured data, but invoking an LLM on every row is prohibitively expensive. Proxy-based execution can reduce this ple with the LLM and training a lightweight proxyto label the remaining rows. Nevertheless, in practical scenarios where semantic queries are highly selective, it remainschallenging to identify representative samples foLM budget and to achieve accurate predictions overthe remaining data using the proxy. We present PROBE, a learned proxy-based execution framework for highly selective multimodal semantic queries. PROBE uses selectivity-adaptive sampling to discover rare polightweight proxy on the acquired labels. It thenrefines proxy predictions through residual correction and homogeneity smoothing over a similarity graph. To address sampling bias, PROBE jointly calibrates refined scores usiarate calibration sample, then selectively routescandidates to the LLM by optimizing the tradeoff between estimated F1 and evaluation cost. On queries from SemBench and LRO-Bench with positive rates as low as 2.17x10^-5 budget yields a geometric-mean F1 of 0.762,compared with 0.797 for exhaustive LLM evaluation, at a geometric-mean speedup of 4.87x and a maximum speedup of 9.3x.

title: Iterative Gumbel Planning for Continuous Control
authors: Shaohuai Liu, Weirui Ye, Yilun Du, Le Xie
abstract: Search-based planning remains a powerful policy improvement paradigm in reinforcement learning, driving milestone successes in discrete domains. However, extending this paradigm to continuous control exposes a structural mismatch: search evaluates a finite set of action candidates, whereas continuous RL typically relies on Gaussian policies. We show that winner-action distillation into a continuous Gaussian induces a \textit{projection error} and a stepwise variance-expanding gradient tendency when the selected action is sufficiently far from the current mean. Empirically, this tendency is associated with elevated terminal variance and a return gap on the evaluated tasks. To address this, we propose \textbf{Iterative Gumbel Planning (IGP)}. By adopting a per-dimension factorized categorical policy, IGP naturally aligns the policy support with the search candidates, eliminating the projection error and reducing the residual approximation to a bounded discretization error. To bypass the combinatorial explosion of high-dimensional discrete action spaces, IGP pairs Gumbel Top-$K$ candidate sampling with an MPPI-style multi-round iterative search to refine the policy at each state. Empirically, IGP achieves state-of-the-art aggregate performance and sample efficiency on DMControl and HumanoidBench. Furthermore, it produces more stable action sequences with lower temporal variance, demonstrating its practical potential for real-world robotic deployment.

title: PixelBench: Can LLMs Understand and Generate Images Pixel by Pixel?
authors: Haoquan Zhang, Feiyang Liu, Juanxi Tian, Wanhua Li, Haodong Duan, Weiyang Liu
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate visual assets through text-based formats such as SVG and CAD, but these symbolic representations describe images using high-level primitives rather than explicit raster values. We ask whether LLMs can instead generate pixel images directly through their existing vocabulary, without a learned image tokenizer or decoder. We introduce PixelBench, a benchmark for text-to-pixel (T2P) and image-to-pixel (I2P) generation across multiple resolutions, together with a complementary pixel-understanding evaluation. Models generate an RGB color palette followed by a grid of indices specifying the palette color of each output pixel. In T2P, the strongest models produce recognizable images directly from text. In I2P, the strongest models outperform palette-matched downsampling and specialized pixelization algorithms at low resolutions. Pixel-understanding performance correlates strongly with generation performance. A resolution-scaling study shows that pixel-generation performance often improves initially before declining at high resolutions. Finally, we introduce Pixel Reconstruction Tuning (PRT), which augments visual instruction tuning with caption-palette-grid trajectories. We post-train Molmo2-4B from its pretraining checkpoint by mixing general instruction data with our curated PRT data, improving performance across 16 visual-centric benchmarks, indicating that explicit pixel reconstruction can provide useful auxiliary supervision.
comment: Technical report, 38 pages, 7 figures. Project page: https://haoquanzhang.github.io/pixelbench

title: Lookahead Prediction-Guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing for Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning
authors: Mengzhao Wang, Yanli Ji, Peng Ye
abstract: Interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning improves the visual reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models by dynamically incorporating visual evidence during reasoning. However, existing methods primarily select evidence from historical context. When the reasoning focus shifts, history-guided evidence may remain focused on prior regions and fail to cover the visual information required by the next step. We refer to this lag between visual evidence and subsequent reasoning demands as Temporal Evidence Myopia. To address this issue, we propose Lookahead Prediction-guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing (LPAVR), a training-free test-time framework. LPAVR transforms Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) from a decoding acceleration mechanism into a lookahead signal for anticipating upcoming reasoning intent. During MTP decoding, the draft head generates multiple future tokens, while the target model verifies them in parallel and retains the longest prefix consistent with its decoding trajectory. This target-verified prefix contains near-future semantics, which LPAVR uses to construct lookahead-guided visual evidence and assess whether history-guided evidence covers the indicated regions. If the coverage is sufficient, the history-guided evidence is retained; otherwise, LPAVR switches to the lookahead-guided evidence. This better aligns the visual context with upcoming reasoning and improves consistency between draft predictions and target-model decoding. Experiments on multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks show that LPAVR improves both reasoning accuracy and the acceptance rates of MTP speculative tokens, jointly enhancing visual reasoning and speculative decoding efficiency.
