The proposed CLIC defines a formal consistency score using a small quantized language model, which is deployed as a Non-RT rApp for model-integrity certification along with a Near-RT xApp for runtime enforcement. We implement CLIC on the OpenAI Cellular (OAIC) platform and evaluate it under domain-adapted JailbreakBench, AdvBench, and VPI workloads. The experimental results show that the proposed CLIC reduces the attack success rate from 0.92 to 0.29 and residual VPI attacks from 0.37 to 0.04, while improving isolation and fairness at slightly higher latency costs, i.e. approximately 27 ms.

title: Safin-1.5: Safety-Native Architecture and Verifiable Reasoning for Recursive Safety Improvement
authors: Jingnan Zheng, Cheng Jin, Ming Zhang, Huan Sun, Zhongtian Ma, Kaisen Yang, Ziyuan Zhou, Tong Wu, Dongcheng Zhang, Yi Zhang, Xiao Wang, Han Qi, Shu Yu, Ermo Hua, Zongji Yu, Chaozhuo Li, Xiaoyu Wen, Zhekai Chen, Jiawei Zhou, Sirui Chen, Ning Ding, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua, Xiangnan He, Xia Hu, Bowen Zhou, Qiaosheng Zhang, Youbang Sun, Xiang Wang, Zhongyu Huang, Chaochao Lu
abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) enables large language models to advance their capabilities through successive updates, but these updates can also introduce new risks and weaken existing safeguards. In line with the AI-45° Law, we pursue Safety RSI, in which safety develops as an intrinsic capability alongside general model capabilities through continual risk discovery and repair, while preserving utility and limiting over-refusal. We introduce Safin-1.5, a model built on a safety architecture and trained through recursive safety improvement, with an inference-time harness that extends its capabilities to formal reasoning. Our approach comprises three components: i) The safety architecture combines persistent safety states with hazardous-knowledge disentanglement. The former retains and selectively invokes safety knowledge, while the latter relocates targeted hazardous knowledge into removable experts, enabling its removal with minimal impact on general capabilities. ii) Recursive safety improvement establishes a discovery-evaluation-repair loop. The loop identifies new vulnerabilities and uses experimental feedback to develop repair strategies. It accepts updates only when they improve safety while preserving general capabilities and limiting over-refusal. iii) The formal reasoning harness combines the model's language understanding with symbolic inference and verification. Proof-obligation-guided semantic bridging recovers missing relations in formal representations, enabling symbolic solvers to construct checkable proofs under formalized premises and accepted semantic bridges. Experimental results demonstrate that Safin-1.5 achieves safety and reasoning performance, outperforming frontier models.

title: PathoJev: Efficient Pathology Decisions from Shared Visual Context
authors: Chengyang Zhang, Wenchuan Zhang, Bo Li, Xinyu Liu, Jiaming Yang, Mengran Li, Jie Chen, Wei Ju, Yuhao Yi, Hong Bu, Jiancheng Lv
abstract: Pathology workflows require multiple visual judgments about the same slide, from identifying tumor type to assessing grade and invasion. Generating and parsing a separate textual response for each structured question adds latency between visual evidence and usable decisions. Building on the System One paradigm, we introduce PathoJev, a pathology model that directly predicts answer probabilities for whole-slide and region-level assessment. PathoJev encodes each slide once and evaluates independent question suffixes in batches over the shared visual context. Reusing the hybrid backbone's recurrent states further limits the computation that grows with slide-context length for each additional question. Across three whole-slide benchmarks, the 9B and 27B models achieve mean accuracies of 77.2% and 78.1%, exceeding SlideChat by 5.4 and 6.3 percentage points. Both scales also maintain competitive accuracy on five ROI benchmarks. On WSI-Bench, the 9B model runs 9.1x faster than SlideChat. Shared context accelerates eight-question workloads by 6.9x and 5.9x over separate prefix encoding, rising to 11.2x and 8.9x for 64 questions. These results provide a reusable probabilistic interface for combining multiple visual judgments in whole-slide and local tissue assessment. Code: https://github.com/ChyaZhang/PathoJev.

title: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval for Autonomous Coding Agents
authors: Weiheng Wu, Junkai Chen, Zhensu Sun, Jieke Shi, Yunbo Lyu, David Lo
abstract: Coding agents increasingly rely on automated approvers to decide whether a proposed shell command may run. Existing approvers, from rule-based checkers to guardrail models and deployed permission classifiers, base their decisions on the text of the request and command. Yet a command's behavior depends on the code it invokes and the state of the workspace, and systems that observe file changes leave the assessment to the agent or a human after execution. We present Caper, a consequence-aware approval mechanism that pre-executes each command in a snapshotted sandbox, provides an independent approver with a bounded report of its observed effects, commits allowed commands, and rolls back blocked ones with a reason the agent can act on. Compared with six existing systems, Caper achieves the lowest harmful-outcome rate on SABER (6.7% versus at least 14.8%) and YoloFS-Ext, a benchmark we build in which harmful behavior is hidden inside invoked tools (7.8% versus at least 35.3%), while blocking 1.0% of the safe twins of the dangerous tasks in YoloFS-Ext.

title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
authors: Jun Cen, Yubo Guo, Hao Li, Liangkai Li, Yaoxu Lyu, Meng Wei, Zeqi Xiao, Sizhe Yang, Yuqiang Yang, Yifan Ye, Shanghang Zhang, Duo Zheng
abstract: Achieving the broad task generalization of embodied models in physical environments remains a central challenge in robot learning. We study this challenge in World Action Models (WAMs) through two complementary capabilities: video generalization, which predicts the visual evolution of new tasks, and action generalization, which translates these predictions into executable behavior through a video-to-action bridge. By varying video and action supervision for tasks outside an initial training set, we examine their respective contributions to task transfer. On RoboTwin 2.0, using only in-distribution video-action supervision yields a 25.07% success rate on out-of-distribution tasks. Introducing videos of these tasks without their action labels raises success to 55.90%, while adding just one action-labeled demonstration per task further improves it to 70.70%. These findings suggest that broader video coverage enables task transfer by leveraging existing inverse-dynamics capabilities, while even sparse action supervision further strengthens those capabilities. Guided by this perspective, we introduce WorldBridge, a WAM with separate video and action experts connected through structured attention and trained with joint flow matching. WorldBridge incorporates visual memory at two temporal scales and action forcing, alongside a unified data processing pipeline that standardizes and filters heterogeneous robot trajectories and egocentric hand-derived supervision. Across multiple manipulation benchmarks, WorldBridge achieves state-of-the-art performance among the compared methods, including 96.23% on RoboTwin 2.0 full data setting and 80.9% on clean to random setting, 82.8% on RoboCasa GR1 TableTop, and 57.6% on DOMINO Level-1. Our study highlights the complementary roles of video prediction and action grounding in developing robots that generalize across tasks.
comment: Authors are listed in alphabetical order. Project page: https://worldbridge-jd.github.io/

title: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
authors: Jeff Tan, Hang Dai, Zeqian Long, Yanzhe Lyu, R. Kenny Jones, Shangzhe Wu, Chen Geng, Jiajun Wu
abstract: While frontier coding agents can generate high-quality 3D scenes and articulated assets, they struggle to create coherent long-horizon animations. When equipped with general-purpose harnesses, they frequently produce physically implausible outputs, generating objects that interpenetrate, lack physical support, or move unnaturally. Such bare agents struggle to repair these errors because they default to scripting the full animation in one pass, making it difficult to verify their work and disentangle complex spatiotemporal constraints. Drawing on the practice of human animators, we introduce DyCraft, a system for animated 3D scene generation that breaks animation into steps that coding agents can more reliably solve. DyCraft first expands the user's prompt into a detailed plan and builds a static scene. It then creates a 3D storyboard of key animation poses, where each frame is a static 3D scene that the agent can build and debug in isolation. Storyboarding decomposes the problem into pairs of verified start and end states, allowing the agent to author local motion between them with a collection of motion authoring tools. We evaluate DyCraft on 24 long-horizon, multi-shot animation tasks covering humanoid robots, human and animal characters, and physical mechanisms. Compared with a native GPT-6 agent in Codex and prior agentic baselines, DyCraft substantially reduces physical violations and generates higher-quality animated 3D scenes that are more often preferred by human raters.

title: TAPE: Learning General Audio Effect Representations
authors: Phillip Long, Yongyi Zang, Qihui Yang, Christodoulos Benetatos, Junfei Liu, Randal Leistikow, Julian McAuley, Perry R. Cook
abstract: Musicians and mixing engineers often can decipher the signal processing chain they hear on a reference recording, then adapt it to new material. We present TAPE (Transformations of Audio Parameter Embeddings), which estimates this processing from the processed reference audio alone. An encoder trained to identify processors in eight major effect families maps the reference to an embedding. A differentiable digital signal processing (DSP) chain decodes the embedding into editable parameters in one forward pass and applies them to a different unprocessed recording. Its modules are equalization, compression, waveshaping, a small residual network, and reverberation. TAPE achieves lower spectral error than DeepAFx-ST, the previous state of the art for single-step regression, and lower spectral error than per-example search over a chain approximating ST-ITO's, while running 275$\times$ faster than that search. Because the decoder outputs DSP parameters, its chain can also run causally: a C++ implementation with the trained weights processed 128-sample buffers 1.8$\times$ faster than real time, with no missed deadlines.
comment: Submitted to Transactions of Machine Learning Research; 25 pages, 5 figures, 18 tables

title: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn
authors: Daniel Levine, David van Dijk, Kenneth Kay
abstract: Humans and animals have a unique capacity to generalize and learn in novel circumstances, including "0-shot" inference (ZI) and continual learning (CL) -- two powerful cognitive abilities. Despite this importance, efforts to model ZI and CL are seriously limited in several ways. First, existing models typically lack components critical to ZI and CL in the brain, namely, strong inductive biases (for ZI) and autonomous control of learning (for CL). Second, models can be less tractable to analysis if model components are overly complex (lacking simplicity), or too task-restricted if model components are overly bespoke (lacking expressivity). Here we introduce autonomous Hebbian networks ("AutoHebb"), a class of online learning feedforward neural networks that realize strong inductive biases and autonomously controlled learning, and are both simple and expressive. Unlike standard models that learn via externally controlled optimization (e.g. gradient descent), AutoHebb networks combine external feedback with internally generated activity to produce a global learning signal ('neuromodulator') fed back to the network. The neuromodulator in turn gates a biologically grounded local learning rule (3-factor Hebbian rule) that updates networks' plastic weights. Using meta-learning to search for fixed (non-plastic) weights, we find that AutoHebb networks (1) succeed on ZI tasks, (2) show emergent (untrained) ZI/CL abilities, (3) admit reverse-engineering into explicit algorithms, and (4) outperform modern learning models on ZI/CL tasks. Lastly, performance comparisons to related models implied an essential role for three model components: meta-learning, Hebbian plasticity, and autonomous control of learning. These findings indicate that AutoHebb may be useful in hypothesis generation, analysis, and discovery of biologically grounded forms of learning and generalization.

title: Uniform Non-Deterministic Semantics for Ciuciura's $mbC^n$-Hierarchy
authors: Ela Drozdowska, Pawel Pawlowski
abstract: We introduce a uniform non-deterministic semantics for the hierarchy of paraconsistent systems mbC^n introduced by Ciuciura. The proposed construction generalizes Omori's three-valued semantics for mbC^1 to all systems of the hierarchy. We prove soundness and completeness of the semantics with respect to the corresponding axiomatizations and show that the consequence relations of the systems mbC^n cannot be characterized by finite deterministic matrices.

title: Retrieve-then-Disambiguate: Scalable Reviewer Discovery
authors: Vicente Amado Olivo, Joe Petrecca, Wolfgang E. Kerzendorf
abstract: The growing number of scientific submissions is straining the peer review process, while a large pool of relevant researchers remains unidentified and is therefore not considered as potential reviewers. We formulate the discovery of these researchers as a retrieval problem: given a submission, we retrieve and rank researchers based on domain similarity. We present retrieve-then-disambiguate, an open-source algorithm that identifies domain relevant researchers for a query submission by retrieving similar publications from the scientific literature and resolving ambiguous author names into unique researcher identities. We evaluate the algorithm on 500 astronomy and physics publications. We use ORCID-linked first authors, coauthors, and cited researchers as proxy labels to evaluate the recovery of researchers with known connections to each query publication. When retrieving the top 500 most similar papers, the algorithm recovers roughly 68\% of first authors, 60\% of coauthors, and 45\% of cited researchers. Our code is available at https://github.com/deepthought-initiative/Retrieve-then-Disambiguate.

title: Personalised 3D Mnemonics for Vocabulary Learning in Context
authors: Karolina Trajkovska, Matjaž Kljun, Maheshya Weerasinghe, Klen Čopič Pucihar
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) can support vocabulary learning by placing mnemonic cues in the physical contexts where new words are encountered. Prior work has augmented real objects with bilingual labels, audio, keywords, and 3D visualisations of those keywords interacting with the objects, but these cues are typically predefined by system designers. This limits scalability and reduces learners' ability to construct personal mnemonic links. By grounding mnemonics in objects that learners already recognise, use, and associate with prior experiences, a system could connect new vocabulary to existing mental models rather than requiring learners to adopt designer-defined associations. We outline a proof of concept and a storyboard of a generative AR approach in which learners create personalised 3D mnemonics by transforming familiar objects in their surroundings into situated mnemonic anchors. We position this concept within a timeline of related work and argue that recent advances in generative 3D asset creation enable a new design point: personalised 3D mnemonics that do not merely place content in the physical learning environment, but modify familiar real-world objects so that they become part of the mnemonic itself.

title: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum
authors: Chenjie Qiu, Boyan Xu, Shaobin Shi, Bingfeng Chen, Ruichu Cai, Dongsheng Luo
abstract: Self-evolving agents rewrite a persistent state from feedback, but it is largely untested whether this lets them learn a rule nobody told them. An agent can also pass by writing down each correction as an exception, and its list then grows with every new rule. We introduce CLR-Bench, a Curriculum of Latent Rules benchmark. Each chain adds one hidden rule per level on top of the earlier ones. A rule acts on an opaque label that stands for a named grouping published on the Web, such as the founding members of an airline alliance. The task gives one example value, practice feedback reveals one more member and one non-member, and the test checks unseen members and similar non-members. Probes certify that the base model knows the members of each grouping and does not guess it without feedback, and that the evidence identifies the grouping once labels are read as named groupings. An automated pipeline builds chains from a new data domain, and we release 20 chains over 10 domains. We evaluate six recent self-evolution methods. With the certifying model they barely learn. The best gain at most 5 points over a frozen agent and exclude only 6-12% of the unseen members from the count, fewer than the 20% reached by simply keeping the raw practice history. A fixed lesson that states the named-grouping convention lifts the same methods by 14.5 to 16.5 points. Their states hold the revealed member in 75-98% of cases and almost never the class name, and when practice exposes a member the list misses, they add that member to the list. With the stronger GPT-6-Sol, ACE and Dynamic Cheatsheet learn from feedback alone. They reach 78% accuracy and solve 59-60% of the single cells, against 53% and 8% with the certifying model, and they surpass the raw history. CLR-Bench therefore measures how well an agent learns, and this ability differs across models.

title: On Some Logics Intermediate Between S4.2 and S4.3 Defined by the Notion of Independence
authors: Maciej A. Hałapacz
abstract: Hamkins and Loewe described modal logic S4.2 through the notion of sets of independent buttons - statements that are possibly necessary - and switches - necessarily contingent statements. In this article we investigate logics intermediate between S4.2 and S4.3 that are defined through a different notion of independence. We provide an axiomatic description of such logics, state some basic facts and prove various completeness and decidability results.

title: A Basic Modal Logic for the Abstract Treatment of Quantum Mixed States
authors: Tomoaki Kawano
abstract: Quantum logic has developed in various directions since its inception. However, many existing logical approaches either focus only on pure states, or use Hilbert-space models in which the abstract relationship between pure states, mixed states, and probabilities is not made explicit. In this work, we introduce a model designed to handle quantum mixed states abstractly. Furthermore, we construct a proof system for the proposed logic and establish its completeness with respect to the intended semantics.

title: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models
authors: Zhifei Hu, Alexandra I. Cristea, Adel Bibi, Jialin Yu
abstract: Web world models increasingly predict the consequences of candidate actions before agents act, yet a plausible predicted future does not necessarily support the correct safety decision. In a matched human evaluation of 3,000 predictions from ten frozen open models, 86.1% are judged semantically plausible. However, several models exhibit highly asymmetric authorisation behaviour, combining low false-safe execution with poor recall of clarifiable ASK cases and a strong preference for BLOCK. This motivates safety sufficiency: whether a predictive interface preserves and exposes the policy-decisive information required to distinguish actions that may be EXECUTED, require clarification through ASK, or should be BLOCKED. We introduce SafeWebWorld, a benchmark for evaluating safety sufficiency across five web-safety domains through action-conditioned futures, policy-decisive evidence, and policy-conditioned decisions. Under a controlled Security-Aligned Supervised Fine-Tuning protocol, evidence preservation can improve substantially while authorisation-sensitive decisions deteriorate. To determine whether this deterioration reflects loss of authorisation-sensitive score structure or a failure of the decision readout, we introduce Latent Authorisation Recovery (LAR). Frozen-score recalibration reveals substantial but backbone-dependent recovery, while paired recovery provides only a modest additional gain. Yet within-family and matched-authorisation evaluations remain poor, showing that aggregate recoverability does not imply robust fine-grained authorisation behaviour. Overall, plausible prediction, evidence preservation, and aggregate recovery are each insufficient on their own to establish robust authorisation.

title: Drone-PUR: From Visual Clue Discovery to Understanding and Reasoning in UAV Scenes
authors: Jiahe Wu, Bing Cao, Xingyue Guo, Ruipu Zhao, Beiming Yu, Jiekang Feng, Qinghua Hu, Pengfei Zhu
abstract: The reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) can be limited by incomplete or inaccurate visual observations in the general domain. In unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) scenes, small targets, subtle attributes, and changing viewpoints further complicate perception and understanding. Therefore, we introduce Drone-PUR, a dataset and benchmark organized around visual clue discovery, interpretation, and integration, corresponding to the three capability dimensions of perception, understanding, and reasoning. Reasoning samples are designed to require models to combine multiple visual clues to derive visually grounded conclusions. Its 11 tasks provide 175k training and 20k test samples spanning single images, image sequences, cross-modal images, and multiple viewpoints. All test samples undergo human review. Evaluating 22 general-purpose VLMs reveals persistent limitations in spatial judgment and cross-modal and cross-view reasoning. Across models, stronger perception is associated with better reasoning, while single-task fine-tuning further reveals selective bidirectional transfer between these capabilities. To examine domain adaptation, we develop UAV-PUR from Qwen3-VL through staged fine-tuning with auxiliary supervision. Its 4B and 8B variants improve overall multiple-choice accuracy by 18.33 and 17.52 percentage points over their pretrained counterparts, respectively. The dataset and project resources are available at https://drone-pur.github.io.

title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
authors: Yijia Fan, Xilin He, Yilei Jiang, Dongming Wu, Jiaxu Wang, Xiangyu Yue
abstract: Across coding, web, and tool-use tasks, language-model agents are now routinely trained with the same recipe: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn the interface, then multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) to master it. Code-as-policy (CaP) casts robot manipulation in the same form, as the policy writes code against robot APIs and reads back the results, so the same recipe should apply. Yet existing CaP agents sidestep training: they either prompt closed frontier models or delegate manipulation to pre-trained vision-language-action models (VLAs) and high-level skills, while small open vision-language models (VLMs) fail outright. We present CaPtain, an open post-training pipeline that turns a small open VLM into a capable CaP agent, with no VLA, frontier model, or privileged state at test time. CaPtain trains and deploys the policy inside CaPtain-Harness, which exposes low-level perception, geometry, and guarded-motion primitives across simulation and real hardware. We first align the base model via SFT on synthetic trajectories generated with GPT-6 Astra, then apply multi-turn RL. Multi-turn RL must credit tens of agent requests, whose physical effects often surface turns later, from a single end-of-episode outcome. We therefore introduce a physical critic that reads privileged simulator state, never seen by the policy, and credits each request by how much it changes the predicted chance of success. Starting from Qwen3.5-4B (0% zero-shot), CaPtain-4B reaches 55.4% held-out LIBERO success after SFT and 73.8% after RL. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 78.5%, surpassing several frontier-model agents, and its RL gains persist across three perturbation suites (+17.6 to +21.2 points). Without target-domain training, it attains 83.3% on SimplerEnv WidowX, exceeds frontier models on CaP-Bench, and runs on a real robot after simulation-only adaptation. We release all code, data, and model weights.

title: On Łukasiewicz Topological Semantics
authors: Muhammad Afaq Khan, Manuel A. Martins, Alexandre Madeira, Babar Zaman
abstract: In this paper, we propose fuzzy topological semantics for Łukasiewicz valued modal logic, based on the standard Łukasiewicz algebra. Within this setting, formulas are interpreted as fuzzy sets of truth values, while the modal operators are realized through fuzzy interior and closure operators. We define a Kripke-induced fuzzy Alexandroff topology and establish a precise correspondence between Łukasiewicz fuzzy Kripke semantics and its topological counterpart. The proposed topological semantics validates the S4 modal axioms that include reflexivity, transitivity, monotonicity, normality, and the necessitation of truth.

title: On the Reconstruction of Orthomodular Logic via Restricted Negation
authors: Tomoaki Kawano, Ryo Kashima
abstract: Orthomodular logic has long been studied as a fundamental logical framework within quantum logic. In addition to its lattice-theoretic foundations, various formulations have been proposed that incorporate specialized implication connectives and more complex logical connectives. In this study, we reconstruct orthomodular logic by introducing a connective referred to as restricted negation, which has received comparatively little attention in the existing literature. We demonstrate that this connective provides a natural and expressive basis for formulating the core principles of orthomodular logic. Furthermore, as a main result, we construct a new proof system for orthomodular logic founded on this connective.

title: Merging and Evolution of Data Bases: A Many-Logic Approach
authors: Manuel A. Martins, Abilio Rodrigues
abstract: A new approach to information-based logics using many-logic modal structures (MLMSs) was recently proposed by Martins et al. In such a setting, it is possible to have worlds with different underlying logics within the same frame, all anchored to a base lattice that contains the semantics of each logic as a down-complete sublattice. In this paper, we take the lattice L6, defined by the six-valued semantics of the logic of evidence and truth LET + K , as our base lattice. We also consider four-, three-, and two-valued formal systems associated with down-complete sublattices of L6. These logics are capable of representing paracomplete, paraconsistent, and classical contexts with six, four, three, and two informational scenarios, respectively. As applications of MLMSs, we will discuss the merging and temporal evolution of databases whose underlying logics are two-, three-, four-, and six-valued. We will also investigate inconsistency measures in this context.

title: Paraclassical Logics with Two Negations
authors: Pawel Pawlowski, Pietro Vigiani
abstract: We study three paraclassical propositional logics with two negations, CLoaN, CLouN, and CLauN, obtained by pairwise combining the one-negation systems CLuN, CLaN, and CLoN.  CLuN's negation  is glut-tolerant and paraconsistent, CLaN's negationis gap-tolerant and paracomplete, and CLoN's negation is both paraconsistent and paracomplete. We provide sound and complete two-valued non-deterministic semantics for each of the two-negations systems. We then focus on CLauN, the system containing the primitive dual pair of CLaN and CLuN negations. In this setting, we show deductive relationships between different negations expressible in CLauN; we show two diferent ways to recapture classical logic by means of translations, locally and globally; and we show a duality results for the multiple conclusion consequence relation of the logic.

title: Restricted Peirce's Law and Natural Deduction
authors: Satoru Niki
abstract: The constructive logic JP' is known to be the weakest logic between intuitionistic and minimal logic that satisfies Glivenko's theorem. In spite of this natural and desirable formal property, the motivation for its notion of negation remains rather elusive: it can be characterised by a restriction of Peirce's law or by the double negation of ex falso quodlibet, neither of which is very intuitive. In order to have an alternative perspective on this negation, we study in this paper a couple of  natural deduction systems for JP'. We first present a system that is normalisable and satisfies a restricted form of the subformula property. Then a modification of this system is introduced, whose rules satisfy the separation of connectives and the full subformula property. Afterwards we turn our attention to a typed lambda-calculus, with respect to which our natural deduction enjoys the Curry-Howard correspondence, followed by a concluding discussion.

title: Normalisation for a Neutral Free Logic with Definite Descriptions
authors: Yaroslav Petrukhin
abstract: In this paper, we present a natural deduction system for a strong Kleene-based neutral free logic with definite descriptions. The system combines a three-valued propositional basis with free quantification, identity, existence, and rules for definite descriptions. The main result is a normalisation theorem for a proof-theoretically equivalent restricted formulation of the system; we also establish a corresponding modified subformula property for its fragment.

title: Cyclic Nonassociative Bilinear Logic With Additive Constants as Extension of Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus
authors: Paweł Płaczek, Cheng-Syuan Wan
abstract: Cyclic Linear Logic (CyMALL, CyBL) is a compromise between Commutative Linear Logic (MALL) and Noncommutative Linear Logic (Bilinear Logic, BL). We do not admit commutativity of the tensor, but we still admit only one De Morgan negation. MALL and its variants are natural extensions of Full Lambek Calculus (FL). Abrusci proved that CyBL is not a conservative extension of FL, if we admit additive constants in these logics. In this paper we show that Cyclic Nonassociative Bilinear Logic (CyNBL) with both additive constants is a strongly conservative extension of Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus with only one additive constant - the upper bound - and that this holds even in the presence of an arbitrary set of nonlogical axioms.

title: Quantifying Linepack Storage Potential of Hydrogen Networks
authors: Ulrike Herrmann, Hans Würfel, Albertus Johannes Malan, Anton Plietzsch, Johannes Schiffer
abstract: Future hydrogen systems depend on large-scale storage to balance supply and demand. Hydrogen networks can store energy in the pipelines themselves, but the potential of this linepack storage has not been quantified comparably to dedicated storage facilities. We transfer metrics established for conventional storage, such as volume capacity and full-cycle equivalents, to hydrogen networks. To evaluate them, we formulate an optimization problem maximizing linepack storage utilization, subject to non-convex PDE-based constraints describing transient gas flow. We solve the optimization problem over a full-year horizon to capture seasonal variations and to assess the interaction with cavern storage. For computational tractability, we propose a simulation-informed sequential convex programming approach with adaptive time stepping that reduces problem size by up to 98% at accuracy comparable to fixed-resolution methods. For the GasLib-40 topology with German scenario data, the network provides a volume capacity of 24 million normal cubic meters at 28 full-cycle equivalents per year.
comment: 23 pages, 6 figures, submitted to the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy

title: On the NP-Hardness of Rank-Metric Minimum Distance and Syndrome Decoding, at Every Rate
authors: Venkata Gandikota, Vatsal Jha, S. Venkitesh
abstract: In this work, we investigate the hardness of computing minimum distance, as well as the hardness of syndrome decoding, for rank-metric codes. It is known (Gaborit and Zémor, IEEE TIT 2016) that for $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-linear rank-metric codes of length $N$, minimum distance when $m=O(N)$ and syndrome decoding when $m=O(N^2)$ are NP-hard under randomized reductions. We obtain a derandomization of these results and a bit more. We show that for any fixed small $\varepsilon>0$, for $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-linear rank-metric codes of length $N$ with $m=O(N^{1+\varepsilon})$, the problems of minimum distance, nearest codeword, and syndrome decoding are NP-hard under deterministic reductions. Further, we can prescribe the rate; that is, if we restrict to codes having any fixed rational rate $R\in(0,1)$, then the NP-hardness for all three problems persists. Our main technical contribution is simple, and possibly of independent interest. The reduction of Gaborit and Zémor (IEEE TIT 2016) relies on a distance-preserving embedding of a Hamming-metric code into a rank-metric code, obtained by multiplying its coordinates by a uniformly random vector. We show that we can choose an explicit vector from a slightly larger extension field.
comment: A longer version of this manuscript has been submitted for publication

title: Tight Lower Bounds for Distributional Paging
authors: Ali Vakilian
abstract:
Distributional paging seeks a polynomial-time eviction rule that competes with the optimal \emph{online} policy $\mathrm{OPT}$ when requests come from a known stochastic source. Two algorithms by Lund, Phillips, and Reingold [FOCS, 1994] are canonical. Their randomized \emph{dominating distribution} algorithm, for Markov sources, evicts a page drawn from a distribution over the cache satisfying pairwise linear inequalities; their deterministic \emph{median} algorithm, for sources with independent inter-arrival times across pages, evicts the cached page with the largest lower median of its conditional next-request time. Their original guarantees of $4$ and $5$ were recently improved to $2$ and $4$ by Pabbaraju and Vakilian [ICALP 2025].
  We show that neither improved constant can be reduced in its respective source model. For Markov paging, we give two complementary factor-$2$ lower-bound constructions, each with an explicit polynomial-time dominating selector. A directed-cycle family has ratio $2k/(k+1)$, while a recurrent four-page family with cache size three has ratio $2-4\varepsilon/3$.
  For the independent inter-arrival model, we show that the median algorithm is not $c$-competitive for any $c<4$. These are separate results for distinct stochastic models. Matching the known upper bounds, they establish tight competitive ratios of $2$ and $4$, respectively, improving on previous lower bounds of $1.5907$ and $1.511$.

title: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation
authors: Ammar N. Abbas, Aayush Jain, Prashanth Viswanath, Nivesh Gadipudi, Giulia Vilone, Jim Gibbons
abstract: Imitation learning policies are intended to make robotic manipulation robust to variations in object pose, appearance, and environment that challenge pre-programmed motion. However, real-world performance remains difficult to predict, as conventional optimization signals such as validation loss show no consistent relationship with robot success. To identify the design choices that govern real-world performance, 281 imitation-learning policies spanning seven policy families were evaluated in approximately 1,700 real-robot trials of RJ45 connector grasping and insertion using a five-fingered robotic hand. Controlled ablations showed that observation and action representations dominated conventional optimizer and sampling choices. For point-cloud policies, region-of-interest cropping, representation in the robot-base frame, and normalization within the point encoder each improved success by 70-100 percentage points. For the vision-language-action policy, absolute rather than relative action prediction improved insertion success by up to 70 percentage points. Skill decomposition, multi-view perception, and recovery demonstrations were associated with the strongest-performing systems, although their effects were not independently isolated. Of 67 offline metrics evaluated, only five measures of predicted-motion smoothness and directness reliably correlated with insertion success (r = -0.70 to -0.80), and only within a single policy family. These results identify representation choices as key determinants of real-world imitation-learning performance and show that offline metrics can shortlist policies, but cannot replace real-robot evaluation.

title: Arithmetical Characterizations of Two Intuitionistic Logical Principles
authors: Kaito Ichikura
abstract: This paper investigates the role of negation in arithmetic by analyzing subsystems based on subminimal logic. We introduce NA^PR, a system of subminimal arithmetic equipped with all primitive recursive functions, and answer the following four questions: (1) Can we develop reasonable arithmetic within NA^PR? (2) Can we characterize logical rules Absorption of Negation (An) and Ex Falso Quodlibet (ECQ) by arithmetical principles? (3) Are there strict differences in deductive power among NA^PR, MA^PR, and HA? (4) Do MA^PR and MA, and NA^PR and NA have a similar mutual interpretability relationship as HA? We show the following: First, Heyting Arithmetic (HA) is shown to be a conservative extension of NA^PR for positive formulas. Based on NA^PR, we prove that (ECQ) is equivalent to the definability of disjunction, and that (An) is equivalent to a variant of the least number principle. Furthermore, using the constant domain neighbourhood semantics, we show that the systems NA^PR, MA^PR (written as NA^PR+(An)) and HA (written as NA^PR+(An)+(ECQ)) form a strictly increasing hierarchy of strength. Finally, we demonstrate the essential role of primitive recursive functions in weak arithmetic using classical countermodels.

title: Tableaux Rules for Theories of Definite Descriptions in Positive Free Logic with Some Philosophical Remarks
authors: Nils Kürbis
abstract: While Russell's theory of definite descriptions, expressions of the form 'the F', is almost incontrovertible in classical logic, in free logic matters stand differently. Several alternatives have been proposed. In Lambert's hierarchy, the weakest theory is his minimal free theory of definite descriptions (MFD), which only says that anything is the F iff it is the unique existing F, the strongest one is a chosen object theory in which all improper definite descriptions refer to the same object (FD2). Intermediate is Lambert's FD1, which adds ix(x = t) = t as an axiom to MFD. MFD is very weak. FD2 is very strong. One might hope to find intermediate systems in which ix(x = t) = t is provable from more fundamental principles. The present paper considers one avenue where one might hope to find them and closes it. Two theories, FDA and FDH, will be considered that are motivated by considerations from proof-theoretic semantics. The former turns out to be equivalent to FD2, the latter to have unreasonable consequences. A third theory, similarly motivated, is also not viable. The philosophical upshot of this is briefly discussed.

title: Circumventing the Computational Hardness of Computational Arbitrage
authors: Nastaran Okati, Ricardo Olmedo, Moritz Hardt
abstract: AI model marketplaces host providers with heterogeneous costs and capabilities. These differences create an opportunity for computational arbitrage (Olmedo et al., 2026), in which an intermediary purchases inference from a portfolio of models and resells it to users at a profit. Beyond creating profit opportunities for the arbitrageur, computational arbitrage offers financial value to both consumers and providers and could therefore significantly influence AI model markets. While prior work empirically demonstrates the feasibility of computational arbitrage for small model pools, scaling it to large marketplaces requires arbitrage strategies that are both computationally tractable and inexpensive to identify and deploy. In this work, we formalize computational arbitrage as an allocation problem and prove that it is generally NP-hard. However, we show that the optimal allocation can be computed efficiently under a natural diminishing-returns condition on how model performance scales with inference spending. We further develop a sample-efficient method for estimating model performance from limited data, reducing the upfront cost of identifying arbitrage strategies. Our analysis also yields several economic insights: at the optimum, every funded model delivers the same marginal utility per dollar; arbitrage directs revenue away from providers offering little utility relative to their prices; and it rewards complementary specialization.

title: How Global Is Anycast?: Evaluating Performance Gaps
authors: Mohammad Shaikh Sadid Khan, Karishma Setya, ASM Rizvi
abstract: Anycast networks aim to reduce latency by directing users to nearby service sites. However, users can still experience high latency even when accessing services via anycast. Some anycast deployments are localized and intended to serve a specific geographic region, while others are globally distributed to support users worldwide, with the expectation of consistently low latency across locations. In practice, latency can remain poor for certain users due to factors such as routing inefficiencies and peering relationships. These inefficiencies are often more pronounced in regions such as Africa, Asia or South America, where Internet connectivity is generally less mature than in North America or Europe. Despite this, there has been no in-depth analysis of anycast performance in these continents. In this paper, we examine the latency experienced by users in these regions when accessing anycast networks. We analyze more than 10,000 anycast prefixes, quantify the severity of latency problems, and show that clients in Africa, Asia, and South America experience substantially higher latency than those in North America. We also investigate the underlying causes of this performance gap.
zh_title: Anycast有多全球化？：评估性能差距
translation: Anycast网络旨在通过将用户导向附近的服务站点来降低延迟。然而，即使通过Anycast访问服务，用户仍可能经历高延迟。一些Anycast部署是本地化的，旨在服务特定的地理区域，而另一些则是全球分布式，以支持世界各地的用户，并期望在所有位置提供一致的低延迟。实际上，由于路由效率低下和对等关系等因素，某些用户的延迟可能仍然很差。这些效率低下在非洲、亚洲或南美洲等地区通常更为明显，这些地区的互联网连接通常不如北美或欧洲成熟。尽管如此，这些大陆的Anycast性能尚未得到深入分析。本文中，我们检查了这些地区用户在访问Anycast网络时所经历的延迟。我们分析了超过10,000个Anycast前缀，量化了延迟问题的严重性，并表明非洲、亚洲和南美洲的客户端比北美洲的客户端经历显著更高的延迟。我们还调查了造成这种性能差距的根本原因。
tldr: Anycast网络旨在降低延迟，但非洲、亚洲和南美洲的用户仍面临显著更高的延迟，这主要是由于路由效率低下，且这些区域的性能此前缺乏深入分析。
ai_comments: 该论文揭示了Anycast网络在全球服务质量方面存在的一个关键差异，对全球相当一部分人口产生了影响。其关注未被充分研究的地区（非洲、亚洲、南美洲）并量化性能差距，为网络运营商和研究人员提供了宝贵的见解，有助于改善全球互联网的公平性和效率。
motivation: Anycast网络旨在通过将用户导向附近的服务站点来降低延迟，但某些用户（尤其是在互联网连接不如北美或欧洲成熟的非洲、亚洲和南美洲地区）仍会经历高延迟。尽管存在这种现象，但这些大陆的Anycast性能尚未得到深入分析，因此本研究旨在填补这一空白，调查这些区域的延迟问题。
method: 本研究检查了非洲、亚洲和南美洲用户在访问Anycast网络时所经历的延迟。论文分析了超过10,000个Anycast前缀，量化了延迟问题的严重性，并调查了造成这种性能差距的根本原因。
results: 研究发现，非洲、亚洲和南美洲的客户端在访问Anycast网络时，其延迟显著高于北美洲的客户端。论文量化了延迟问题的严重性，并揭示了造成这种性能差距的潜在原因。
conclusion: Anycast网络的性能并非在全球范围内一致，非洲、亚洲和南美洲的用户由于路由效率低下和对等关系等因素，在访问Anycast服务时会经历比北美用户更高的延迟。

title: EgoHSI3R: Online 4D Hand-Scene Interaction Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
authors: Mingzhi Pei, Zhangchen Ye, Ruoqu Chen, Liu Cao, Mengdi Xu
abstract: Egocentric videos offer an abundant source of hand-scene interactions for embodied learning, which requires recovering hands, camera, and scene consistently in a shared 3D world. Existing methods focus on either camera-frame hands or world-space hand trajectories, without jointly recovering the scene pointmaps or interaction information. Building a complete reconstruction from such specialized predictions therefore typically requires per-sequence optimization. We propose EgoHSI3R, a unified feed-forward framework for online 4D hand-scene interaction reconstruction from egocentric monocular video. To jointly recover these components, it maintains a recurrent scene representation that accumulates geometric evidence over time and provides a shared world space and scale. We introduce hand-centric prompts that fuse pretrained hand priors and local scene context, while MANO vertex queries attend to scene features to predict dense per-vertex contact. These designs enable a single network to jointly estimate camera motion, dense scene geometry, world-space bilateral MANO hands, and per-vertex hand contact. Despite operating causally, EgoHSI3R achieves the lowest world-space hand joint error on ARCTIC among the evaluated methods, while offering faster inference than existing world-space hand reconstruction pipelines and competitive camera and scene reconstruction accuracy.
zh_title: EgoHSI3R：基于第一人称视频的在线4D手部-场景交互重建
translation: 第一人称视频为具身学习提供了丰富的手部-场景交互来源，这需要在一个共享的3D世界中一致地恢复手部、相机和场景。现有方法侧重于相机坐标系下的手部或世界空间中的手部轨迹，而没有联合恢复场景点云图或交互信息。因此，从这些专业化预测构建完整的重建通常需要针对每个序列进行优化。我们提出了EgoHSI3R，一个统一的前馈框架，用于从第一人称单目视频进行在线4D手部-场景交互重建。为了联合恢复这些组件，它维护了一个循环场景表示，该表示随时间积累几何证据，并提供共享的世界空间和尺度。我们引入了以手为中心的提示，融合了预训练的手部先验和局部场景上下文，同时MANO顶点查询关注场景特征以预测密集的每顶点接触。这些设计使单个网络能够联合估计相机运动、密集场景几何、世界空间中的双边MANO手部模型以及每顶点手部接触。尽管是因果操作，EgoHSI3R在评估方法中在ARCTIC数据集上实现了最低的世界空间手部关节误差，同时提供了比现有世界空间手部重建管线更快的推理速度，并在相机和场景重建精度方面具有竞争力。
tldr: EgoHSI3R是一个统一的前馈框架，用于从第一人称单目视频在线重建4D手部-场景交互，它能同时估计相机运动、场景几何、世界空间中的手部姿态和每顶点接触，并在ARCTIC数据集上实现了最低的世界空间手部关节误差和更快的推理速度。
ai_comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于提出了一个统一的、前馈的在线框架，能够从第一人称视频中同时重建4D手部-场景交互的所有关键组件，包括相机、手部和场景几何，并解决了一致性和效率问题。其循环场景表示和手部中心提示是关键的技术贡献，显著提高了世界空间手部重建的精度和速度，对于具身学习和人机交互领域具有重要意义。
motivation: 现有方法在手部-场景交互重建方面存在局限性，它们通常只关注相机坐标系下的手部或世界空间中的手部轨迹，未能联合恢复场景点云图或交互信息，并且通常需要针对每个序列进行优化才能获得完整的重建。
method: 本文提出了EgoHSI3R，一个统一的前馈框架，用于从第一人称单目视频进行在线4D手部-场景交互重建。该方法通过维护一个循环场景表示来随时间积累几何证据，提供共享的世界空间和尺度。它引入了以手为中心的提示，融合预训练的手部先验和局部场景上下文，同时MANO顶点查询关注场景特征以预测密集的每顶点接触。这些设计使单个网络能够联合估计相机运动、密集场景几何、世界空间中的双边MANO手部模型以及每顶点手部接触。
results: EgoHSI3R在ARCTIC数据集上取得了最低的世界空间手部关节误差，优于所有评估方法。此外，它比现有的世界空间手部重建管线提供了更快的推理速度，并在相机和场景重建精度方面具有竞争力。
conclusion: EgoHSI3R成功地提供了一个高效且准确的在线4D手部-场景交互重建解决方案，克服了现有方法的局限性，实现了手部、相机和场景在共享3D世界中的一致恢复。

title: Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss Ensembles for Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation
authors: Grant N. Chau, Bashirul A. Biswas, Biratal Wagle, Matthew E. Maeder, Michael S. Leapman, James B. Yu, Indrani Bhattacharya
abstract: Existing whole-body PSMA PET/CT prostate metastasis segmentation methods generally rely on images alone, without explicitly incorporating where metastases tend to occur. We investigate whether a population metastasis atlas can improve lesion detection when integrated into model training. We constructed voxel-wise mean and standard deviation maps from 375 expert-annotated training scans and used them to weight the cross-entropy loss of an nnU-Net. The additional penalties for missed lesions and false positives depend on spatial atlas statistics and diminish as predictions become confidently correct. Seven configurations were compared on validation data; three were combined by majority voting into SAILS (Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss enSemble). We compared SAILS with a baseline nnU-Net and inference-time atlas fusion on AutoPET~III (110 disease-positive cases) and Deep-PSMA (100 external cases). No atlas or registration is needed at inference. Results: On AutoPET~III, SAILS improved whole-body Dice (0.531 vs. 0.520; p=0.006), reduced missed-lesion volume (9.5 vs. 12.1 cc/case; p<0.01), and increased pooled lesion sensitivity (0.857 vs. 0.843; p=0.004). On Deep-PSMA, SAILS detected 126 additional reference lesions (sensitivity 0.769 vs. 0.751; p<0.001), without a significant whole-body Dice change (-0.009; p=0.36). High-risk bone Dice improved in both cohorts (0.576 vs. 0.552 and 0.667 vs. 0.653; both p<0.01). False-positive volume increased by 2.3 and 18.2 cc/case, respectively (p<0.001). Atlas-weighted training improves lesion detection, especially in high-risk bone, without test-time atlas registration, but increases false positives.
zh_title: 基于空间图谱引导的损失集成用于全身PSMA PET/CT转移灶分割
translation: 现有的全身PSMA PET/CT前列腺癌转移灶分割方法通常仅依赖图像本身，未显式结合转移灶倾向发生部位的信息。我们探究了将人群转移灶图谱整合进模型训练中是否能够改善病灶检出。我们从375例经专家标注的训练扫描中构建了体素级的均值和标准差图谱，并用其对nnU-Net的交叉熵损失进行加权。对漏诊病灶和假阳性的额外惩罚依赖于空间图谱统计量，并在预测变得可信且正确时逐渐减小。在验证集上对比了7种配置，并将其中3种通过多数投票组合成SAILS（空间图谱引导的损失集成）。我们在AutoPET III（110例阳性病例）和Deep-PSMA（100例外院病例）上对比了SAILS与基线nnU-Net及推理期图谱融合方法。推理阶段无需图谱或配准。结果显示：在AutoPET III上，SAILS提升了全身Dice（0.531 vs. 0.520；p=0.006），减少了漏诊病灶体积（9.5 vs. 12.1 cc/例；p<0.01），并提高了汇总病灶敏感度（0.857 vs. 0.843；p=0.004）。在Deep-PSMA上，SAILS额外检测到126个参考病灶（敏感度0.769 vs. 0.751；p<0.001），且全身Dice无显著变化（-0.009；p=0.36）。在两个队列中，高危骨转移的Dice均获得提升（分别为0.576 vs. 0.552和0.667 vs. 0.653；均p<0.01）。假阳性体积分别增加了2.3和18.2 cc/例（p<0.001）。图谱加权训练能够在无需测试期图谱配准的前提下改善病灶检出（尤其是高危骨转移），但会增加假阳性。
tldr: 该研究提出SAILS方法，将转移灶空间先验图谱融入训练损失函数，在推理无需配准的前提下有效提升了PSMA PET/CT前列腺癌转移灶（特别是骨转移）的检测敏感度。
ai_comments: 该研究的创新之处在于将先验的人群转移病灶空间图谱统计量无缝整合到模型训练的损失函数中，避免了推理阶段繁重且容易出错的图谱配准工作；其重要性体现在有效提升了高危骨骼等区域的微小病灶敏感度与检测表现；局限性在于该方法在提高敏感度和减少漏诊的同时，显著增加了假阳性体积。
motivation: 现有的全身PSMA PET/CT前列腺癌转移灶分割方法通常仅依赖图像本身，缺乏对转移常发解剖部位等先验信息的显式引入。
method: 从375例专家标注的训练扫描中构建体素级均值和标准差图谱，利用其对nnU-Net的交叉熵损失进行加权，对漏诊病灶和假阳性的惩罚依赖于空间图谱统计，并在预测趋于高度自信且正确时逐渐衰减；验证集上对比7种配置，将其中3种通过多数投票集成构建SAILS（空间图谱引导的损失集成模型）；该方法在推理时无需任何图谱或配准。
results: 在AutoPET III数据集上，SAILS提高了全身Dice（0.531 vs. 0.520，p=0.006），降低了漏诊体积（9.5 vs. 12.1 cc/例，p<0.01），并提高了总病灶敏感度（0.857 vs. 0.843，p=0.004）；在Deep-PSMA外部数据集上多检出126个参考病灶（敏感度0.769 vs. 0.751，p<0.001），全身Dice无显著差异；两数据集的高危骨转移Dice均有提升（分别提升至0.576与0.667，均p<0.01）；但假阳性体积分别增加了2.3和18.2 cc/例（p<0.001）。
conclusion: 基于图谱加权的训练方法能够在无需测试阶段图谱配准的前提下改善病灶检出能力（尤其是高危骨骼转移），但会导致假阳性有所增加。

title: The nodally bound-preserving finite element method for the transport equation
authors: Nicolás Espinoza-Contreras, Gabriel Barrenechea, Douglas Pacheco
abstract: Numerical approximations of transport problems, even when stabilised, often violate the bounds respected by the exact solution. Depending on the problem being solved, this can produce non-physical results, such as negative densities or higher-than-unity concentrations. Various bound-preserving numerical methods exist, yet they are usually either conditionally stable or only first-order accurate. In this context, the present work extends the nodally bound-preserving finite element method to the linear transport equation. As a baseline discretisation we use the least-squares finite element method, which is instrumental in achieving unconditional stability for second-order time stepping. It also leads to symmetric algebraic systems, thereby enabling simple, efficient solvers, which we further enhance through Anderson acceleration. Unconditional stability is proved for the backward Euler and Crank--Nicolson discretisations. We also derive error estimates for the fully discrete second-order scheme and provide various numerical examples, including two-phase incompressible flows.
zh_title: 输运方程的节点保界有限元方法
translation: 输运问题数值近似即使在稳定化后，也常常违反精确解所满足的边界条件。根据所求解的问题，这可能会产生非物理结果，例如负密度或大于1的浓度。现有的各种保界数值方法通常要么是条件稳定的，要么仅有一阶精度。在此背景下，本工作将节点保界有限元方法推广到了线性输运方程。作为基准离散化，我们使用了最小二乘有限元方法，这对于实现二阶时间步进的无条件稳定性起到了关键作用。它还导出了对称代数系统，从而实现了简单、高效的求解器，并通过安德森加速（Anderson acceleration）对其进行了进一步增强。证明了后向欧拉和Crank-Nicolson离散化的无条件稳定性。我们还推导了全离散二阶格式的误差估计，并提供了各种数值算例，包括两相不可压缩流。
tldr: 本文提出了一种用于输运方程的节点保界有限元方法，实现了无条件稳定和二阶精度，避免了非物理结果的产生。
ai_comments: 该论文针对输运方程的数值求解中常见的边界违背问题，提出了一种新型的节点保界有限元方法。其创新点在于结合了最小二乘有限元方法，实现了无条件稳定性并保持二阶精度，同时生成对称代数系统以提高求解效率。这对于模拟如两相不可压缩流等物理问题具有重要意义。
motivation: 现有的保数值输运问题解的边界的方法通常存在条件稳定或仅有一阶精度的局限，容易产生非物理结果（如负密度），因此需要发展一种无条件稳定且高精度的保界数值方法。
method: 采用最小二乘有限元方法作为基准离散化手段，结合后向欧拉和Crank-Nicolson时间步进格式，并利用Anderson加速技术提高求解器效率。
results: 证明了后向欧拉和Crank-Nicolson离散化的无条件稳定性，导出了全离散二阶格式的误差估计，并通过包含两相不可压缩流在内的多个数值算例验证了方法的性能。
conclusion: 本文成功将节点保界有限元方法扩展至线性输运方程，证明了其无条件稳定性，导出了误差估计，并通过数值算例验证了其有效性。

title: How a group that cannot communicate knows itself by its enemy
authors: Gregory Falco
abstract: Teams that cannot communicate seem stuck with what each member sees. We show that their opponent can tell them the rest. Silent hunters, jammed robots and traders who never meet all face an adversary that reacts to the group as a whole; every member can read that reaction, a tell, and learn what no member knows alone. One tell can do the work of a message from every member. The adversary would rather hide, but hiding interferes with its own task, and a team that commits in advance to how it will respond decides how much hiding is worth. A committed team never loses when its opponent cares more about its own goals, and does as well as a fully informed team exactly when the opponent's stake outweighs any gain from lying. Below that point the team learns more by trusting less: in a solved Gaussian model it obtains the truth by promising not to use all of it and keeps the cost the opponent would have paid to conceal; an exact test decides when this holds in finite games. How a team spreads its trust matters too. A lone uninformed member with a full-support prior needs a private coin, but with additive squared-error losses two interchangeable members who respond differently replace it, and a small discount on trust insures against misjudging the enemy. Information, on this view, is not only gathered or aggregated; it is produced by how a team commits to respond.
comment: 6 pages main text; 35-page SI Appendix included as an ancillary file. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23743441
zh_title: 无法沟通的群体如何通过敌人了解自己
translation: 无法沟通的团队似乎受限于每个成员所看到的一切。我们展示了它们的对手可以告诉它们其余的信息。沉默的猎人、被干扰的机器人和从未见面的交易员都面临着一个对整个群体做出反应的对手；每个成员都可以读取这种反应，即一个“信号”，并学习到没有任何成员单独知道的信息。一个信号可以完成每个成员发送消息的工作。对手宁愿隐藏，但隐藏会干扰其自身任务，而一个事先承诺如何响应的团队决定了隐藏的价值。当对手更关心自身目标时，一个有承诺的团队永不失败，并且当对手的利害关系大于任何撒谎收益时，其表现与完全知情的团队一样好。低于这个点，团队通过更少信任学习更多：在一个已解决的高斯模型中，它通过承诺不完全使用所有信息来获取真相，并保留对手为隐藏信息所支付的成本；一个精确测试决定了这在有限博弈中何时成立。团队如何分配信任也很重要。一个拥有完全支持先验的单独不知情成员需要一个私人硬币，但对于附加平方误差损失，两个反应不同的可互换成员可以替代它，并且对信任的小幅折价可以防止误判敌人。在这种观点下，信息不仅仅是收集或聚合的；它是由团队承诺如何响应而产生的。
tldr: 本文研究了无法内部沟通的团队如何通过观察其对手的反应来获取集体信息，并指出团队的承诺响应方式可以产生信息。
ai_comments: 本文提出了一种新颖的视角，即在缺乏内部沟通的情况下，外部对抗者的反应可以成为团队获取自我认知和集体信息的重要来源。其创新之处在于将对抗性互动视为一种信息生成机制，而非仅仅是信息对抗。这种观点对于理解非中心化系统、博弈论和信息不对称环境下的决策具有重要意义。局限性可能在于其理论模型的普适性，以及在实际复杂情境中如何准确识别和利用“信号”的挑战。
motivation: 无法沟通的团队受限于每个成员的个体认知，本文旨在展示其对手如何提供关键信息，帮助团队了解自身。
method: 本文采用理论建模方法，包括一个已解决的高斯模型和有限博弈中的精确测试，来分析团队如何从对手的反应中获取信息。
results: 对手的一个“信号”可以起到每个成员传递信息的作用。当对手更关心自身目标时，一个有承诺的团队永不失败，并且当对手的利害关系大于撒谎收益时，其表现与完全知情的团队一样好。在此之下，团队通过更少信任学习更多。在高斯模型中，通过承诺不完全使用信息来获取真相，并保留对手为隐藏信息所支付的成本。团队如何分配信任也很重要。两个可互换且反应不同的成员可以替代一个拥有完全支持先验的单独不知情成员，并且对信任的小幅折价可以防止误判敌人。
conclusion: 信息不仅仅是收集或聚合的；它是通过团队承诺如何响应而产生的。

title: Stochastic Minimum Spanning Tree Identification with Binary Weights
authors: Haya Diwan, Lisa Hellerstein, Sanjeev Khanna, Junkai Song
abstract: We introduce the Stochastic MST Identification Problem, with binary weights. In this problem, we need to identify a minimum spanning tree (MST) of a graph, each of whose edge weights is either 0 or 1. The weight of each edge $e$ is a random variable which is 1 with probability $p_e$ and 0 with probability $1-p_e$. The probability $p_e$ is given for each edge $e$, but the realized weight of an edge can only be determined by querying the edge. The problem is then to determine a strategy for querying the edges of the graph that minimizes the expected number of queries that need to be performed until we can identify a subset of edges that form an MST of the graph. We address both adaptive and non-adaptive versions of this problem. For the non-adaptive version of our Stochastic MST Identification problem, we give an $O(\log E)$-approximation algorithm via a reduction to submodular ranking. For the adaptive version, we show that solving the problem is trivial when all $p_e$ are equal to 1/2, because of a relation to the Tutte polynomial. However, computing the expected cost of an optimal querying strategy is #P-hard, even when all $p_e$ equal $\frac{1}{2}$. For arbitrary $p_e$ values, we present a constant-factor approximation algorithm for simple planar graphs. We investigate the question of whether the submodular goal value approach of Deshpande et al. could be used to achieve a $\log$-factor approximation algorithm that would work for arbitrary $p_e$ values and general graphs. In this context, we address the structural question of determining optimal submodular goal values for MST identification in graphs.
zh_title: 具有二值权重的随机最小生成树识别
translation: 我们介绍了具有二值权重的随机MST识别问题。在该问题中，我们需要识别一个图的最小生成树（MST），其每条边的权重非0即1。每条边 $e$ 的权重是一个随机变量，其概率 $p_e$ 为1，概率 $1-p_e$ 为0。每条边 $e$ 的概率 $p_e$ 是给定的，但边的实际权重只能通过查询该边来确定。问题在于确定一种图的边查询策略，以最小化在能够识别出构成图MST的边子集之前必须执行的期望查询次数。我们研究了该问题的自适应和非自适应版本。对于随机MST识别问题的非自适应版本，通过归约到次模排序，我们给出了一个 $O(\log E)$ 近似算法。对于自适应版本，我们表明当所有 $p_e$ 都等于 1/2 时，由于与Tutte多项式的关系，问题变得微不足道。然而，计算最优查询策略的期望成本是 #P-hard 的，即使所有 $p_e$ 都等于 1/2。对于任意 $p_e$ 值，我们为简单平面图提出了一个常数因子近似算法。我们探讨了Deshpande等人的次模目标值方法是否可用于实现适用于任意 $p_e$ 值和一般图的 $\log$ 因子近似算法。在此背景下，我们探讨了确定图MST识别的最优次模目标值的结构性问题。
tldr: 本文研究了通过最小化边查询次数来识别随机二值权重图的最小生成树问题，并针对不同图结构和策略提出了相应的近似算法与复杂度结论。
ai_comments: 该论文首次研究了带有二值权重的随机最小生成树识别问题，兼顾了自适应与非自适应策略，并给出了针对不同图结构的近似算法和复杂度结果，具有较高的理论创新性。
motivation: 在边权重为随机二值变量的情况下，如何设计一种边查询策略，以最小化识别图的最小生成树所需的期望查询次数。
method: 通过将非自适应版本归约到次模排序（submodular ranking）来设计$O(\log E)$近似算法；对于自适应版本，利用与Tutte多项式的关系分析等概率情况，并为简单平面图设计了常数因子近似算法。
results: 对于非自适应版本提出了$O(\log E)$近似算法；证明了当所有$p_e = 1/2$时计算最优期望代价是#P-hard的；对于任意$p_e$值的简单平面图，提出了常数因子近似算法。
conclusion: 论文成功建立了随机MST识别问题的理论框架，给出了非自适应版本的$O(\log E)$近似算法以及针对平面图的常数因子近似算法，并指出了计算最优查询策略期望代价的#P-hard难度。

title: Structural Exposure and Subsequent Neighborhood Stability in Temporal Networks: Evidence and Limits of Generalizability
authors: Mehmet Simsek
abstract: Can temporal path based structural exposure serve as a reliable indicator of subsequent local neighborhood stability across different temporal networks? We investigate this question using the completed observational results from 12 networks spanning face to face nteraction, communication, online activity, and urban mobility. Exposure aggregates source node structural mass along time respecting paths; the outcome is Jaccard neighborhood turnover between later, nonoverlapping windows, with greater turnover indicating lower stability. Six complementary analyses examine the direction and consistency of exposure-turnover associations, proximity to high mass nodes, functional response shapes, distance decay kernels, alternative mass definitions, and temporally ordered changes in source mass. The evidence is heterogeneous rather than uniformly negative or positive. In the primary association analysis, two networks retained positive coefficients after within question false discovery rate adjustment, indicating lower subsequent stability at higher exposure, whereas no negative association survived that adjustment. The pooled proximity coefficient was not distinguishable from zero, and significant mass change associations appeared in opposite directions across networks. More flexible functional, kernel, and mass choices yielded only modest cross validated improvements over simpler comparators; available temporal randomizations also gave model dependent contrasts. The study therefore does not establish structural exposure as a directionally consistent, network independent stability indicator. It also cannot establish a lack of predictive value relative to a no exposure baseline, because that specific comparison and independent cross network validation were unavailable. Incomplete null simulations, unrecorded covariance estimation fallbacks constrain inference.
zh_title: 时序网络中的结构暴露与后续邻居稳定性：泛化性的证据与局限性
translation: 基于时序路径的结构暴露能否作为跨不同时序网络的后续局部邻居稳定性的可靠指标？我们利用涵盖面对面互动、通信、在线活动和城市移动的12个网络的完整观测结果来研究这个问题。暴露沿着遵循时间路径聚合了源节点的结构质量；结果是后来、不重叠窗口之间的雅卡尔（Jaccard）邻居周转率，周转率越大表明稳定性越低。六项互补分析检验了暴露-周转关联的方向和一致性、与高质量节点的邻近度、功能响应形状、距离衰减核、替代质量定义以及源质量的时序有序变化。证据是异质性的，而非完全消极或积极。在主要的关联分析中，经过错误发现率调整后，两个网络保持了正系数，表明在较高暴露下随后的稳定性较低，而没有负相关性在该调整中存活。汇聚的邻近度系数与零没有区别，显著的质量变化关联在不同网络中表现出相反的方向。更灵活的功能、核和质量选择与更简单的比较器相比，仅在交叉验证中带来了适度的改进；可用的时序随机化也给出了依赖于模型的对比。因此，该研究并未将结构暴露确立为方向一致、独立于网络的稳定性指标。相对于无暴露基线，它也不能确定缺乏预测价值，因为该特定比较和独立的跨网络验证不可用。不完整的零模拟、未记录的协方差估计回退限制了推断。
tldr: 该论文研究发现，基于时序路径的结构暴露无法作为跨不同时序网络的、方向一致且独立于网络的局部邻居稳定性可靠预测指标，其表现出高度的异质性。
ai_comments: 该论文探讨了时序网络中基于时序路径的结构暴露对后续邻居稳定性的预测能力。创新之处在于利用了12个跨领域的真实时序网络进行大规模实证检验，并进行了多维度的稳健性分析；局限性在于结果呈现高度异质性，未能确立结构暴露作为通用、方向一致的稳定性指标的有效性。
motivation: 探讨基于时序路径的结构暴露是否可以作为跨不同时序网络的后续局部邻居稳定性的可靠指标，并检验其泛化性与局限性。
method: 利用覆盖面对面互动、通信、在线活动和城市移动的12个完整观测时序网络，通过六项互补分析（包括暴露-周转关联的方向和一致性、高质量节点邻近度、函数响应形状、距离衰减核、替代质量定义以及源质量的时序有序变化），系统考察结构暴露与后续邻居周转之间的关系。
results: 证据呈现异质性：在主关联分析中，仅有2个网络在校正后保持正相关（高暴露对应较低稳定性），未发现经校正的负相关；汇聚的邻近度系数与零无异；显著的质量变化关联在不同网络间呈现相反方向；更灵活的函数、核和质量选择仅带来 modest 的改进。
conclusion: 结构暴露不能作为跨时序网络、方向一致且独立于网络的局部邻居稳定性通用指标，其预测表现出高度的异质性和局限性。

title: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources
authors: Maciej Skorski
abstract: Estimating biased finite-memory sources from a single trajectory is a fundamental problem with practical impact, for example in estimating entropy for cryptography. We study order-$d$ binary sources whose conditional probabilities have bias at most $ε$, and establish *sharp* sample complexity bounds: relative accuracy $γ$ with confidence $1-δ$ needs $γ^{-2}\,(\tfrac12-ε)^{-d}\,(\log d+\log\tfrac1δ)$ samples up to constants depending on $ε$, with matching upper and lower bounds and no dependence on mixing time or spectral gap. The proof rests on a sharp bound on expected hitting times of the sliding-window (de Bruijn) chain, which stay of order $1/π(w)$ uniformly in $d$ exactly when $ε<\tfrac3{10}$, and on majorization of the window masses by those of independent biased coins. Applied to published entropy-source validations, the bounds show that their trace lengths may be underpowered: $10^6$ bits cannot resolve all transitions of an $8$-bit model to better than about $4.5\%$ relative error.
zh_title: 学习有限记忆二元信源
translation: 从单个轨迹估计有偏的有限记忆信源是一个基本问题，在密码学中的熵估计等领域具有实际影响。我们研究了条件概率偏差至多为 $\varepsilon$ 的 $d$ 阶二元信源，并建立了*尖锐的*样本复杂度界限：在依赖于 $\varepsilon$ 的常数范围内，达到相对精度 $\gamma$ 且置信度为 $1-\delta$ 需要 $\gamma^{-2}\,(\frac12-\varepsilon)^{-d}\,(\log d+\log\frac1\delta)$ 个样本，该界限具有匹配的上下界，且不依赖于混合时间或谱隙。该证明基于对滑动窗口（de Bruijn）链的期望命中时间的尖锐界限（当 $\varepsilon<\frac3{10}$ 时，在 $d$ 上一致地保持在 $1/\pi(w)$ 的阶数），以及通过独立偏置硬币对窗口质量的主导性分析。将其应用于已发布的熵源验证中，这些界限表明它们的轨迹长度可能不足：$10^6$ 比特无法将一个 8 比特模型的转换解析到优于大约 $4.5\%$ 的相对误差。
tldr: 本文为有限记忆二元信源的估计推导出了精确的样本复杂度界限，证明其不依赖混合时间或谱隙，并对密码学中的熵源验证提出了重要修正。
ai_comments: 该论文在有限记忆二元信源估计领域取得了理论上的突破，给出了精确的样本复杂度上下界，摆脱了对混合时间和谱隙的依赖，并在密码学熵源验证的实际应用中指出了现有方法的潜在不足。
motivation: 从单个轨迹估计有偏的有限记忆信源是一个基础问题，在密码学熵估计等领域具有实际影响，现有的估计方法和理论界限需要得到精确的样本复杂度分析。
method: 通过建立滑动窗口（de Bruijn）链期望命中时间的精确界限（在$ε<\frac{3}{10}$时保持在$1/\pi(w)$量级），以及利用独立偏置硬币对窗口质量进行主导性分析来证明样本复杂度界限。
results: 推导出了具有匹配上下界的尖锐样本复杂度界限，即在置信度$1-\delta$下达到相对精度$\gamma$需要 $\gamma^{-2}(\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon)^{-d}(\log d + \log\frac{1}{\delta})$ 级别的样本量，且该界限不依赖于混合时间或谱隙；同时指出发布的一些熵源验证中样本长度可能不足（例如$10^6$比特无法将8比特模型的相对误差解析到优于4.5%）。
conclusion: 本文建立了阶为$d$的二元信源估计的精确样本复杂度界限，证明了其与混合时间和谱隙无关，并通过滑动窗口链的期望到达时间及主导性证明了该理论，同时对密码学熵源验证提出了实践警示。

title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation
authors: Haaris Mian, Miles Cranmer, Alessandro Favero, Payel Mukhopadhyay
abstract: Scientific foundation models (SciFMs) have achieved remarkable performance on a wide range of PDEs, including the ability to efficiently adapt to unseen data distributions with additional finetuning. As with all neural architectures, finetuning such models comes with the risk of catastrophic forgetting, whereby adapting to new tasks degrades prior knowledge of the model. We study catastrophic forgetting in Walrus-1.3B, a SciFM for continuum dynamics, over the course of a two-stage sim-to-real adaptation: first finetuning on simulated flow around a cylinder and then adapting to experimental data of the same system. We find that finetuning on the simulations rapidly degrades rollout performance on the original pretraining datasets, with one-step errors increasing up to 35x after just 20 epochs. Subsequent adaptation to real data further erodes performance on the simulated task. We characterize the potential drivers of forgetting, such as dataset dependence and task representation similarity. We then show that replaying as little as 1% simulated data during real-data finetuning recovers most of the lost simulation performance while retaining effective adaptation to the experimental dynamics. Our results identify catastrophic forgetting as a practical obstacle to sim-to-real adaptation of SciFMs and show that lightweight replay strategies significantly improve retention.
comment: Accepted at the Sim2Science workshop, NeurIPS 2026. Code: https://github.com/haarisamian/walrus-forgetting-paper
zh_title: 时间冻结：物理基础模型在模拟到现实适应中如何遗忘
translation: 科学基础模型（SciFMs）在广泛的偏微分方程（PDEs）上取得了卓越的性能，包括能够通过额外的微调有效地适应未见过的数据分布。与所有神经网络架构一样，微调此类模型存在灾难性遗忘的风险，即适应新任务会降低模型的先验知识。我们研究了Walrus-1.3B（一个用于连续介质动力学的SciFM）在两阶段模拟到现实（sim-to-real）适应过程中的灾难性遗忘：首先在绕圆柱流动的模拟数据上进行微调，然后适应相同系统的实验数据。我们发现，在模拟数据上进行微调会迅速降低原始预训练数据集上的rollout性能，仅20个epoch后一步误差就增加了高达35倍。随后适应真实数据进一步侵蚀了模拟任务上的性能。我们表征了遗忘的潜在驱动因素，例如数据集依赖性和任务表示相似性。然后我们展示，在真实数据微调期间回放仅1%的模拟数据，可以恢复大部分丢失的模拟性能，同时保持对实验动力学的有效适应。我们的结果表明，灾难性遗忘是SciFM进行模拟到现实适应的一个实际障碍，并且轻量级回放策略显著提高了知识保留。
tldr: 科学基础模型（SciFMs）在模拟到现实（sim-to-real）适应中存在灾难性遗忘，表现为在模拟数据上微调后，模型在原始预训练数据集上的性能急剧下降。研究发现，通过在真实数据微调期间回放少量模拟数据，可以有效缓解遗忘并保持对实验数据的适应能力。
ai_comments: 这篇论文揭示了科学基础模型在实际应用中，尤其是在从模拟环境过渡到真实环境时，面临的一个关键挑战：灾难性遗忘。其创新之处在于不仅识别了这一问题，还通过实验量化了遗忘的严重性（一步误差增加35倍），并提出了一个简单而有效的解决方案——轻量级数据回放。这种方法对于确保SciFM在复杂科学和工程领域中的长期适用性和鲁棒性具有重要意义，尤其是在数据获取成本高昂或模型需要持续适应新环境的场景下。
motivation: 科学基础模型（SciFMs）在偏微分方程（PDEs）上表现出色，并能通过微调适应新数据分布。然而，微调可能导致灾难性遗忘，即模型在适应新任务时会失去先前的知识。本文旨在研究SciFMs在两阶段模拟到现实适应过程中如何发生灾难性遗忘。
method: 研究对象为Walrus-1.3B（一个用于连续介质动力学的SciFM）。研究采用两阶段模拟到现实适应：首先在绕圆柱流动的模拟数据上进行微调，然后适应相同系统的实验数据。研究表征了遗忘的潜在驱动因素（如数据集依赖性和任务表示相似性），并测试了在真实数据微调期间回放少量（1%）模拟数据对缓解遗忘的效果。
results: 在模拟数据上微调后，模型在原始预训练数据集上的rollout性能迅速下降，仅20个epoch后一步误差增加了高达35倍。随后适应真实数据进一步侵蚀了模拟任务上的性能。然而，在真实数据微调期间回放仅1%的模拟数据，可以恢复大部分丢失的模拟性能，同时保持对实验动力学的有效适应。
conclusion: 灾难性遗忘是科学基础模型（SciFMs）进行模拟到现实（sim-to-real）适应的一个实际障碍。轻量级的数据回放策略可以显著改善模型知识的保留。

title: FARO: Function-Space Adaptive Return-to-Risk Optimization via Cross-Block Equal-Risk-Contribution Budget Allocation
authors: Xiaojun Wu, Cehao Yang, Xuhui Jiang, Chengjin Xu, Jia Li, Jian Guo
abstract: Training a large language model is compute-bound, and current recipes divide the work between optimizers by hand: orthogonalized momentum for attention and MLP matrices, Adam-style updates for the rest. This division rests on human priors about which layer type deserves which geometry, and it fixes a single global update budget that every parameter block shares. We introduce FARO, a function-space adaptive optimizer that makes the partition of parameters into blocks the unit of decision. FARO gives each block a geometry by its realized counterfactual return, then freezes the routes and reallocates the frozen per-block budget by cross-block equal risk contribution (ERC), the risk-parity principle from portfolio theory. On a GPT-style model trained on FineWeb, the framework gives two results. First, its FARO-Adaptive arm reaches 3.2780 nats at the full schedule, matching NorMuonAndAdam (3.2794), the best hand-designed recipe: it recovers the human prior without hand-setting per-layer geometry. Second, FARO-ERC improves on that arm: it lowers the clean-data loss at every one of 6 seeds, by 0.0136 nats on average, a modest but robust gain. Its sign test, paired test, and confidence interval all agree, and it exceeds the measured run-to-run noise at no added time or memory. It works by trimming the riskiest blocks rather than expanding the safest, and it holds up under a corrupted stream, still lowering the mean loss and winning the seed majority. The source code is available at https://github.com/wxj630/FARO.
zh_title: FARO：基于跨块等风险贡献预算分配的函数空间自适应风险收益优化
translation: 训练大型语言模型受到计算资源的限制，而当前的训练方案通常依赖人工在优化器之间分工：对注意力和MLP矩阵使用正交化动量，其余部分使用Adam风格的更新。这种划分依赖于关于哪种层类型适宜何种几何结构的人类先验，并固定了所有参数块共享的单一全局更新预算。我们提出了FARO，这是一种函数空间自适应优化器，它将参数划分为块作为决策单元。FARO根据每个参数块实现的逆事实回报为其赋予特定的几何构型，随后冻结选择路径，并利用投资组合理论中的风险平价原则——跨块等风险贡献（ERC）来重新分配冻结的块级预算。在FineWeb上训练的GPT风格模型中，该框架展现了两项成果：首先，其FARO-Adaptive分支在完整调度下达到了3.2780 nats，与最佳人工设计配方NorMuonAndAdam（3.2794 nats）相匹配，在无需手动设置逐层几何的情况下复现了人类先验；其次，FARO-ERC在Adaptive分支的基础上进一步提升：在全部6个随机种子下均降低了干净数据的损失，平均降低0.0136 nats，取得了温和但稳健的提升。符号检验、配对检验和置信区间均一致支持这一结果，且在不增加时间或显存的情况下超过了实测的运行间噪声。其作用机制在于修剪风险最高的块而非扩大最安全的块，并且在受损数据流下依然有效，仍能降低平均损失并在多数随机种子中保持优势。源代码可在 https://github.com/wxj630/FARO 获取。
tldr: FARO借鉴投资组合的风险平价原则，通过自适应选择参数块几何结构并按等风险贡献重分配更新预算，在不增加时间和显存开销的前提下实现了优于手工设计优化方案的稳健性能。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地将金融投资组合理论中的等风险贡献（ERC/风险平价）原则引入大语言模型优化中，摆脱了以往依赖人工先验为不同层手工分配优化器几何构型及共享全局预算的限制。其机制通过裁剪高风险参数块的更新预算来实现稳健提升，且不引入额外的运行时间和显存开销，展示了函数空间自适应优化与跨学科理论结合的潜力。
motivation: 当前大语言模型训练通常依赖人工先验为不同网络层手动划分优化器（如注意力/MLP层使用正交化动量，其余使用Adam），且所有参数块共用一个固定的全局更新预算，缺乏自适应性与合理的预算分配机制。
method: 提出FARO优化框架：以参数块为决策单元，根据各参数块实现的逆事实回报为其自适应分配优化几何；随后冻结选择路径，并利用投资组合理论中的跨块等风险贡献（ERC，风险平价原则）重新分配各块的更新预算，通过裁剪高风险块而非盲目扩大低风险块来优化更新。
results: 在FineWeb上训练的GPT风格模型上：1）FARO-Adaptive达到3.2780 nats，媲美最佳手工设计方案NorMuonAndAdam（3.2794 nats），自动复现了人类先验；2）FARO-ERC在6个随机种子下均超越FARO-Adaptive，平均降低0.0136 nats的损失，具有显著统计意义且不增加计算和显存成本；3）在受损数据流测试中同样保持优势。
conclusion: FARO成功证明了无需人工指定层级几何即可自适应恢复优秀优化配置，并通过等风险贡献预算重分配在不增加时间和显存开销的情况下实现了稳定、稳健的模型性能增益。

title: ProdCrawl: A Replayable Test Collection for Focused Crawling
authors: Manuel Rey-Escobar, David Otero, Javier Parapar
abstract: A focused crawler searches for web pages on a specific topic under a constrained download budget. Since it can only fetch a limited number of pages, its success depends on choosing which links to follow. Focused crawlers are usually evaluated on live websites by harvest rate, the fraction of downloaded pages that are relevant. This has two problems: on the one hand, websites change over time, so a crawl cannot be repeated under the same conditions; on the other hand, there is no ground truth for which pages are relevant. As a result, comparisons between crawlers are unreliable. We present ProdCrawl, a replayable test collection for focused crawling. It comprises static mirrors of 621 company and organization websites, about 1.1 million pages, with each page labeled as a product page or non-product page based on a majority vote among three large language models. Any crawler can be run on exactly the same sites and scored against the same labels. We use ProdCrawl to compare simple baselines (breadth-first, depth-first and text classifiers) with an approach that scores each link by searching for similar link texts whose target pages have already been labeled. Our results show that text classifiers and keyword matching do not significantly outperform breadth-first crawling, whereas neural embeddings, which compare link texts by semantic meaning, outperform all simple strategies. Because every run evaluates over identical pages and labels, these results are exactly reproducible. The collection, codebase, and models are publicly released to support experimental replication and fair crawler comparison.
zh_title: ProdCrawl：一个用于聚焦爬虫的可重放测试集合
translation: 聚焦爬虫在受下载预算限制的情况下搜索特定主题的网页。由于只能获取有限的页面，其成功取决于选择哪些链接进行跟踪。聚焦爬虫通常在实时网站上通过收获率（下载页面的相关性比例）进行评估。这带来两个问题：一方面，网站随时间变化，因此爬虫无法在相同条件下重复；另一方面，哪些页面是相关的缺乏地面真实标签。因此，爬虫之间的比较是不可靠的。我们提出了ProdCrawl，这是一个用于聚焦爬虫的可重放测试集合。它包含621个公司和组织网站的静态镜像，约110万个页面，每个页面根据三个大语言模型的多数投票标记为产品页面或非产品页面。任何爬虫都可以在完全相同的网站上运行，并根据相同的标签进行打分。我们使用ProdCrawl将简单的基准（广度优先、深度优先和文本分类器）与一种通过搜索目标页面已被标记的相似链接文本来对每个链接打分的方法进行了比较。我们的结果表明，文本分类器和关键词匹配并没有显著优于广度优先爬虫，而通过语义相似性比较链接文本的神经嵌入方法则优于所有简单策略。由于每次运行都在相同的页面和标签上进行评估，这些结果是完全可复现的。该集合、代码库和模型已公开发布，以支持实验复制和公平的爬虫比较。
tldr: ProdCrawl是一个基于大语言模型标注的静态网页测试集，解决了传统聚焦爬虫评估不可靠和无法复现的问题，并证明了神经嵌入方法在聚焦爬虫中的有效性。
ai_comments: 该论文针对聚焦爬虫评估中长期存在的实时网页变动快、缺乏明确地面真实标签（ground truth）导致评估不可靠的问题，推出了ProdCrawl数据集。通过利用大语言模型自动标注静态网页镜像，实现了完全可复现的聚焦爬虫评测，对推进该领域的研究具有重要意义。
motivation: 传统的聚焦爬虫评估依赖于实时网站，存在网站内容随时间变化无法重复、缺乏相关页面地面真实标签（ground truth）等问题，导致爬虫之间的比较不可靠。
method: 构建了包含621个公司和组织网站（约110万个页面）的静态镜像集合，利用三个大语言模型的多数投票机制为每个页面标注是否为产品页面，并在此集合上测试了包括广度优先、深度优先、文本分类器以及神经嵌入在内的多种爬虫策略。
results: 实验表明，文本分类器和关键词匹配的表现并未显著优于广度优先爬虫，而基于语义嵌入的方法表现最佳，且所有评估结果均可在相同页面和标签下实现完全可复现。
conclusion: ProdCrawl作为一个可重放的测试集合，有效解决了聚焦爬虫评估不可靠的问题，并通过基准实验证明了基于神经嵌入的语义匹配策略在聚焦爬虫中的优越性。

title: The Generative Gap Between Speculative Drafter and Continuous Diffusion Language Model
authors: Yujian Chen, Hao Jiang, Guang Cheng, Weijian Luo, Tianyang Hu
abstract: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) and speculative drafters offer efficient language generation but are typically evaluated differently: CDLMs generate independently through iterative refinement, whereas drafters propose text for target-model verification and correction. We compare their architectures without verification, using LangFlow for CDLMs and adapting DSpark's Markov and recurrent-head architectures for standalone generation. All models are trained from scratch for unconditional, single-block OpenWebText generation at lengths 16, 128, and 1024, without target features or verification, using common preprocessing, backbone dimensions, and training-update budgets. We evaluate generation perplexity (GenPPL) with an external language model and distributional similarity to reference text with MAUVE. With default denoising steps equal to sequence length, LangFlow outperforms both DSpark variants on both metrics at lengths 128 and 1024, while DSpark-RNN leads at 16. A conditional KL analysis characterizes dependencies excluded by the Markov head's previous-token conditioning. Recurrent memory removes this restriction and improves both metrics, but the longer-sequence gap persists. Teacher probability matching further lowers Markov GenPPL without observed MAUVE gains. Increasing LangFlow's denoising steps at fixed weights improves both metrics at lengths 16 and 128, changing the length-128 ordering relative to DSpark-RNN. These results establish LangFlow's longer-sequence advantage under the evaluated budgets and highlight iterative full-sequence refinement as a route to improving standalone generation beyond gains from recurrent head memory.
zh_title: 推理草稿器与连续扩散语言模型之间的生成差距
translation: 连续扩散语言模型（CDLMs）和推测草稿器都能提供高效的语言生成，但它们的评估方式通常不同：CDLMs通过迭代细化独立生成，而草稿器则提出文本供目标模型验证和修正。我们比较了它们在没有验证情况下的架构，CDLMs使用LangFlow，并改编了DSpark的马尔可夫和循环头架构用于独立生成。所有模型都从头开始训练，用于无条件、单块OpenWebText生成，长度分别为16、128和1024，不使用目标特征或验证，采用共同的预处理、骨干维度和训练更新预算。我们使用外部语言模型评估生成困惑度（GenPPL），并使用MAUVE评估与参考文本的分布相似度。在默认去噪步长等于序列长度的情况下，LangFlow在128和1024长度上在两项指标上均优于两种DSpark变体，而DSpark-RNN在16长度上领先。条件KL分析表征了马尔可夫头的前一词元条件作用所排除的依赖关系。循环记忆消除了这一限制并改善了两项指标，但长序列差距依然存在。教师概率匹配进一步降低了马尔可夫模型的GenPPL，但未观察到MAUVE增益。在固定权重下增加LangFlow的去噪步长可改善16和128长度上的两项指标，改变了128长度上相对于DSpark-RNN的排名。这些结果确立了LangFlow在所评估预算下的长序列优势，并强调迭代式全序列细化是提高独立生成能力的一条途径，其效果超越了循环头记忆带来的提升。
tldr: 本文比较了连续扩散语言模型（CDLMs）LangFlow和推测草稿器DSpark在独立生成任务中的性能。结果显示，LangFlow在较长序列（128和1024）上表现更好，而DSpark-RNN在短序列（16）上领先，强调了迭代式全序列细化对独立生成的重要性。
ai_comments: 这篇论文通过在统一的设置下比较CDLM和推测草稿器，填补了现有评估方法的空白。其创新之处在于将推测草稿器改造为独立的生成模型进行公平对比，并揭示了CDLM在长序列生成方面的潜在优势。研究结果对于理解不同生成模型架构的生成能力边界及其优化方向具有重要意义，特别是强调了迭代式全序列细化在提升生成质量方面的潜力。局限性可能在于其评估仅限于无条件、单块生成，以及特定的数据集和序列长度。
motivation: 连续扩散语言模型（CDLMs）和推测草稿器都能高效生成语言，但它们的评估方式不同。该研究的动机是在没有验证的情况下，比较这两种模型的架构，以理解它们在独立生成任务中的生成能力差距。
method: 研究者在无条件、单块OpenWebText生成任务上，从头开始训练了CDLM（使用LangFlow）和推测草稿器（改编自DSpark的马尔可夫和循环头架构）。模型在长度为16、128和1024的序列上进行训练，不使用目标特征或验证。评估指标为生成困惑度（GenPPL）和与参考文本的分布相似度（MAUVE）。
results:
1. 在默认去噪步长下，LangFlow在128和1024长度上优于两种DSpark变体，而DSpark-RNN在16长度上领先。
2. 循环记忆改善了指标，但长序列差距依然存在。
3. 教师概率匹配降低了马尔可夫模型的GenPPL，但未观察到MAUVE增益。
4. 增加LangFlow的去噪步长可改善16和128长度上的指标，并改变128长度上与DSpark-RNN的排名。
conclusion: LangFlow在评估预算下具有长序列优势。迭代式全序列细化是提高独立生成能力的一条途径，其效果超越了循环头记忆带来的提升。

title: Near-Optimal First-Order Regret for Bandits with Feedback Graphs
authors: Mengxiao Zhang, Yuheng Zhang, Haipeng Luo, Paul Mineiro
abstract: We study first-order regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with a fixed, known directed feedback graph. For strongly observable graphs, [ACBDK15] establishes a minimax regret of $\widetildeΘ(\sqrt{αT})$, where $α$ denotes the independence number of the graph and $T$ denotes the horizon. On the other hand, the best existing first-order bound scales as $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{(κ+1) L^\star})$ [LLZ20], where $κ$ denotes the clique partition number, satisfying $κ+1\geqα$, and $L^\star$ denotes the cumulative loss of the best arm, leaving a gap between the graph dependence in worst-case and first-order guarantees. In this paper, we bridge this gap by obtaining an expected regret bound of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$. Our first result is an algorithm for the special case of self-aware graphs, in which every vertex has a self-loop. The algorithm combines the update of EXP3 [ACBFS02] with a sampling rule inspired by exploration by optimization [LS20]. More specifically, we construct a map whose fixed points yield sampling distributions that control the one-round regret remainder in terms of the learner's loss and the graph's independence number, which is crucial in deriving optimal first-order guarantees. We further show that a sufficiently accurate fixed point can be computed in polynomial time by a geometrically convergent iteration. Finally, we extend the algorithm to general strongly observable graphs and achieve the same $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ guarantee by adapting the two-level aggregation approach of [LLZ20].
zh_title: 带反馈图的老虎机问题的近最优一阶遗憾
translation: 我们研究了具有固定、已知有向反馈图的对抗性多臂老虎机的的一阶遗憾保证。对于强可观测图，[ACBDK15] 建立了 $\widetildeΘ(\sqrt{αT})$ 的极小极大遗憾，其中 $α$ 表示图的独立数，$T$ 表示时间范围。另一方面，现有的最佳一阶界为 $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{(κ+1) L^\star})$ [LLZ20]，其中 $κ$ 表示满足 $κ+1\geqα$ 的团划分数，$L^\star$ 表示最优臂的累积损失，这导致最坏情况与一阶保证中的图依赖性之间存在差距。在本文中，我们通过获得 $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ 的期望遗憾界弥补了这一差距。我们的第一个结果是针对自感知图（其中每个顶点都有一个自循环）的特殊情况的算法。该算法将 EXP3 [ACBFS02] 的更新与受通过优化进行探索 [LS20] 启发的采样规则相结合。更具体地说，我们构造了一个映射，其不动点产生的采样分布可以根据学习者的损失和图的独立数来控制单轮遗憾余项，这对于推导最优一阶保证至关重要。我们进一步证明了可以通过几何收敛迭代在多项式时间内计算出足够精确的不动点。最后，通过采用 [LLZ20] 的两层聚合方法，我们将该算法推广到一般的强可观测图，并实现了相同的 $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ 保证。
tldr: 本文解决了对抗性反馈图老虎机中一阶遗憾界的图依赖差距，提出了达到 $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ 遗憾界的新算法。
ai_comments: 该论文在带反馈图的对抗性多臂老鼠问题中，首次给出了关于图独立数 α 和最优臂累积损失 L* 的近最优一阶遗憾界，弥补了最坏情况与一阶遗憾界之间的图依赖差距，技术上结合了EXP3更新与基于优化的探索采样规则。
motivation: 现有的对抗性带反馈图老虎机的最坏情况遗憾界与一阶遗憾界在图的依赖性上存在差距（最坏情况依赖独立数 α，而现有的一阶界依赖团划分数 κ+1），本文旨在弥补这一理论差距。
method: 提出了一种结合EXP3更新和受“通过优化进行探索”启发的新型采样规则的算法。通过构造固定点映射来控制单轮遗憾余项，并利用两层聚合方法将其扩展到一般强可观测图。
results: 对于强可观测的反馈图，本文算法取得了期望遗憾界为 $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ 的近最优一阶遗憾保证。
conclusion: 本文成功将反馈图中独立数 α 的最坏情况依赖推广到一阶遗憾界中，提出了针对自感知图及一般强可观测图的近最优算法。

title: Dynamic Persuasion: Managing Reputation under Censored Feedback
authors: Ahmet E. Arcaklioglu, Ceyhun Eksin
abstract: We study a long-run sender who repeatedly communicates about a state to a sequence of myopic receivers and whose credibility is a public score updated from past interactions. Receivers face a lemon loss and an opportunity loss, and their behavior depends on these only through a single index, the tolerance. Because the score records only detected misrepresentations, it rests above the sender's true honesty rate; we characterize this credibility premium in closed form. In a fluid limit in which the score adjusts slowly, no policy earns more than operating at a single credibility level, and the sender's gain from managing credibility equals the value of the premium: against receivers who correct for imperfect detection, that gain vanishes.
