The mutual information expansion specialises arbitrary input fading results and gives an explicit remainder. Standard random-coding and second-order achievability tools relate these quantities to reliability over independently faded Alamouti blocks. All alphabets preserve symbol-wise maximum-likelihood detection at the Alamouti level. Numerical energy, mutual information, and error-rate comparisons support the analysis. Centred comparisons with classical Alamouti, Golden, and Silver codes illustrate the trade-off between reliability, symbol rate, and decoding effort.

title: Precision--Recall Trade-off on the Inference Level for LLMs in Grammatical Error Correction
authors: Ryszard Staruch, Filip Graliński
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently been adopted for Grammatical Error Correction (GEC), achieving strong performance via both full fine-tuning and prompt-based approaches. As probabilistic sequence models, LLMs expose inference-time parameters that directly modify token generation behavior; however, their potential for controlling GEC-specific trade-offs has not been systematically studied. In this work, we investigate decoding strategies for grammatical error correction. We show that the repetition penalty parameter enables controllable adjustment of the precision--recall trade-off at inference time, without modifying the model architecture, training procedure, or prompt. Through experiments on standard GEC benchmarks, we demonstrate that repetition-penalty-based decoding enables inference-time control of the precision--recall balance, conceptually related to methods previously proposed for sequence-to-sequence GEC models, such as Align-and-Predict Decoding (APD), while remaining simple and broadly applicable to existing LLMs that expose inference-time decoding penalties.

title: From fleet trajectories to single-cell promises: hierarchically weighted conformal prediction for battery SOH monitoring
authors: Xiangyu Liu
abstract: Interval predictions from conformal prediction are usually read as "90% coverage", but on nested battery data that number promises the fleet average, not the individual cell. We measure the gap on 124 public LFP cells under a preregistered three-tier reporting protocol (fleet, batch, cell): pooled coverage looks healthy (0.875-0.906 across splits) while the worst cell is covered 0.1-2% of the time, with exact binomial tests against the nominal level. We then repair part of the gap with a hierarchically weighted conformal engine whose weights consume only side information frozen at prediction time - signature features, batch labels, cycle indices - and never touch residuals. The preregistered repair criterion passes: 10th-percentile cell coverage moves 0.750 to 0.830 (53% of the gap), the worst cell 0.642 to 0.694, with zero deferrals and a flat sensitivity spectrum. What the engine does not repair is localized rather than left open: under protocol drift the frozen weights harm monotonically on the SOH scale (the absolute scale is reported in full), a structural dead end we report instead of tuning away; and repair capacity is bounded by calibration-pool battery diversity, measured on both datasets. On a cross-chemistry external set the calibrated intervals collapse (0.286), while the within-domain skeleton replicates (pooled 0.933, worst cell 0.686). The deliverable is a reporting protocol - three tiers of promise anchored to measured regimes, worst-cell statistics, deferral share - that makes per-cell interval claims auditable before deployment.

title: TSBPO: Tree-Structured Branching for Policy Optimization in Interactive Language Agents
authors: Rui Yu, Chong Mu, Jinchuan Zhang
abstract: Training interactive language agents from terminal outcomes poses three coupled problems: which task and state continuations to sample, how to assign delayed feedback to decisions, and how to aggregate token losses for multi-token actions. We present TSBPO, a tree-structured sampling-to-update paradigm that addresses these problems within one training loop. A likelihood-fitted Root/Branch allocator uses retained task and state evidence to target continuations likely to produce contrasting terminal outcomes under fixed rollout budgets. On the resulting replayed physical trees, trajectory advantages compare immediate sibling segments, while observation-group step advantages compare outcomes at matched task/observation states. The actor then sums clipped token surrogates over each complete response and normalizes across active turns, avoiding response-length averaging in the policy-gradient term. With a Qwen2.5-1.5B actor, fixed checkpoints obtain 97.79% seen and 96.64% unseen stochastic success on ALFWorld and an 81.07% per-episode success rate over six stochastic episodes for each of the 500 WebShop test goals. A WebShop step-term ablation yields 75.93% at the same update-100 evaluation; an ALFWorld aggregation comparison shows higher observed command validity with complete-turn weighting. These results support the evaluated training configuration on two interactive benchmarks.

title: Provisioning Networks for AI Supercomputers: A Trace-Driven Study of Performance Sensitivity at Unprecedented Scale
authors: Tommaso Bonato, Amirreza Rastegari, Daniele De Sensi, Timo Schneider, Siyuan Shen, Ales Kubicek, Prabhat Ram, Torsten Hoefler
abstract: AI workloads on supercomputers make interconnect performance a primary design constraint. Hardware specifications and microbenchmarks alone do not show how real workloads respond to latency, bandwidth, and jitter. We present a trace-driven study of network sensitivity for training and inference workloads at scales up to 4,096 GPUs. Our methodology combines signature-based trace decomposition with linear programming to make broad network-parameter sweeps feasible. It preserves the recorded NCCL schedules and program dependencies, and estimates a lower bound on runtime under the LogGP model. We validate the compositional analysis against monolithic linear programs, LogGOPSim, and hardware measurements at feasible scales. The resulting latency-bandwidth envelopes identify low-sensitivity regions and performance cliffs that vary substantially across workloads. They also show when bandwidth upgrades provide meaningful returns and when additional network performance has little effect. These results translate execution traces into practical guidance for evaluating network configurations while making the model assumptions explicit.

title: Nereus: A Large-Scale Underwater Dataset for Fine-Grained Attribute Understanding and Grounded Counting Perception
authors: Jingtao Deng, Zihao Jin, Yuehe Chen, Feixiang He, Shuiwang Li, Dan Zeng
abstract: Underwater imagery records rich ecological information and supports applications such as science communication, fishery monitoring, ecological conservation, and oceanographic research. Beyond general scene understanding, these applications require models to recognize fine-grained biological traits and reason over spatially grounded evidence. However, existing underwater datasets often provide coarse category labels, generic captions, or total-count supervision, which limits their use for organism-level analysis and ecological reasoning. We introduce Nereus, a large-scale dataset for Underwater Fine-grained Perception that jointly supports Fine-Grained Object Attribute Understanding and Grounded Counting Perception. Nereus contains 88K images and 2.68M question-answer pairs, including annotations for 136K marine organism objects across 2,690 species and 1,515 genera, as well as 65K point annotations and 67K grounded counting QA pairs. Experiments with representative multimodal models show that Nereus improves downstream adaptation over existing underwater-domain data and provides a foundation for future research on fine-grained marine perception.
comment: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track

title: Flexibility-Aware Robotic Manipulation: Deformation Estimation, Kinematics, and Control via Distributed Inertial Measurement
authors: Amir Hossein Barjini, Sadeq Yaqubi, Pauli Mustalahti, Jouni Mattila
abstract: Flexible robot links challenge the rigid-body assumption, making joint measurements alone insufficient for accurate manipulation. This paper introduces a flexibility-aware manipulation framework that connects structural dynamics directly to sensing, kinematics, and control. Instead of prescribing a dense inertial measurement unit (IMU) network, the dominant vibration modes of each flexible link are first identified from response-convergence and excitation-bandwidth criteria. Under a full-rank modal observability condition, $m$ retained modes require only $m$ independent slope measurements and one reference IMU, defining the minimum observable IMU configuration. The resulting measurements are used to reconstruct the continuous link deformation, which is then incorporated into flexibility-aware forward kinematics and a deformation-informed partial differential equation-based controller. Experiments on hydraulic single- and double-link manipulators evaluate the framework. On the long-reach double-link platform, the proposed kinematics achieves end-effector root mean square errors of $0.0107$~m, $0.0194$~m, and $0.0102$~rad while using fewer sensors than the piecewise-rigid method. Closed-loop reaching experiments further demonstrate real-time integration of IMU-estimated joint states and reconstructed deformation into the proposed controller. The results show that dominant modal information can determine sensing requirements and enable real-time flexibility-aware robotic manipulation.

title: GraphNIAH: A Benchmark for Long-Context Reasoning over Real-World Graphs
authors: Minh-Nam Tran, Abulhair Saparov
abstract: The needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) benchmark was introduced as a test for measuring a model's ability to find small relevant facts within a very large body of input text. However, existing NIAH benchmarks each suffer from one or more of the following limitations: (1) reliance on synthetic data, so their evaluations may not generalize to real-world settings; (2) reuse of previously published datasets, leading to the risk of benchmark contamination; (3) dependence on manual annotation, which requires human effort to create and update data and is prone to future benchmark contamination; and (4) unrealistic simplification of long-context multi-hop reasoning where each next step is trivial given previous steps, while real-world reasoning often requires planning over multiple possible proof paths. To address these limitations, we introduce \Benchmark, a dynamic benchmark built from real citation relationships among scientific papers published after the evaluated models' knowledge cutoff date, which utilizes real-world information while ensuring no benchmark contamination. The fully automated benchmark construction pipeline samples representative subgraphs of the citation graph formed by these papers and converts each subgraph into a long-context QA example with a verifiable answer. We use GraphNIAH to evaluate eight LLMs from the GPT-5.6, Gemini-3, and Qwen3.5 families. We find that accuracy falls as questions require longer reasoning paths: at question depths of 16 and 32, the GPT-5.6 and Qwen3.5 models answer YES/NO questions no better than random guessing, mostly by answering NO; four of the eight models answer no counting example correctly, and the others model get worse as the subgraph size increases. These findings suggest that current LLMs often stop searching the citation relationships in their context before they reach the answer, even though every fact they need is in the context.

title: Ordered Chaos: Towards Adaptive Multipath Load Balancing with Precise Fast Loss Detection
authors: Tommaso Bonato, Ahmad Ghalayini, Nadeen Gebara, Benoit Pit-Claudel, Jiayong Li, Mikhail Khalilov, Luca Piccolboni, Waleed Reda, Pei-Huan Tsai, Tao Ji, Abdul Kabbani, Torsten Hoefler
abstract: Load balancing in best-effort datacenter fabrics faces a tradeoff. Order-preserving schemes such as Equal-Cost Multipath (ECMP) retain loss semantics but use path diversity coarsely, while packet spraying balances load well but removes the ordering signals needed for fast, precise loss detection. We present Ordered Chaos, an end-host design that preserves enough structure for reliable loss detection without giving up fine-grained multipath routing. Reactive Subflow Spraying (RSS) divides each flow into ordered, dynamically routed subflows. Precise Fast Loss Detection (PFLD) combines this ordering with probes to distinguish reordering from congestion, corruption, tail, and retransmission losses within one RTT. Across simulations, AI and HPC workloads, and a DPU prototype, RSS+PFLD improves tail flow completion time by up to $3\times$, eliminates up to 99% of timeout-based recoveries, and accelerates collective and training communication by up to 35%.
comment: To appear in the proceedings of the International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis (SC 2026)

title: Advancing Clinical Trial Outcome Prediction with Domain-Specific Large Language Models
authors: Burak Bakkar, Hana Moalla, Mohamed Salem Jedidi, Haifa Ben Messaoud, Nicolas Lopez Carranza
abstract: Clinical trial failures are a major barrier to efficient drug development, incurring substantial costs and delaying patient access to effective therapies. Structured approaches such as the Hierarchical Interaction Network (HINT) predict trial outcomes by explicitly modelling interactions between drugs, diseases and protocols, but make limited use of the free text in trial registrations. We evaluate two domain-specific language models, BioBERT (108M parameters) and BioMistral (7B parameters), for phase-level outcome prediction on the TOP benchmark (12,477 trials), representing each trial as text built from ten ClinicalTrials.gov fields. We compare fine-tuning (full fine-tuning for BioBERT, low-rank adaptation for BioMistral) with probing, in which the pretrained model is frozen and only a lightweight classifier is trained on its embeddings. On the held-out test set of each phase, all four language-model variants achieved higher ROC-AUC (0.613--0.772) and PR-AUC (0.649--0.901) than the published HINT results, corresponding to relative PR-AUC gains of 10--20\%. F1 differences were small and mixed, and no model, including HINT, clearly exceeded the F1 of a trivial classifier that predicts success for every trial. Under the configurations tested, probing performed comparably to fine-tuning: fine-tuned models scored highest on ROC-AUC and PR-AUC in Phases I and II, and frozen BioMistral embeddings in Phase III (ROC-AUC 0.772; PR-AUC 0.901), although most differences between variants were below 0.03 and were not tested for significance. These results suggest that pretrained biomedical representations already encode signal relevant to trial outcome, and that probing is a computationally cheaper alternative to fine-tuning for this task.

title: Hierarchical Residuals: A Minimalist Decoupling of Residual Width from Compute Width
authors: Ziteng Wang, Jianqiao Lu, Xinyu Ma, Jintao Zhang, Jun Zhu, Yiyuan Ma, Jianfei Chen
abstract: Residual connections underpin Transformers, but they implicitly tie the residual width carried through depth to the compute width used inside each layer. We introduce Hierarchical Residuals (HiRes), a minimalist architectural change that decouples these dimensions, widening the residual state while keeping per-layer compute width fixed. HiRes groups layers into blocks: standard d-dimensional PreNorm layers operate inside each block, while a wider D-dimensional PostNorm outer residual connects blocks. Learned read/write projections bridge the two spaces at block boundaries, leaving individual Transformer layers unchanged. Across different model sizes and depths, HiRes consistently outperforms vanilla residual addition, with fitted scaling laws indicating a 1.30-fold improvement in FLOPs efficiency. On OLMoE-1B-7B pretraining for 500B tokens, HiRes achieves 0.0208 lower training loss and 1.14-point higher downstream accuracy. HiRes is also competitive with other residual expansion methods such as VWN, mHC and AttnRes with less activation memory and I/O costs. Built from only dense projections and normalizations, it requires neither specialized kernels nor infrastructure-level optimizations. HiRes thus exposes residual width as a practical scaling variable using only standard operators.

title: Simple Features Beat Most AI Control Monitors
authors: Shubhrangshu Debsarkar, Valmik Nahata
abstract: AI control relies on monitors to catch a capable model that sabotages its work. These monitors are evaluated on their ability to differentiate honest from backdoored code. We show that on a standard evaluation dataset, simple features beat most monitors without ever running the code, outranking 20 of 24 open-weight models prompted as monitors. The dataset gives its labels away in two ways. People wrote the honest solutions and older language models the backdoors, so the style of the code reveals the class. Additionally, problems that LLMs can backdoor have different characteristics, so basic facts about the problem reveal it too. Swapping one class at a time for code by Claude Sonnet 5 shows that these features reward a contrast between authors, since human code against Sonnet 5's backdoors is easier to separate than the original pairs, 0.95 against 0.79. One in seven backdoors in the standard test set fails our validity checks, which distorts comparisons between attackers. A Sonnet 5 monitor appears to catch 77% of the older models' backdoors but 37% of Sonnet 5's, and 78% against 61% once both are verified. We do not show that published monitors rely on these shortcuts, but our findings suggest that a high score on such a dataset is not by itself evidence of sabotage detection. We release the rebuilt dataset and checks.
comment: 19 pages (5-page main body plus appendix), 7 figures, 10 tables. Accepted at the EvoRobust workshop at NeurIPS 2026. Code and data: https://github.com/ShubsDS/authorship-not-sabotage

title: Numerical analysis of linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem
authors: Tianyang Chu, Mingyan Zhang
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the standard and the mass-lumped linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem. For the standard method, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of the discrete ground state up to sign for sufficiently small mesh sizes, which only requires the $H^1$-convergence of the discrete ground states. For both methods, we establish optimal convergence rates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-norms for $1 \le p < \infty$. Under additional regularity assumptions on the potential, we further obtain an optimal convergence rate in the $W^{1,\infty}$-norm and an almost optimal convergence rate, up to a logarithmic factor, in the $L^\infty$-norm. Moreover, we prove that the discrete ground states superconverge to the Ritz projection of the exact ground state in the $W^{1,p}$-seminorm. The analysis is based on a perturbation argument. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

title: A Fully Polynomial Randomized Approximation Scheme for Hypergraph Unreliability
authors: Zhijie Zheng
abstract:
We give a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for all-terminal unreliability in explicitly represented undirected hypergraphs of arbitrary rank. The algorithm estimates the probability that independent hyperedge failures disconnect the hypergraph, allowing a different rational failure probability for every edge. For a common failure probability, this improves the quasi-polynomial approximation schemes of Cen, Li, and Panigrahi to polynomial time and answers the polynomial-time approximation question reiterated in their subsequent work on graphs.
  The construction turns their representative-survival bound into an importance sampler whose relative second moment is bounded solely in terms of the number of vertices. We protect one randomly chosen representative pair during contraction, correct the path likelihood, and divide by the number of pairs surviving at the end. The resulting unbiased estimator has relative second moment at most $\binom n2$, even when unreliability is exponentially small.
  A minimum-cut normalization makes this estimator implementable with polynomially bounded precision: the residual likelihood becomes a survival probability in an auxiliary absorbing process, which admits rational discretization with a fixed random-bit budget. Logarithmic rate rounding and an exact weighted minimum cut extend the construction to unequal rational failure probabilities. The algorithm's worst-case running time and random-bit usage are polynomial in the input length, the inverse relative error, and $\log(1/δ)$ for confidence $1-δ$.

title: UpLoop: Training Looped Transformers via Upcycling at No Extra Pretraining Compute
authors: Cheng Liang, Tengfei Zhang, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Zhouhan Lin
abstract: Looped language models can strengthen reasoning through repeated computation with shared weights, increasing execution depth without adding independent parameters. However, each additional pass increases training floating-point operations (FLOPs), making these gains more expensive to obtain. To address this cost, we propose UpLoop, a pretraining schedule that uses upcycling to train looped Transformers while exactly matching a standard dense baseline in final parameter count, total training tokens, and training FLOPs. Specifically, UpLoop begins with a shallow Transformer, progressively grows its depth by copying learned layers, and uses the computation saved early to support repeated execution of a shared middle block later in training. Experiments across model scales show improvements in language modeling and downstream performance, with the average score across 22 downstream tasks increasing from 22.99 to 27.52 at 1.3B parameters. These gains also extend to mathematical reasoning after supervised fine-tuning.

title: When Architectural Spaces Start to Act
authors: Alex Binh Vinh Duc Nguyen
abstract: Architectural spaces are increasingly gaining robotic capabilities. Architectural robots such as robotic partitions, ceilings, furniture, facades, and other spatial components can autonomously move and reconfigure in response to occupants' needs and activities. Yet, when architectural robots start shaping the spatial conditions in which people continuously live, work, and interact, we may begin to experience the architectural space itself as robotic. What does this shift mean for how we inhabit such spaces? Drawing on our previous studies, I reflect on how architectural robots interact with people not only through their motions, but also through the spatial configurations that persist after those motions stop; how their actions may benefit some occupants while disadvantaging others; and how multiple robots may together make a whole architectural space appear to act. I argue that as computation gains the capacity to physically reconfigure our environments, interaction extends beyond the moment of computational action into the spatial conditions that people continue to inhabit. Understanding robotic architecture therefore requires us to look beyond short-term human-robot interaction and toward how people inhabit, negotiate, and maintain control over spaces that can autonomously reconfigure.

title: Catalytic space-efficient algorithms for Distance and Determinant
authors: Srijan Chakraborty, Samir Datta, Kushagra Shandilya
abstract:
Catalytic computation reuses potentially large but in-use space (or catalytic space) which must be restored to its initial contents while the clean space is small. This allows all problems in $\mathsf{NL}$ and even larger classes to be in catalytic logspace [Buhrman et al, STOC2014]. In [Chmel et al, CCC2026] the catalytic space for reachability was restricted to sublinear space (specifically, $n \big/ 2^{θ(\sqrt{\log n})}$ space) while remaining in polynomial time. This matches the non-catalytic bounds from [Barnes et al, SICOMP1998].
  We extend the reachability bound to shortest distance, proving a simultaneous sublinear catalytic space and polynomial time bound (henceforth called, sublinear $\mathsf{CLP}$). This is the first simultaneous sublinear space and polynomial time bound for distance even without the catalytic discipline. Moreover, our bound works even for polynomially weighted graphs.
  Along the way we prove simultaneous near linear catalytic space ($\mathcal{O}(n\log^{O(1)}{n})$) and polynomial time bounds for the determinant. We also show some applications to planar matching problems.
  Our starting point was catalytic computation of reachability in directed graphs by [Cook-Pyne, ITCS2026]. [Edenhofer, arXiv:2602.21088] used it to give a tradeoff between catalytic and non-catalytic space, while [Chmel et al, CCC2026] compress the graph to a smaller graph preserving $s,t$-reachability to achieve a smaller space bound. All three can be modified to yield an algorithm for unweighted distance.
  Our contribution is to define an approximation to the walk polynomial in weighted graphs that allows us to infer weighted $s,t$-distance in sublinear $\mathsf{CLP}$. We do so by non-trivially combining elements from each of the above three papers.

title: Leakage-Controlled Structure-Preserving Augmentation and Template-Aware Evaluation for Bangla Symptom-Based Disease Prediction
authors: Sabah Nushra, Shovan Samanta Turzo, Moinul Hossain, Md Kishor Morol
abstract: Bangla symptom-based disease prediction is commonly evaluated on a small, imbalanced structured benchmark containing many profiles that differ by only one or two symptoms. We test whether train-only asymmetric Bernoulli perturbation improves classification using 725 unique profiles spanning 85 diseases and 172 binary symptoms. Experiments use ten repeated real-profile holdouts and parent-grouped inner cross-validation. The 2 x 2 design separates augmentation from hyperparameter tuning, with exact duplication, random oversampling, class weighting, and SMOTEN as balancing controls. For Bernoulli Naive Bayes (BNB), the gain over tuned raw training does not withstand Holm correction, although BNB attains the highest mean accuracy (97.50%). The boosted-tree models benefit substantially: XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost improve by 18.10, 28.45, and 10.09 percentage points, respectively. A Hamming-distance audit places 91.0% of standard held-out profiles within one symptom bit of the training data. Accuracy decreases on a same-disease 1-bit-purged challenge; nevertheless, XGBoost and LightGBM retain large augmentation gains. We also evaluate robustness to missing and spurious symptoms and the faithfulness of BNB explanations. Overall, Bernoulli perturbation is useful for some model families, but benchmark accuracy should be interpreted together with template proximity.

title: From Training Exposure to Membership Evidence: A Controlled Study of OLMo 2
authors: Ali Banaei, Muhammad Shahab Shahzad, Gerald Q. Maguire Jr., Marco Chiesa, Dejan Kostić
abstract: Whether a language model was trained on a document matters for copyright, privacy, and benchmark contamination. Yet most membership-inference (MI) evaluations on language models collect members and non-members after the fact, so success may reflect distribution shift and failure is inconclusive. We re-ran OLMo 2 1B's official 50-billion-token mid-training stage, replacing selected training chunks with documents from 7,814 pairs matched on domain and difficulty. For each pair, a coin flip determined which document was inserted and which was held out. The run released by the Allen Institute for AI (AI2) from the same seed saw identical data everywhere else and serves as the counterfactual. One exposure raises a previously unseen document's likelihood on average but rarely identifies it. Using the counterfactual as reference, the reference ratio has an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.767 but, with one threshold across domains, catches 3.8% of members at a 1% false-positive rate (FPR). In contrast, 13 matched pairs give a paired test 80% power at the 5% level to detect training on a collection, given same-domain non-members and a close reference. A reference trained with another seed recovers 92% of the counterfactual's AUC advantage over chance, whereas reference-free attacks stay within 0.07 of chance when pooled over domains. The full official post-training recipe, re-run on both models, leaves 89% of the average effect. Even with a closely matched reference, substantial document-level variability limits individual membership inference. We will release the checkpoints, per-token log-probabilities, and the evaluation documents; the code is available at https://github.com/ali-bana/OLMo-Twin.

title: SAR-TS-BERT: Physics-Guided Self-Supervised Pre-Training With Polarimetric Features for SAR Time-Series Crop Classification
authors: Jieqiu Wang, Yuhan Zhang, Bo Zheng, Shaoming Zhang
abstract: Multitemporal synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery provides continuous, cloud-free observations of crop phenology for agricultural monitoring in cloudy and rainy regions, yet high-accuracy classification typically requires extensive labeled samples. Although self-supervised pre-training mitigates label dependency in remote sensing, existing frameworks primarily target optical imagery or generic spatial SAR scenes, underutilizing temporal backscatter dynamics and polarimetric scattering mechanisms. We propose SAR-TS-BERT, a physics-guided BERT-style self-supervised pre-training framework for SAR time-series crop classification. SAR-TS-BERT integrates backscatter intensities and polarimetric ratio features (VV, VH, and VV/VH) with dual-polarimetric Cloude-Pottier decomposition parameters ($H/α/A$) into a six-band input representation through two core designs: 1) a physics-guided span masking strategy (SpanPhysics) that adaptively selects contiguous masked spans based on temporal backscatter change rates to prioritize key phenological transitions; and 2) a dual-branch cross-modal fusion encoder that models backscatter and polarimetric decomposition features through separate Transformer branches followed by bidirectional cross-attention fusion. On independent test sets in Estonia (EuroCropsML) and the USA (California CDL), SAR-TS-BERT achieves overall accuracies (OAs) of 96.78% and 87.29%, respectively, and attains a mean monthly OA of 99.37% on Chongming Island, Shanghai. On the Estonia benchmark, pre-training improves OA and Macro F1 by 1.17 and 1.59 percentage points over training from scratch under full supervision, and by 2.58 and 5.19 percentage points using only 1% labeled data. Incorporating SAR scattering physics into temporal self-supervised pre-training effectively enhances crop classification accuracy, parcel-level mapping consistency, and few-shot transferability.
comment: 18 pages, 13 figures, 18 tables. Jieqiu Wang and Yuhan Zhang contributed equally to this work

title: Locality-Controlled Out-of-Distribution Guidance for Robust Regulatory DNA Sequence Design
authors: Dabin Jeong, Marwane Bourdim, Mo Lotfollahi
abstract: Designing regulatory DNA sequences for targeted gene-expression control is an important challenge. Recent approaches frame this task as property-conditioned generation, where diffusion models trained on natural sequences are guided toward high predicted activity through reward-based fine-tuning or sampling-time guidance. We show that single-reward evaluation can obscure reward-hacking behavior. By decomposing evaluation into property, novelty, and plausibility, we identify an empirically underexplored region of the evaluation space in which all three objectives are satisfied, but no existing baseline succeeds. We postulate that this gap arises because prior methods treat guidance primarily as a matter of magnitude. In regulatory DNA, however, sequence grammar is spatially nonuniform: motif positions are sensitive to perturbation, while background regions allow more exploration. We therefore propose LOCOGEN by reformulating guidance as a problem of locality. LOCOGEN learns an invariant motif mask through sequence-level invariance learning to protect motif positions, while applying OOD damping only to background positions. It operates at sampling time on a frozen diffusion backbone, without retraining the backbone. Across HepG2, K562, and SK-N-SH, LOCOGEN reaches this previously underexplored region of the property-novelty-plausibility space. Code is available at https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/LocoGen.

title: Task Vectors Can Be Linearly Decomposed into Interpretable and Controllable Components
authors: Yukiya Horiba, Hakaze Cho, Takahiro Yakoh
abstract: Task Vectors (TVs) provide a compact way to steer large language models, but they are typically treated as atomized directions merely extracted from hidden states, leaving their internal functional structure poorly understood. Motivated by prior work that decomposes in-context learning into Task Recognition (TR) and Task Learning (TL), we ask whether a single TV can likewise be decomposed into functionally meaningful components. We formulate a TR/TL-based decomposition from candidate-label unembeddings, separating each TV into TR, TL, and residual components, and try to optimize the TR and TL coefficients using Bayesian optimization for more effective intervention. We evaluate this formulation across multiple model families, classification tasks, and both instruction- and demonstration-based TVs. Across these settings, TR/TL-based optimization identifies intervention directions that outperform the original TVs. Although optimization over random directions can also improve performance, TR/TL-based search yields more reliable gains, particularly for instruction-based TVs. Moreover, isolated interventions on the decomposed components produce distinct logit-level effects that are consistent with their intended functional roles. Together, these results suggest that TVs are not monolithic steering directions, but can be decomposed into functionally meaningful components that support both interpretation and control.

title: Feasibility of Common-Stream-Only Sensing in ZF-RSMA with Imperfect CSIT
authors: Surya Harsha, Shankar Prakriya
abstract: Reusing the Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) common stream for sensing eliminates dedicated probing signals in Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC), but creates a feasibility bottleneck: the common-power fraction must simultaneously support common decoding, private decoding, and target detection. This paper investigates this tradeoff in downlink zero-forcing RSMA with imperfect channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT) and imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). With the common beam fixed over a sensing dwell through sensing geometry, the common-power fraction becomes the sole design variable. We prove that the communication-feasible set is either a closed interval or empty. Analytical outage expressions localize these endpoints, revealing a high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) floor-ceiling effect: common decoding dictates a common-power floor, while imperfect CSIT and SIC impose a private-decoding ceiling. For sensing, the conditional detection constraint is affine, preserving the interval structure. A geometry-matched common beam ensures monotonic detection improvement, reducing joint-feasibility check to the communication-feasible upper endpoint. Simulations validate our analysis, identifying regimes where common-stream-only sensing is viable.
comment: Accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026. 6 pages, 5 figures

title: Do LLMs Know When They Are Wrong About Molecules? In-Context Property Prediction with Self-Reported Uncertainty
authors: Matthias Busch, Marius Tacke, Tamadur Albaraghtheh, Sviatlana V. Lamaka, Mikhail L. Zheludkevich, Roland C. Aydin, Christian Feiler, Christian J. Cyron
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are used in many domains, but molecular property prediction with them is still little explored. In this work we evaluate the capability of 7 frontier LLMs to predict molecular properties together with a self-reported uncertainty from in-context examples, and compare them with classical baselines trained on the same molecules. We use 4 datasets and screen each for contamination of the training data of the LLMs: three are clean, and the fourth, ESOL, is memorised by most of the models and serves as a comparison. On the clean datasets every LLM improves with the context, at 30 examples the most accurate one beats every baseline. The requested reasoning effort changes accuracy little. The self-reported uncertainty ranks the prediction errors weakly, with Spearman rank correlations of up to 0.46, about the level reached by the uncertainties of the baselines. Combining uncertainty and prediction, on lipophilicity the most certain half of the best LLM is the most accurate at small context sizes; on BACE and antiviral, and on lipophilicity at large context sizes, the best LLMs are on par with the best baseline. On the contaminated ESOL dataset the LLMs show no improvement with the context size, as expected for a memorised dataset, and their stated uncertainty is smaller on the molecules whose value they recall.

title: Search When Needed, Proceed When Reliable: Metacognitive Reliability Supervision for Efficient Agentic Search
authors: Minhao Sun, Zhijing Wu, Xian-Ling Mao
abstract: Efficient agentic search requires large language models (LLMs) to determine whether they can reliably proceed with their current knowledge or need additional external evidence. Supervision based on final-answer correctness or trajectory-level feedback evaluates realized trajectory performance. However, observed trajectory performance is jointly shaped by stochastic generation, retrieval quality, and downstream reasoning. Such signals therefore provide only indirect evidence of how reliable the current decision state was and how retrieved evidence changed its reliability. An effective reward should encourage search when external information is needed and favor searches that contribute to the answer. To this end, we propose a metacognitive framework for training LLMs to make search decisions based on the reliability of their intermediate reasoning states. Our framework estimates the reliability of local conclusions to distinguish whether the current information supports proceeding without search from how much retrieved evidence improves that reliability. The current-state reliability score assesses whether the model can proceed without search. The search-action score measures how retrieved evidence changes estimated reliability. Together, these scores define a reliability-aware process reward for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), providing finer-grained supervision for search and no-search behavior. Experiments across seven question-answering benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves a better accuracy-efficiency trade-off than strong agentic-search baselines. Our code and model checkpoints will be open-sourced.

title: Higher-Order Kinematic Derivatives for Aspect-Preserving Real-Time Numerical Inverse Kinematics
authors: Steffan Lloyd
abstract: This paper leverages the higher-order kinematic derivatives of serial robots to achieve efficient, aspect-preserving real-time inverse kinematics. First, a family of higher-order solvers is derived, with a necessary orientation-error correction map, yielding the QuIK4 and QuIK5 methods with fourth- and fifth-order convergence. Second, an aspect-preserving step limiter extrapolates the Jacobian determinant along the step to predict and avoid singularities, shortening steps only when they head toward a singularity rather than when the current iterate is ill-conditioned. Third, a Hermite-interpolation certifier verifies the aspect of each answer, and a certified restart algorithm recovers failures from proven same-aspect seeds. The proposed methods are shown to outperform prior methods, reducing failures by up to four orders of magnitude and nearly eliminating aspect switching at tracking-level errors. A C++ library is released with ROS 2 integration.
zh_title: 保持构型的实时数值逆运动学的高阶运动学导数
translation: 本文利用串联机器人的高阶运动学导数来实现高效、保持构型的实时逆运动学。首先，推导了一系列带有必要方向误差校正映射的高阶求解器，产生了具有第四阶和第五阶收敛性的QuIK4和QuIK5方法。其次，提出了一种保持构型的步长限制器，沿步长外推雅可比行列式以预测和避免奇异性，仅在趋向奇异性时缩短步长，而不是在当前迭代条件数差时缩短。第三，利用Hermite插值认证器验证每个解的构型，且经证实的同构型种子所设计的 certified restart 算法可恢复失败。实验表明，所提出的方法优于先前的方法，将失败率降低了多达四个数量级，并在追踪级误差下几乎消除了构型切换。同时发布了带有 ROS 2 集成的 C++ 库。
tldr: 本文提出了一种利用高阶运动学导数实现高效、保持构型、实时数值逆运动学的新方法，大幅降低了失败率和构型切换。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地结合了高阶运动学导数、雅可比行列式外推步长限制器以及Hermite插值构型保持认证器，极大地提升了串联机器人实时逆运动学的求解效率、收敛速度和构型保持能力，并开源了C++/ROS 2实现，具有很高的实用价值。
motivation: 传统的实时逆运动学求解器在收敛速度、奇异性处理以及保持机器人运动学构型（aspect）方面存在不足，容易导致失败或构型突变。
method: 首先推导了具有第四和第五阶收敛性的高阶求解器（QuIK4和QuIK5）；其次设计了基于雅可比行列式外推的构型保持步长限制器以预测和避免奇异性；最后通过Hermite插值认证器验证构型，并采用经证实的同构型种子恢复失败。
results: 实验表明，该方法优于先前的方法，将失败率降低了多达四个数量级，并在追踪级误差下几乎消除了构型切换，同时发布了带有ROS 2集成的C++库。
conclusion: 通过利用高阶导数、前瞻性奇异性规避和严格的构型认证，所提出的方法在实时逆运动学中实现了极高的收敛速度和构型保持率，大幅超越现有技术。

title: $W^{1,p}$ error estimates of an IPDG and a class of HDG methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains
authors: Haitao Leng, Weifeng Qiu
abstract: This paper analyzes a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) method, a hybrid mixed DG method, and two representative hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains. For any fixed $ε\in (0,\frac{1}{2})$, we first derive optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates for $2\leq p<\frac{1}ε$ by combining the interface Green's functions developed in \cite{lq2026} with the Fubini-type weighted estimates established in this paper. These error estimates lead to discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability for $2\leq q<\frac{1}ε$, where $q$ is the conjugate number of $p$ such that $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. Using this stability result and a suitably constructed dual problem, we extend the optimal error estimates to $\frac{1}{1-ε}<p<2$ and subsequently establish the corresponding inf-sup stability for $\frac{1}{1-ε}< q<2$. Thus, both optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates and discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability hold throughout the range $\frac{1}{1-ε}<p<\frac{1}ε$, with $q=p/(p-1)$. Note that all of the aforementioned results are free of logarithmic factors and also hold on polyhedral meshes (except for the hybrid mixed DG method). Compared with the conforming finite element method (FEM), establishing such error estimates and inf-sup stability results for DG methods on convex polyhedral domains is more delicate because their analysis involves mesh-dependent norms. Consequently, the operator interpolation theory employed for conforming FEMs cannot be directly applied to DG methods. Finally, a numerical example is presented to illustrate the theoretical results.
zh_title: 凸多面体区域上泊松问题的IPDG方法及一类HDG方法的 $W^{1,p}$ 误差估计
translation: 本文分析了凸多面体区域上泊松问题的一种对称内部惩罚间断有限元（IPDG）方法、一种混合杂化DG方法以及两种具有代表性的可杂化间断有限元（HDG）方法。对于任意固定的 $\varepsilon \in (0, \frac{1}{2})$，我们首先将已有文献开发的界面格林函数与本文建立的Fubini型加权估计相结合，推导出了当 $2 \leq p < \frac{1}{\varepsilon}$ 时的最优离散 $W^{1,p}$ 误差估计。这些误差估计导出了在 $2 \leq q < \frac{1}{\varepsilon}$ 下的离散 $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup 稳定性，其中 $q$ 是 $p$ 的共轭数，满足 $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} = 1$。利用该稳定性结果和一个构造合适的对偶问题，我们将最优误差估计推广到 $\frac{1}{1-\varepsilon} < p < 2$，并随后建立了 $\frac{1}{1-\varepsilon} < q < 2$ 时对应的 inf-sup 稳定性。因此，在整个范围 $\frac{1}{1-\varepsilon} < p < \frac{1}{\varepsilon}$（其中 $q=p/(p-1)$）内，最优离散 $W^{1,p}$ 误差估计和离散 $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup 稳定性均成立。值得注意的是，上述所有结果均不含对数因子，且在多面体网格上也成立（混合杂化DG方法除外）。与协调有限元方法相比，在凸多面体域上为DG方法建立此类误差估计和 inf-sup 稳定性更为精细，因为其分析涉及依赖网格的范数；因此，适用于协调有限元的算子插值理论无法直接应用于DG方法。最后，本文给出了一个数值算例以验证理论结果。
tldr: 本文利用界面格林函数、加权估计和对偶技术，证明了凸多面体域上IPDG和HDG方法在 $\frac{1}{1-\varepsilon}<p<\frac{1}{\varepsilon}$ 范围内无对数因子的最优离散 $W^{1,p}$ 误差估计及 inf-sup 稳定性。
ai_comments: 该论文通过将界面格林函数与Fubini型加权估计相结合，成功克服了不连续有限元（DG）涉及网格依赖范数而无法直接应用传统连续算子插值理论的难点，在凸多面体区域上建立了不含对数因子的最优离散 $W^{1,p}$ 误差估计与 inf-sup 稳定性，成果具有较强的理论创新性和通用性。
motivation: 对于凸多面体域上的泊松问题，由于间断有限元（DG）方法的分析涉及依赖于网格的范数，导致经典协调有限元法所用的算子插值理论无法直接适用，因此在多面体域上建立DG方法的最优 $W^{1,p}$ 误差估计和 inf-sup 稳定性更为困难和精细。
method: 将已有文献建立的界面格林函数与本文提出的Fubini型加权估计相结合，推导 $2\leq p < \frac{1}{\varepsilon}$ 下的误差估计；进而利用所得稳定性及巧妙构造的对偶问题，通过对偶技巧将最优估计和 inf-sup 稳定性推广到 $\frac{1}{1-\varepsilon} < p < 2$ 的范围。
results: 针对对称IPDG、混合杂化DG以及两种代表性HDG方法，在 $\frac{1}{1-\varepsilon} < p < \frac{1}{\varepsilon}$（其中 $q=p/(p-1)$）的整个范围内，证明了最优离散 $W^{1,p}$ 误差估计与离散 $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup 稳定性，所得结果均无对数因子，且对多面体网格适用（混合杂化DG除外），并给出了数值算例验证。
conclusion: 论文成功证明了所考虑的IPDG和HDG方法在凸多面体域及多面体网格上，对于 $p\in (\frac{1}{1-\varepsilon}, \frac{1}{\varepsilon})$ 的整个区间均满足无对数因子的最优离散 $W^{1,p}$ 误差估计和对应的离散 inf-sup 稳定性。

title: Multimodal In-Context Learning with Explicit Rule Induction
authors: Yuquan Li, Xinyang Jiang, Yuhao Xue, Cairong Zhao
abstract: A central challenge in multimodal in-context learning (MICL) arises from tasks that are ill-defined without context and require uncovering the underlying rules from demonstrations. Existing methods predominantly treat MICL as direct input-output mapping, overlooking the importance of explicitly inducing and reasoning over such rules, limiting both performance and interpretability. We propose ERIM, Explicit Rule-Induction for Multimodal In-Context Learning, a unified framework that enhances MICL by explicitly inducing the latent rules governing demonstration samples. Leveraging the reasoning ability of multi-modal large language model (MLLM), ERIM constructs rule-centric MICL datasets, introduces explicit supervision for rule induction, and fine-tunes MLLM to perform explicit rule-induction via a two-stage training strategy that combines mixed cold-start supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments show consistent performance improvements across diverse MICL settings and demonstrate that correctly inducing underlying rules directly leads to stronger and more stable performance.
zh_title: 基于显式规则归纳的多模态上下文学习
translation: 多模态上下文学习（MICL）的一个核心挑战源于那些在没有上下文时定义模糊、需要从演示中揭示潜在规则的任务。现有方法主要将MICL视为直接的输入-输出映射，忽视了显式归纳和推理此类规则的重要性，从而限制了性能和可解释性。我们提出了ERIM（用于多模态上下文学习的显式规则归纳），这是一个统一的框架，通过显式归纳支配演示样本的潜在规则来增强MICL。利用多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的推理能力，ERIM构建了以规则为中心的MICL数据集，引入了规则归纳的显式监督，并通过结合混合冷启动监督微调与强化学习的两阶段训练策略，微调MLLM以执行显式规则归纳。大量实验表明，在各种MICL设置下性能均有一致的提升，并证明了正确归纳底层规则能直接带来更强、更稳定的性能。
tldr: 本文提出了ERIM框架，通过显式规则归纳和两阶段训练策略，显著提升了多模态大语言模型在上下文学习中的性能与可解释性。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地将显式规则归纳引入多模态上下文学习（MICL）中，通过结合监督微调与强化学习的两阶段训练策略，提升了多模态大模型的性能和可解释性。
motivation: 现有的多模态上下文学习（MICL）方法主要将任务视为直接的输入-输出映射，忽视了显式归纳和推理底层规则的重要性，从而限制了模型的性能和可解释性。
method: 提出ERIM框架，构建规则中心的MICL数据集，引入规则归纳的显式监督，并通过混合冷启动监督微调与强化学习相结合的两阶段训练策略对多模态大语言模型进行微调。
results: 广泛的实验表明，ERIM在各种MICL设置下都能带来持续的性能提升，证明了正确归纳底层规则能够直接带来更强、更稳定的性能。
conclusion: ERIM框架通过显式规则归纳有效提升了多模态大模型在上下文学习中的性能与稳定性，为解决定义模糊的多模态任务提供了新途径。

title: Latent-Lens: Visual Perception in Small Language Models Through Latent Communication
authors: Mo Shahdloo, Faegheh Sardari, Mathew Salvaris
abstract: Bridging independent vision-language models (VLMs) and small language models (SLMs) in a modular multi-agent system typically forces them to exchange information as discrete text, which creates a lossy bottleneck for spatial and fine-grained details. This constraint is especially acute for SLMs, whose limited capacity makes them more reliant on the quality of the input signal. Recent latent-communication methods exchange states between language models. How a VLM can pass visual information to a separately pretrained text-only SLM though remains unexplored. We propose \textbf{Latent-Lens}, a lightweight codec that bridges the representation gap between a frozen VLM and a frozen SLM directly in latent space, enabling them to communicate purely through hidden states. The codec consists of a domain encoder that projects hidden states from the VLM into the SLM's embedding space, and an attention decoder formalised as a LoRA that teaches the SLM to attend to these visual prefixes, while training only ${\sim}1.6$M parameters (0.2\% of the combined model size). On visual question answering (CLEVR, GQA), Latent-Lens achieves $81.0\pm7.9$\% and $65.4\pm5.4$\%, compared with $58.3\pm5.7$\% and $61.8\pm1.0$\% for text communication with the same LoRA budget (+30.2--69.8pp relative to frozen text communication), while on image captioning (Flickr8k) it improves over the same baseline by +16.5 (+18.8 frozen). We also evaluate Latent-Lens with TinyLlama-1.1B and InternVL2-1B, which use different architectures, vocabularies, and hidden dimensions.
zh_title: Latent-Lens：通过潜在通信实现小型语言模型的视觉感知
translation: 将独立的视觉-语言模型（VLMs）和小型语言模型（SLMs）桥接在一个模块化多智能体系统中，通常会迫使它们以离散文本形式交换信息，这为空间和细粒度细节带来了有损的瓶颈。这种限制对于容量有限的SLMs来说尤其严重，因为它们更依赖于输入信号的质量。最近的潜在通信方法在语言模型之间交换状态。然而，VLM如何将视觉信息传递给单独预训练的纯文本SLM仍未被探索。我们提出了Latent-Lens，一个轻量级的编解码器，它直接在潜在空间中弥合了冻结VLM和冻结SLM之间的表示差距，使它们能够纯粹通过隐藏状态进行通信。该编解码器由一个域编码器组成，将VLM的隐藏状态投影到SLM的嵌入空间，以及一个注意力解码器，形式化为LoRA，用于训练SLM关注这些视觉前缀，同时仅训练约1.6M参数（占组合模型大小的0.2%）。在视觉问答（CLEVR，GQA）任务上，Latent-Lens实现了81.0±7.9%和65.4±5.4%的性能，与相同LoRA预算下文本通信的58.3±5.7%和61.8±1.0%相比（相对冻结文本通信提升+30.2–69.8pp），而在图像字幕（Flickr8k）任务上，它比相同基线提高了+16.5（冻结模型提高+18.8）。我们还使用TinyLlama-1.1B和InternVL2-1B评估了Latent-Lens，它们使用了不同的架构、词汇和隐藏维度。
tldr: Latent-Lens通过在潜在空间直接通信，使小型语言模型能够感知视觉信息，避免了基于文本的瓶颈，显著提高了性能。
ai_comments: 该论文的创新点在于提出了Latent-Lens，通过直接在潜在空间而非离散文本空间实现冻结VLM和冻结SLM之间的通信。这种方法有效解决了传统文本通信带来的信息损失瓶颈，特别是对资源受限的SLM而言。其核心贡献在于采用轻量级编解码器（域编码器和LoRA形式的注意力解码器），仅需训练极少量参数即可显著提升SLM的视觉感知能力，体现了高效性和模块化设计的优势。
motivation: 在模块化多智能体系统中，独立的视觉-语言模型（VLMs）与小型语言模型（SLMs）之间通过离散文本交换信息会造成空间和细粒度细节的信息丢失瓶颈，这对容量有限的SLMs尤为严重。现有的潜在通信方法未探索VLM如何将视觉信息传递给单独预训练的纯文本SLM。
method: 本文提出了Latent-Lens，一个轻量级的编解码器，它直接在潜在空间中弥合了冻结VLM和冻结SLM之间的表示差距，使它们能够纯粹通过隐藏状态进行通信。该编解码器包含一个域编码器，将VLM的隐藏状态投影到SLM的嵌入空间；以及一个注意力解码器，形式化为LoRA，用于训练SLM关注这些视觉前缀，总共只训练了约1.6M参数（占组合模型大小的0.2%）。
results: 在视觉问答（CLEVR, GQA）任务上，Latent-Lens实现了81.0±7.9%和65.4±5.4%的性能，与相同LoRA预算下文本通信的58.3±5.7%和61.8±1.0%相比有显著提升（相对冻结文本通信提升+30.2–69.8pp）。在图像字幕（Flickr8k）任务上，它比相同基线提高了+16.5（冻结模型提高+18.8）。该方法还通过TinyLlama-1.1B和InternVL2-1B进行了评估，显示其对不同架构、词汇和隐藏维度的适应性。
conclusion: Latent-Lens通过在潜在空间直接实现VLM和SLM的通信，有效地克服了基于文本的信息传递限制，并以极小的训练开销显著增强了SLM的视觉感知能力。

title: Scaly: an Optimizing Compiler for Optimal Control
authors: Tudor A. Oancea, Colin N. Jones
abstract: We present Scaly, an open-source optimizing compiler for optimal control, written in Python, that generates fast C code. Scaly provides a modeling language embedded in Python for the parametric optimization problems that arise in model predictive control and moving horizon estimation, and computes the sparse derivatives that standard optimization solvers need. Scaly accepts general nonlinear programs but applies optimizations specific to optimal control, which preserve the repeated structure of a problem, such as the stages of a horizon, through differentiation down to the generated loops. The generated C depends only on the C math library and never allocates memory dynamically. On three benchmark problems, Scaly evaluates the Hessian of the Lagrangian up to 26 times faster than CasADi, with smaller binaries and build times that stay nearly constant with the horizon. With the same solver, Scaly shortens the solver time per control step on every benchmark, by a factor of up to 9.
zh_title: Scaly：一个用于最优控制的优化编译器
translation: 我们提出了Scaly，一个用Python编写的开源最优控制优化编译器，它能生成快速的C代码。Scaly提供了一个嵌入在Python中的建模语言，用于模型预测控制和移动视界估计中出现的参数优化问题，并计算标准优化求解器所需的稀疏导数。Scaly接受一般的非线性规划，但应用了针对最优控制的特定优化，通过微分将问题的重复结构（例如视界阶段）保留到生成的循环中。生成的C代码仅依赖于C数学库，并且从不动态分配内存。在三个基准问题上，Scaly计算拉格朗日Hessian的速度比CasADi快26倍，生成更小的二进制文件，并且构建时间随视界保持几乎不变。使用相同的求解器，Scaly将每个控制步骤的求解器时间缩短了最多9倍。
tldr: Scaly是一个开源的Python优化编译器，专门用于最优控制，能生成快速的C代码，并在基准测试中显著提升了性能。
ai_comments: Scaly的创新之处在于其专门针对最优控制问题进行优化，通过在编译过程中保留问题的结构（如视界阶段），从而生成高度优化的C代码。这种方法显著提升了计算效率，尤其是在稀疏导数计算和求解器时间方面，使其成为模型预测控制和移动视界估计等应用中一个非常有前景的工具。其不动态分配内存的特点也增强了代码的稳定性和实时性。
motivation: 为了解决模型预测控制和移动视界估计中出现的参数优化问题，并生成快速的C代码来处理这些问题所需的稀疏导数。
method: Scaly是一个用Python编写的开源优化编译器，它提供了一个嵌入在Python中的建模语言，用于最优控制中的参数优化问题。它能计算优化求解器所需的稀疏导数，并接受一般的非线性规划，同时应用针对最优控制的特定优化，通过微分保留问题的重复结构，直至生成的循环。生成的C代码仅依赖于C数学库且不动态分配内存。
results: 在三个基准测试问题上，Scaly计算拉格朗日Hessian的速度比CasADi快26倍，生成更小的二进制文件，并且构建时间随视界保持几乎不变。使用相同的求解器，Scaly将每个控制步骤的求解器时间缩短了最多9倍。
conclusion: Scaly显著提高了最优控制问题的性能，通过专门的优化和高效的C代码生成，实现了比现有工具更快的导数计算和更短的求解时间。

title: CypherGuard: Database-Grounded Correction for Reliable Text-to-Cypher
authors: Zebin Chen, Dong Wen, Makbule Gulcin Ozsoy, Wenjie Zhang
abstract: Text-to-Cypher translates natural-language questions into Cypher queries over property graphs. Graph database systems increasingly adopt this translation as a native query interface. Large language models generate fluent Cypher but stay unreliable. On Cypher-Bench a small model answers only 31.4% of questions correctly, and even a strong model plateaus at 71.76%. The dominant failure modes are structural rather than linguistic. For example, a generated query may parse correctly and follow the schema, yet still return zero rows because it traverses a relationship against the stored graph direction. To address this issue, we present CypherGuard, a training-free framework that detects and corrects these structural faults. Our approach uses two core components: a graph-native error taxonomy to guide repair, and a mined rule library to guide query generation. At inference time, CypherGuard first rewrites schema-detectable faults, then re-executes each draft and repairs it only when the query errors or returns nothing. On CypherBench test questions, across seven graphs, CypherGuard reaches 88.50% overall execution accuracy, +25.08% over the same-backbone zero-shot floor, surpassing an RL-fine-tuned 7B specialist and the strongest training-based system that we compare against.
zh_title: CypherGuard：面向可靠Text-to-Cypher的数据库落地纠错方法
translation: Text-to-Cypher 将自然语言问题转换为属性图上的 Cypher 查询。图数据库系统越来越倾向于采用这种翻译作为原生查询接口。大型语言模型虽然能生成流利的 Cypher，但依然不可靠。在 Cypher-Bench 上，一个小模型只能正确回答 31.4% 的问题，即使是强大的模型也停留在 71.76% 的瓶颈。主要的失败模式是结构性的，而不是语言学的。例如，生成的查询可能解析正确并符合架构，但由于逆着存储的图方向遍历关系，仍然返回零行。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了 CypherGuard，一个检测并纠正这些结构性故障的无训练框架。我们的方法使用两个核心组件：指导修复的图原生错误分类法，以及指导查询生成的挖掘规则库。在推理时，CypherGuard 首先重写模式可检测的故障，然后重新执行每个草稿查询，并且仅在查询出错或返回空结果时才对其进行修复。在 CypherBench 测试问题中，跨越七个图，CypherGuard 的整体执行准确率达到了 88.50%，比同骨干网络的零样本基线提高了 +25.08%，超越了 RL 微调的 7B 专家模型以及我们对比的最强基于训练的系统。
tldr: CypherGuard是一个无需训练的纠错框架，通过图原生错误分类与挖掘规则库解决Text-to-Cypher中的结构性错误，大幅提升了大模型图查询的执行准确率。
ai_comments: CypherGuard提供了一种无需训练、数据库落地的纠错框架，通过结合图原生错误分类法和挖掘规则库，有效解决了Text-to-Cypher中普遍存在的结构性失效问题，显著提升了大模型生成图查询的准确率。
motivation: 大语言模型在将自然语言转换为Cypher查询时虽然流利，但由于存在结构性错误（如违背存储图方向导致返回空行等），导致准确率不可靠且存在瓶颈。
method: 提出CypherGuard框架，包含两个核心组件：用于指导修复的图原生错误分类法和用于指导查询生成的挖掘规则库。在推理阶段重写模式可检测的错误，并在查询出错或返回空结果时进行动态重执行与修复。
results: 在Cypher-Bench的七个图数据库测试中，CypherGuard达到了88.50%的整体执行准确率，比零样本基线提升了25.08%，超越了RL微调的7B模型以及对比的最强训练系统。
conclusion: CypherGuard在无需模型训练的前提下，通过运行时检测、重写与动态重试机制，大幅提升了Text-to-Cypher的执行准确率，超越了多种基于微调或训练的复杂系统。

title: Measuring What Matters: A Causal Reliance Score for Histopathology Image Segmentation
authors: Samuel Thomas, Daniel Tweneboah Anyimadu, Ahmed Karam Eldaly, Somaia Elsheikh, Mohammed M. Abdelsamea
abstract: Reliable histopathology segmentation requires models that rely on pathology-relevant structures rather than spurious background correlations. In this work, we argue that improving architectures alone is insufficient if models continue to rely on spurious correlations rather than pathology-relevant features. We introduce a causality-inspired evaluation framework based on controlled interventions that explicitly probes model sensitivity to foreground tissue structure and background/domain variation. Building on this, we propose the Causal Reliance Score (CRS), a metric that quantifies the relative sensitivity of model predictions to foreground perturbation versus background/domain variation under controlled interventions. To support this analysis, we design augmentation strategies that act as implicit counterfactual interventions during training, encouraging invariance to nuisance factors while preserving morphology. We demonstrate how these interventions reveal behavioural differences between models that are not captured by standard metrics such as Dice or IoU. While we instantiate our framework using a self-supervised transformer (CAUSE-ViT), the primary contribution of this work is not a new architecture, but a principled intervention-based methodology and evaluation metric for auditing model behaviour in medical image segmentation. Our results suggest that evaluating model behaviour through counterfactual interventions is essential for developing reliable and clinically robust medical image segmentation systems.
comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, accepted into Medical Image Understanding and Analysis (MIUA) 2026 conference
zh_title: 测量重要性：一种用于组织病理学图像分割的因果依赖分数
translation: 可靠的组织病理学分割需要模型依赖于病理学相关的结构，而不是虚假的背景关联。在这项工作中，我们认为，如果模型继续依赖虚假关联而非病理学相关特征，仅改进架构是不足够的。我们引入了一个受因果关系启发的评估框架，该框架基于受控干预，明确探测模型对前景组织结构和背景/领域变化的敏感性。在此基础上，我们提出了因果依赖分数（CRS），这是一个量化模型预测在受控干预下对前景扰动与背景/领域变化的相对敏感性的指标。为了支持这项分析，我们设计了在训练期间作为隐式反事实干预的增强策略，鼓励对无关因素的不变性，同时保留形态。我们展示了这些干预措施如何揭示模型之间行为上的差异，而这些差异是Dice或IoU等标准指标无法捕捉到的。虽然我们使用自监督Transformer（CAUSE-ViT）实例化了我们的框架，但这项工作的主要贡献不是一个新的架构，而是一种基于干预的、有原则的方法论和评估指标，用于审计医学图像分割中的模型行为。我们的结果表明，通过反事实干预评估模型行为对于开发可靠且临床鲁棒的医学图像分割系统至关重要。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于因果干预的评估框架和因果依赖分数（CRS），以量化组织病理学图像分割模型对前景组织结构而非背景噪声的敏感性，揭示了标准指标未捕捉到的模型行为差异，并强调了反事实干预对开发可靠医疗图像分割系统的重要性。
ai_comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于它将因果推断引入了医学图像分割模型的评估中，提出了一种新颖的、基于干预的方法论和指标（CRS），来审计模型的行为。它强调了仅仅改进模型架构是不够的，更重要的是要确保模型依赖于正确的、病理学相关的特征，而不是虚假的背景噪声。这对于提高医疗AI的可靠性和临床可信度具有重要意义，因为它能帮助开发者理解模型失败的原因，而不仅仅是观察其性能指标。

title: WorkIng: A Real-World and Synthetic Highway Work-Zone Benchmark Dataset for Autonomous Navigation
authors: Xujun Xie, Dominik Rößle, Adithya Mohan, Daniel Cremers, Torsten Schön
abstract: Highway work zones are critical edge cases for autonomous vehicles (AVs), combining atypical geometries and jurisdiction-specific regulations that existing benchmarks fail to capture: real-world datasets lack 360° multi-modal, full-scene 3D work zone annotation, and no single recorded site can span the layouts and regulatory variants needed for generalizable models. We present WorkIng, a dual-domain benchmark and training resource. WorkIng-Highway provides a 360° multi-modal work zone benchmark with synchronized 128-channel LiDAR, six RGB cameras, and RTK-GPS across 32 km, yielding 12,000+ annotated frames and 227,399 tracked 3D bounding boxes. WorkIng-CARLA complements this with procedural simulation spanning 24 regulation-aware scenarios across six canonical topologies and six international traffic standards, populated by 100+ custom 3D assets. Benchmarking representative 3D detection and end-to-end planning architectures shows that real-world data remains the primary performance driver, and that scenario-stratified synthetic augmentation improves architectures across 2D recognition, 3D detection, and trajectory planning. Resources: https://github.com/cvims/WorkIng

title: MERIDIAN: Memory-Encoded Rituals for Intimacy across Distance in an Interactive, Asynchronous Neighbourhood
authors: Jingyi Chen, Yifan Yang
abstract: How can shared memories become playable structures for partners who live in different time zones? We present MERIDIAN, a pre-deployment design case of Yi Town, a bilingual browser game developed by one member of a long-distance couple as a gift for the other. Nine levels translate personally meaningful events, places and cultural references into tasks within a navigable pixel town. A birthday prologue and a fictional wedding frame the intended experience. Drawing on research through design, we reconstruct four design changes from 109 development commits, 28 changelog versions and three design specifications. These records support six situated design commitments, including memory-derived mechanics, staged access, local progress storage and bilingual coverage. The implementation combines a union-based progress model with manually exchanged, checksummed codes and time-zone-dependent scenery. An implementation audit reproduced 153 passing unit tests and examined all 1,024 canonical progress codes, while identifying limits involving resets, unversioned level registries and residual transcription errors. The application has no author-operated backend for progress, but external media services and browser speech recognition limit its privacy and offline guarantees. No recipient evaluation or relationship outcomes are reported. The contribution is an inspectable account of design decisions and their trade-offs, including the tension between authoring a personal gift and preserving the recipient's freedom to interpret, decline or reshape it. The game is playable at https://jingyifan.love and its source is public at https://github.com/rayford295/yi-town.

title: Characterizations and MacWilliams-Like Identities of Weakly Regular Bent Partitions
authors: Jiaxin Wang, Yadi Wei, Fang-Wei Fu, Jin Li, Fulin Li
abstract: Bent partitions play a significant role in the theory of bent functions. In this paper, we study weakly regular bent partitions, that is, all generated bent functions are weakly regular (called in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$). Let $Γ=\{A_{i}, i \in V_{m}\}$ be a bent partition of $V_{n}$ in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$, where $V_{n}$ denotes an $n$-dimensional vector space over the prime field $\mathbb{F}_{p}$, $n$ is even, $m \leq \frac{n}{2}$, and $m \geq 2$ if $p=2$. We first characterize bent partition $Γ$ in terms of the duals of component functions of vectorial bent functions. In particular, we prove that if $p \neq 3$, then all bent functions generated by $Γ$ are regular. Building on the above result, we give characterizations of bent partition $Γ$ in terms of two classes of linear codes. When $n \geq 4$ and $m=\frac{n}{2}$, except for the case where $(p, n)=(2, 4)$ and $|A_{i_{0}}|=1$ for some $i_{0}$, we show that $Γ$ is obtained from a spread (after a shift). Particularly, any normal bent partition of $V_{n}$ of depth $p^{\frac{n}{2}}$ in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$ must be obtained from a spread (after a shift), where $n \geq 4$. We establish the Macwilliams-like identities for bent partitions in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$. Furthermore, if $p$ is odd, we present some nonexistence results on bent partitions in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$.

title: Stepwise-Querying: Distilling Reasoning without Access to Teacher Chain-of-Thought
authors: Dicong Yu, Wenhua Wang, Tian Wang
abstract: Reasoning distillation is widely used to transfer the reasoning capabilities of large language models to smaller students through teacher-generated supervision. In the black-box setting, however, teachers may expose only final answers and brief solutions, leaving intermediate calculations and validity conditions unavailable and thus limiting the reasoning supervision available for distillation. We propose Stepwise Querying, which elicits step-specific explanations without requiring access to the teacher's internal chain-of-thought (CoT) traces. Independent queries to the same teacher request intermediate derivations, validity checks, and corrections for individual steps, the assembled solutions are then used for standard supervised fine-tuning. Across two teachers, two students, and four mathematics and code benchmarks, our method achieves the highest score in 14 of 16 comparisons with three baselines. We further introduce Stepwise Explanation Information Gain (SEIG), a diagnostic based on the log-ratio of a frozen student's probabilities of correct step completion under stepwise and global explanations. Analyses on GSM8K show that incorrect-answer trajectories can remain useful when they preserve valid intermediate reasoning, while further decomposition yields limited additional gains.

title: Visual-Inertial RGB-D SLAM with Encoders for a Differential Wheeled Robot
authors: Zhanghao Zhu, Yutaka Kaizu, Kenichi Furuhashi, Kenji Imou
abstract: Recent years have seen multiple impressive results in visual-inertial odometry (VIO) techniques, by which accurate state estimation can be achieved via the extended Kalman filter (EKF) or nonlinear optimization. However, these approaches are rarely open source, and they tend to fail in real experiments due to the temporary lack of feature points and fast motion. Therefore, in this study, we used encoders to overcome the temporary failure of purely vision-based simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Here, we propose a generative measurement model for encoders and derive an expression for the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate and necessary Jacobians for optimization. We use our theory to present a novel tightly coupled visual-inertial encoder RGB-Depth (RGB-D) SLAM system. Tests on our system on an in-house dataset confirmed that our modeling effort led to accurate (with a root mean squared error (RMSE) of approximately 2-7 cm) and robust state estimation in real time. The source code and our dataset containing the encoder information have been published for verification.
comment: 11 pages. Author-accepted manuscript of the article published in IEEE Sensors Journal, 2022
zh_title: 面向差速轮式机器人的结合编码器的视觉-惯性RGB-D SLAM
translation: 近年来，视觉惯性里程计（VIO）技术取得了令人瞩目的成果，通过扩展卡尔曼滤波（EKF）或非线性优化可以实现准确的状态估计。然而，这些方法很少开源，并且在实际实验中往往由于临时缺乏特征点和快速运动而失败。因此，在本研究中，我们使用编码器来克服纯视觉同步定位与建图（SLAM）的临时失效问题。在此，我们为编码器提出了一种生成式测量模型，并推导了最大后验（MAP）估计的表达式以及优化所需的雅可比矩阵。我们利用这一理论提出了一种新颖的紧耦合视觉-惯性-编码器RGB-D SLAM系统。在我们自己采集的数据集上的测试证实，我们的建模工作实现了实时、准确（均方根误差（RMSE）约为2-7厘米）且鲁棒的状态估计。包含编码器信息的源代码和数据集已发布以供验证。
tldr: 本文提出了一种结合轮式编码器的紧耦合视觉-惯性RGB-D SLAM系统，有效克服了纯视觉SLAM易失效的缺点，实现了高精度、鲁棒的实时状态估计。
ai_comments: 本文针对差速轮式机器人，创新性地提出了将轮式编码器与视觉、惯导及RGB-D传感器进行紧耦合的SLAM系统。其最大亮点在于提出了一种用于编码器的生成式测量模型并推导了相应的MAP估计与雅可比矩阵，有效解决了纯视觉方法在特征点缺失或快速运动时失效的问题。该开源工作对具身智能和移动机器人定位具有较高的实用价值。
motivation: 现有的视觉惯性里程计（VIO）方法在实际实验中常常因为临时缺乏特征点和快速运动而失效，且大多数相关方法并未开源。为了克服纯视觉SLAM的这些局限性，本研究引入了轮式编码器来提升系统在恶劣条件下的鲁棒性。
method: 提出了一种针对编码器的生成式测量模型，推导了最大后验（MAP）估计及优化所需的雅可比矩阵，并构建了一个紧耦合的视觉-惯性-编码器RGB-D SLAM系统。
results: 在自建数据集上的测试表明，该系统实现了实时、准确且鲁棒的状态估计，均方根误差（RMSE）约为2-7厘米，并且已将源代码和包含编码器信息的数据集公开。
conclusion: 本文成功开发并验证了一个紧耦合的视觉-惯性-编码器RGB-D SLAM系统，通过融合编码器数据克服了纯视觉SLAM的局限性，实现了高精度和鲁棒的实时状态估计。

title: Clinical-Protocol-Aware Cyber Resilience for Connected Clinical Technologies Under AI-Enabled Adversarial Conditions
authors: Pranav Patel, Siva Kannathasan, Prerak Patel, Jigar Patel, Vansh Patel, Sheel Patel
abstract: Healthcare increasingly relies on connected medical devices, clinical information systems, cloud services, and distributed-care technologies, creating cybersecurity risks across clinical workflows. AI-enabled capabilities can accelerate vulnerability discovery and attack-path analysis, increasing the need to limit compromise propagation. This paper proposes a clinical-protocol-aware cyber-resilience framework based on bounded clinical micro-networks and controlled interconnections. The framework integrates clinical factors into cybersecurity design, management, and evaluation, covering prevention, containment, and incident response. A parameterized Monte Carlo simulation distinguishes technical cyber exposure from modeled clinical consequence. Experiments investigate architectural connectivity, adversarial capability, security controls, protocol dependency, risk alignment, communication directionality, lifecycle integration, and response timing. Under the simulation assumptions, connected architecture increases mean cyber exposure by 56.3% relative to segmented architecture, while combined prevention and containment reduce exposure by 60.1% relative to no controls. Increasing protocol dependency raises the modeled clinical-impact index from 1.021 to 7.567 without changing mean cyber exposure, demonstrating that technical exposure and clinical consequence can diverge. Risk-alignment experiments further indicate higher modeled clinical impact when greater technical risk corresponds to greater clinical significance. The findings support comparative architectural analysis, not calibrated estimates of real-world cyber risk, control effectiveness, or patient harm. The framework provides a clinical-context-aware approach to security-boundary design, control prioritization, and coordinated containment in connected healthcare environments.

title: Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention for Robust Face Recognition
authors: Tahar Chettaoui, Guray Ozgur, Eduarda Caldeira, Naser Damer, Fadi Boutros
abstract: Multi-head attention in Vision Transformers (ViTs) allows independent attention patterns across heads, but without explicit regularization, heads may learn redundant patterns rather than complementary roles. Correlation-based penalties encourage head disentanglement, yet apply uniform regularization across all training samples. In face recognition (FR), hard samples whose embeddings lie close to competing identities are critical for optimization and generalization. Motivated by this, we propose ViT-HarDis, which conditions attention head disentanglement on sample difficulty: samples with high cosine similarity to negative class centers receive stronger head decorrelation, enforcing specialization where identity ambiguity is highest. Experiments show improvements over both the baseline and uniform disentanglement on most benchmarks. Our analysis shows that ViT-HarDis reduces the similarity of hard samples to competing class centers while decreasing inter-head attention similarity, and that applying disentanglement only to the final transformer layers outperforms regularizing the entire network. Trained on WebFace4M, ViT-HarDis achieves SOTA results among ViT-based methods on IJB-B, IJB-C, and TinyFace Rank-1, while achieving the best IJB-B and TinyFace results when trained on MS1MV3, improving FR without architectural modifications or additional inference cost. Code: https://github.com/TaharChettaoui/Hard-Sample-Conditioned-Attention-for-FR.
comment: Accepted at the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027)

title: Peeling the Matryoshka: Extracting Ontological Structure from Retrieval Embeddings
authors: Eunchan Kim, Inwhee Joe
abstract: Taxonomy construction is essential for knowledge-intensive NLP yet remains costly: clustering-based methods (i) need careful per-corpus tuning and yield unstable hierarchies, while LLM-based pipelines (ii) depend on expensive task-specific training that does not transfer across domains. We report an empirical finding that bears on both: in Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) embeddings, where each leading prefix is itself a usable, coarser vector, prefix length aligns with the coarse-to-fine granularity of gold taxonomies; shuffled- and reverse-dimension controls isolate the alignment to the learned early prefix dimensions. The pattern holds across three architecturally distinct MRL models. To test whether this regularity is usable, we introduce PEEL (Peeling Embeddings to Extract Latent ontologies): a minimal probe over these frozen embeddings, trained once with an order-embedding objective that represents hierarchy as vector containment; a minimum spanning arborescence then decodes taxonomic DAGs. Using only a concept vocabulary (no documents), PEEL recovers taxonomic DAGs with high structural fidelity on two OLLM benchmarks, transferring to a new domain with no target-edge supervision. The end-to-end OLLM pipeline, which jointly discovers concepts and induces structure from document corpora, is reported as a cross-task reference. Pre-trained retrieval embeddings encode a decodable granularity gradient; a minimal probe renders it as explicit parent-child (is-a) structure.
