title: Stochastic Rayleigh-Ritz Ascent: Global Linear Convergence under a Spectral Gap
authors: Jonas Bresch, Oleh Melnyk
abstract: We consider the adjoint-free random-plane iteration algorithm for finding the top eigenvector of a matrix proposed in (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 47 (2026), 1349-1374). Unlike standard methods such as the power method or gradient descent, the above algorithm lacked linear convergence guarantees in the presence of a spectral gap. In this paper, we establish explicit spectral-gap-dependent global linear convergence rates in expectation, providing quantitative guarantees for the empirically observed convergence.

title: Embodied Movable Antennas
authors: Yewen Cao, Dengke Wei, Yulin Shao
abstract: This paper introduces embodied movable antennas (MAs), a new MA architecture that rethinks the source of antenna mobility. Unlike conventional MAs that rely on dedicated antenna actuators, embodied MAs harness the mechanical degrees of freedom already present in physical agents to reconfigure antenna position and orientation. We distinguish two modes of embodied MAs: task-coupled and task-preserving. Focusing on the latter, we show how wireless channels can be reconfigured by exploiting task-equivalent host configurations without altering the prescribed physical task. Using a redundant robotic manipulator as a canonical realization, we characterize the intrinsically coupled antenna translation and orientation induced by task-preserving self-motion and derive an exact Fourier representation of the resulting multipath channel. Our analysis reveals that the wireless value of embodied mobility depends not merely on how far an antenna can move, but on which configurations remain feasible under the physical task and how their coupled motion interacts with polarization and multipath propagation. Building on this insight, we develop a cross-task antenna mounting design that enables wireless adaptation with a fixed physical installation. Numerical results demonstrate substantial communication gains through task-preserving motion. These findings establish mechanical redundancy as a new, quantifiable resource for wireless channel reconfiguration.

title: The Quartic Gap Between Quantum and Dequantized Algorithms for Linear Algebra Is Tight
authors: Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Dylan Herman, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Guneykan Ozgul
abstract: Quantum algorithms for linear algebra that access a matrix $A$ through quantum random access memory (QRAM) prepare quantum states proportional to the solutions of linear systems and related problems. Dequantized classical algorithms, when given sampling and query access to $A$, return sampling and query access to an approximate solution. Both kinds of algorithms use a number of queries that is polynomial in the normalized Frobenius norm $ρ=\|A\|_F/\|A\|$ and does not directly depend on the dimension. For linear systems at fixed condition number and accuracy, quantum algorithms use $\widetilde O(ρ)$ queries, whereas the best dequantized algorithms use $\widetilde O(ρ^4)$. We prove that this quartic gap is tight in the worst case, up to a logarithmic factor. For every constant $κ_0>1$, we construct dense linear systems with condition number at most $κ_0$ for which sampling from the solution within a sufficiently small constant total variation distance requires $Ω(ρ^4/\logρ)$ classical queries but only $Θ(ρ)$ quantum queries. The same separation holds, for errors below smaller thresholds, for positive-definite systems, least squares, ridge regression, matrix powers and square roots, imaginary-time and real-time Hamiltonian evolution, and sampling from the top principal component. Our results therefore show that many quantum algorithms for linear algebra, achieve a near-quartic speedup in the worst case, over classical algorithms with sampling and query access. All of these classical lower bounds follow from the same framework, which is based on a lower bound for sampling from distributions that depend on a fixed set of Fourier coefficients of an unknown Boolean function.

title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
authors: Antonio Blanca, Reza Gheissari, Heehyun Park, Xusheng Zhang
abstract:
Sampling from the ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model is a fundamental problem in statistical physics and approximate counting. Although computationally hard in the worst case, sampling is expected to be efficient throughout the high-temperature uniqueness regime of the model using the natural single-site Glauber dynamics. We establish fast mixing bounds for every $q$, in the full high-temperature regimes in the two central graph families on $n$ vertices.
  (1) For every $Δ\ge 3$, the Potts Glauber dynamics mixes in $n\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps with high probability on a uniformly random $Δ$-regular graph for all $β<β_u(q,\mathbb T_Δ)$ where $β_u(q,\mathbb T_Δ)$ is the uniqueness threshold on the $Δ$-regular tree;
  (2) For every $d\ge 2$, the Potts Glauber dynamics has inverse spectral gap $n^{1+o(1)}$ on cubes or tori in $\mathbb Z^d$ for all $β<β_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ where $β_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ is the critical point on $\mathbb Z^d$.
  Both temperature thresholds are sharp as the Glauber dynamics slows down exponentially above them. These results overcome the challenge of bounding mixing times without access to correlation decay bounds in the presence of pinnings (i.e., without spectral independence or strong spatial mixing). For this purpose, our proof introduces a new dichotomy principle: throughout the high-temperature regime, any initial spin distribution is either such that its pinnings ensure good correlation decay, or Glauber dynamics escapes from that distribution quickly. We expect this kind of dichotomy to have further applications. As a demonstration, we also develop its analog for random-cluster dynamics and use it to prove that Swendsen-Wang dynamics on random $Δ$-regular graphs mixes in $O(\log n)$ time throughout uniqueness.
  The results in this paper were arrived at with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 and 6.
zh_title: Potts Glauber动力学在整个唯一性区域内的快速混合
translation:
从铁磁 $q$ 态 Potts 模型中进行采样是统计物理和近似计数中的一个基本问题。尽管在最坏情况下计算困难，但在该模型的高温唯一性区域内，使用自然的单点 Glauber 动力学进行采样被预期是高效的。我们针对任意 $q$，在具有 $n$ 个顶点的两个核心图族的完整高温区域内，建立了快速混合界限：
(1) 对于任意 $\Delta \ge 3$，在所有 $\beta < \beta_u(q, \mathbb{T}_\Delta)$（其中 $\beta_u(q, \mathbb{T}_\Delta)$ 是 $\Delta$ 正则树上的唯一性阈值）下，Potts Glauber 动力学在一致随机 $\Delta$ 正则图上以高概率在 $n \operatorname{polylog}(n)$ 步内混合；
(2) 对于任意 $d \ge 2$，在所有 $\beta < \beta_c(q, \mathbb{Z}^d)$（其中 $\beta_c(q, \mathbb{Z}^d)$ 是 $\mathbb{Z}^d$ 上的临界点）下，$\mathbb{Z}^d$ 上的立方体或环面上的 Potts Glauber 动力学的逆谱隙为 $n^{1+o(1)}$。
由于 Glauber 动力学在这些温度阈值之上会呈指数级减慢，因此两个温度阈值都是尖锐的。这些结果克服了在存在固定点（pinnings）时无法获取关联衰减界限（即没有谱独立性或强空间混合）的混合时间定界挑战。为此，我们的证明引入了一种新的二分原理：在整个高温区域中，任何初始自旋分布要么其固定点确保了良好的关联衰减，要么 Glauber 动力学能迅速从该分布中逃逸。我们期望这种二分法能有进一步的应用。作为演示，我们还开发了其针对随机团簇动力学的模拟，并用它证明了随机 $\Delta$ 正则图上的 Swendsen-Wang 动力学在整个唯一性区域内以 $O(\log n)$ 时间混合。
本文的结果是在 ChatGPT 5.6 和 6 的协助下得出的。
tldr: 论文证明了Potts模型的Glauber动力学在整个高温唯一性区域内可实现快速混合，并引入了全新的二分原理来克服传统分析困难。
ai_comments: 该论文在统计物理和近似计数领域取得了重要突破，通过引入全新的“二分原理（dichotomy principle）”，在无需依赖强空间混合或谱 independence 的情况下，证明了Potts模型Glauber动力学在整个唯一性区域内的快速混合性质。该方法还成功推广到了Swendsen-Wang动力学，具有广阔的应用前景。
motivation: 尽管在最坏情况下从铁磁q态Potts模型中采样计算困难，但在模型的高温唯一性区域内，使用自然的单点Glauber动力学采样被认为应该是高效的。论文旨在建立针对任意q以及两个核心图族在全高温区域内的快速混合界限。
method: 引入了一种新的二分原理（dichotomy principle）：在整个高温区域，任何初始自旋分布要么其固定点（pinnings）能保证良好的关联衰减，要么Glauber动力学能迅速从该分布逃逸。该方法无需访问存在固定点时的关联衰减界限。
results: (1) 对于任意 $\Delta \ge 3$，在所有 $\beta < \beta_u(q, \mathbb{T}_\Delta)$ 条件下，Potts Glauber动力学在一致随机 $\Delta$-正则图上以高概率在 $n \operatorname{polylog}(n)$ 步内混合；(2) 对于任意 $d \ge 2$，在所有 $\beta < \beta_c(q, \mathbb{Z}^d)$ 条件下，$\mathbb{Z}^d$ 的立方体或环面上的Potts Glauber动力学具有 $n^{1+o(1)}$ 的逆谱隙。此外，证明了随机 $\Delta$-正则图上的Swendsen-Wang动力学在唯一性区域内以 $O(\log n)$ 时间混合。
conclusion: 论文证明了Potts Glauber动力学在整个唯一性区域内具有快速混合性质，并引入了新型二分原理，该原理有望在其他统计物理模型和算法分析中得到更广泛的应用。

title: Hard Constraint Projection in a Physics Informed Neural Network (Burgers)
authors: Miranda J S Horne, Peter K Jimack, Amirul Khan, He Wang
abstract: Physics informed machine learning provides a framework to study and simulate fluid dynamics, potentially at a fraction of the computational cost of traditional numerical methods, with the goal of improving the explainability, accuracy and robustness of purely data driven machine learning methods. In this work, we extend the hard constraint projection (HCP) method developed by Chen et al. [Journal of Computational Physics, 445, 110624, 2021] from a linear partial differential equation (PDE) to a nonlinear PDE: the 1D Burgers' equation. To strictly impose a discrete approximation of the governing equation, the Burgers' equation is first locally discretised (using a finite difference stencil) then decomposed into a constraint matrix and a prediction matrix. Using tools from linear algebra, the constraint matrix is used to construct a projection matrix. A physics informed neural network (PINN) [Raissi et al. Journal of Computational Physics, 378, 686, 2019] is used to predict the velocity, and a final unlearnable layer projects the velocity prediction to the hyperplane of exact solutions to a discretised form of the Burgers' equation. Our initial results indicate that the HCP-PINN initially trains similarly to an equivalent PINN, and as the PINN loss plateaus, the HCP-PINN loss continues to decline. When tested on a previously unseen uniform grid of points covering the domain, the HCP-PINN exhibits higher accuracy, converging to a data error approximately an order of magnitude lower than the comparable PINN. We also observe that the inclusion of the HCP layer results in better observance of the governing PDE. Our findings suggest that the HCP-PINN can be more robust to the selection of physics collocation points, and less dependent on collocation point quantity.
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, In proceedings of 1st international Symposium on AI and Fluid Mechanics 2025 (Paper No. S11P2)

title: Regret-Optimal Wasserstein-Robust Linear Regression
authors: Sloan Nietert, Daniel Kuhn
abstract: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) minimizes worst-case risk under distributional uncertainty, but its decisions can be suboptimal in terms of their excess risk, or regret. We study this gap for multivariate least-squares regression, assuming that the observed source law and unknown target law differ by an adversarial 2-Wasserstein perturbation of size $\varepsilon$. We first identify the asymptotic complexity of robust decision-making in the $\varepsilon \to 0$ limit, characterized by a problem-specific condition number $κ$. Here, a wide spectrum of simple algorithms, including DRO, achieve the instance-optimal rate of $O(κ\varepsilon^2)$. For fixed $\varepsilon > 0$, we prove that DRO still achieves the minimax rate if the problem has bounded residual effective rank. On the other hand, we identify significant failure modes where DRO is provably suboptimal by dimension-dependent factors. Fortunately, we prove that two alternative procedures, minimax regret optimization (MRO) and spectral-norm regularization (SNR), attain the minimax rate. We derive an exact convex reformulation of MRO and an accelerated proximal algorithm for SNR, along with high-probability finite-sample guarantees. We support these theoretical results with numerical experiments separating the performance of MRO and SNR from DRO.

title: Dirichlet form approach to stochastic thin-film equations
authors: Benjamin Gess, Felix Otto, Max Sauerbrey
abstract:
The thin-film equation describes the evolution of a thin liquid film driven by capillarity and limited by viscosity. For sufficiently small film heights, thermal fluctuations may not be neglected. Since the thin-film equation as an overdamped evolution equation has a gradient flow structure, the informal implementation of the fluctuation-dissipation principle is straightforward. In this paper, we work out that the concept of Dirichlet forms and the related construction of Markov processes are tailor-made for this type of overdamped continuum evolution with thermal noise. However, the concept of Dirichlet forms relies on the availability of a Gibbsian equilibrium measure, which, in case of the thin-film equation, limits the treatment to the $(1+1)$-dimensional case.
  By means of Dirichlet form theory, we obtain the existence and uniqueness of the evolution of laws on configuration space. We show that the regularity of the realizations of this Markov process matches the heuristics. In a simplified situation with a Gaussian reference measure and a non-degenerate mobility function, we characterize it as what is called an energy solution. The latter provides a pathwise decomposition of the driving forces into a deterministic and a thermal one, which was the starting point.
  Applying the same techniques in the spatially discretized setting proposed in [Math. Comp. 92 (2023), 1931--1976], we obtain the same results uniformly in the discretization parameter. In particular, Galerkin as well as spectral approximations of the stochastic thin-film equation are shown to be uniformly tight in optimal topologies. In the simplified setting, we also prove Mosco convergence of the associated Dirichlet forms and thereby obtain convergence of these approximations.

title: SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts with Satellite Data using Machine Learning
authors: Ioannis Dravilas, Miruna Stoicescu, Roope Tervo, Carlos Horn, Oriol Hinojo Comellas, Sina Montazeri, Andrea Meraner, Ana Lucic
abstract: Atmospheric fronts are associated with much of the high-impact weather in the mid-latitudes, yet their identification and classification remain largely manual and subjective. Existing deep learning approaches rely primarily on gridded reanalysis or forecast data, limiting their applicability to satellite observations available for time-critical applications. We introduce SATFRONT, a machine learning framework for detecting cold, warm, and occluded fronts over Europe from geostationary satellite observations, with reanalysis data as an optional additional input. The model is trained on frontal analyses from five European national meteorological services and evaluated against UK Met Office analyses for 2024. Using satellite observations alone, SATFRONT achieves a Critical Success Index (CSI) of 0.428 at a 150 km tolerance, within the range of agreement between analyses from different meteorological services (0.277-0.501) and higher than that of an operational rule-based front detector that uses satellite data (0.133). Adding ERA5 reanalysis increases the CSI to 0.591. ERA5 substantially improves the placement of individual fronts, although its effect on their annual spatial distribution varies by front type. These results demonstrate that cold, warm, and occluded fronts can be detected directly from geostationary satellite observations, providing a basis for automated frontal analyses at the high temporal frequency required for time-critical applications.

title: Functional Tensor Trains for High-Order Greeks and Exposure Tails of Multi-Asset Structured Products
authors: Javier Lopez-Piqueres, Atithi Acharya, Yue Sun, Niraj Kumar
abstract: Risk management of worst-of autocallables needs price sensitivities (Greeks) up to third order and the potential future exposure, a tail quantile of the note's future value. In Monte Carlo, each order of differentiation multiplies the sampling noise by a factor that grows with the observation frequency, and nested simulation turns the noise of its inner paths into a bias of the quantile. We instead solve the backward pricing recursion, storing the continuation value as an $hp$ functional tensor train (hp-FTT) whose piecewise-polynomial cores are split at the barriers, so that worst-of barrier events act exactly, with rank one. For Gaussian transitions we show that the polynomial degree sufficient for an error $\varepsilon$ grows only as $\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}$. One solve then gives every Greek at any spot without sampling noise, by integrating the likelihood-ratio weight against the stored value, and the values it stores at future dates replace inner simulation. Against the strongest Monte Carlo estimators we could build or find published, on worst-of autocallables observed monthly on three to five assets, the order of the Greek and the accuracy decide which method is cheaper. At $1\%$ accuracy Monte Carlo is more than an order of magnitude cheaper for deltas, second-order Greeks go either way, and hp-FTT is cheaper for every third-order Greek, by up to two orders of magnitude. At $0.1\%$ hp-FTT is cheaper for every Greek we could check, under geometric Brownian motion and local volatility alike. For the exposure alone Monte Carlo is cheaper at $1\%$ and hp-FTT at $0.1\%$, and a solve run for the Greeks yields it for little more than scenario sampling. Sampling pays in variance for each derivative and hp-FTT in rank for each asset, so Monte Carlo keeps low-order Greeks at percent accuracy, rarely observed contracts and many assets.

title: Full-Duplex-Enabled Integrated Sensing and Communications: Opportunities and Challenges
authors: Chandan Kumar Sheemar, George C. Alexandropoulos, Sourabh Solanki, Eva Lagunas, Jorge Querol, Symeon Chatzinotas
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) is one of the six usage scenarios of IMT-2030, with in-band full duplex (IBFD) being the most direct way to realize it. In this paradigm, a base station that transmits and receives on the same time-frequency resources can sense continuously with its own downlink waveform while serving uplink traffic. This article revisits full-duplex-enabled ISAC (FD-ISAC) in light of the technologies lately shaping sixth-generation (6G) radio design, such as extremely large multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems operating in the near field, holographic and dynamic metasurface apertures, fluid and movable antennas, beyond-diagonal reconfigucable intelligent surfaces (BS-RISs) and wave-domain processing with stacked intelligent metasurfaces. We present a holistic FD-ISAC architecture built around a multi-stage, echo-preserving self-interference cancellation chain, and map each 6G technological enabler to the gains it brings and the risks it introduces. A case study with a $28$~GHz full-duplex XL-MIMO base station showcases that near-field-aware beamforming combined with wave-domain, analog, and digital cancellation delivers more than twice the throughput of half-duplex and 3GPP sub-band full-duplex baselines at the same localization-accuracy bound. It is also demonstrated that incorporating a group-connected BD-RIS recovers most of the fully-connected gain at a small fraction of its circuit complexity. The article concludes discussing emerging use cases and open challenges.

title: Time Will Tell: Harness Time to Denoise Collaborative Filtering
authors: Xinyu He, Jose Sepulveda, Mostafa Rahmani, Alyssa Woo, Fei Wang, Hanghang Tong
abstract: Neural graph collaborative filtering is a powerful tool for recommendation due to its superb capability of capturing the user-item interaction. Despite the substantial progress, the noisy nature of interaction data remains a significant challenge in collaborative filtering, especially for data collected from implicit feedback. Both noisy interactions and interactions crafted by malicious users could greatly degenerate model performance. To purify the input data and enhance model robustness, it is vital to understand how noisy interactions can be identified and rectified. Existing denoising methods focus on mining the correlation between user/item embeddings and noisy interactions, neglecting the temporal dimension for denoising. However, time information bears its natural and unique advantage in revealing noisy edges as we observe in this paper. In this work, we introduce a simple yet effective mechanism for generating time-aware user/item embeddings that capture both global preferences and temporal patterns. Two strategies, reweighting adjacency matrix (Tint-A) and reweighting loss function (Tint-L), are proposed to leverage the embeddings for the task of using \underline{t}ime \underline{in}forma\underline{t}ion to denoise \underline{c}ollaborative \underline{f}iltering (TintCF). Extensive experiments have been conducted on four real-world datasets to demonstrate the efficacy of our methods and illustrate how time information indeed helps identify and rectify noisy edges. Our codes are available at \href{https://github.com/xinyuu-he/TintCF}{https://github.com/xinyuu-he/TintCF}.

title: point2vec for Self-Supervised Representation Learning on Point Clouds
authors: Karim Knaebel, Jonas Schult, Alexander Hermans, Bastian Leibe
abstract: We present point2vec, a self-supervised method for learning point cloud representations through masked prediction of a teacher network's latent features. Building on data2vec, we investigate a limitation of applying this approach to point clouds: positional information associated with masked patches reveals the overall object shape to the student, weakening the learning task even under heavy masking. point2vec addresses this issue by passing only visible patches to the student encoder and introducing a shallow decoder to predict representations for masked patches. The teacher processes the complete point cloud to provide contextualized training targets. These targets capture global context through the teacher's self-attention, providing supervision beyond the local geometry of individual patches. This design conceals masked-patch positions from the student and reduces its computational cost during pre-training. Our ablations show that the decoder alone provides only part of the improvement; concealing positional information is key. After pre-training on ShapeNet, point2vec outperforms the evaluated self-supervised baselines on shape classification on ModelNet40 and ScanObjectNN and few-shot classification on ModelNet40, while achieving competitive part segmentation results on ShapeNetPart.

title: Slim attention: cut your context memory in half without loss -- K-cache is all you need for MHA
authors: Nils Graef, Kayvan Zahiri, Andrew Wasielewski
abstract:
Slim attention shrinks the context memory size by 2x for transformer models with MHA (multi-head attention), which can speed up inference by up to 2x for large context windows.
  Slim attention is an exact, mathematically identical implementation of the standard attention mechanism and therefore doesn't compromise model accuracy. In other words, slim attention losslessly compresses the context memory by a factor of 2.
  For encoder-decoder transformers, the context memory size can be reduced even further: For the Whisper models for example, slim attention reduces the context memory by 8x, which can speed up token generation by 5x for batch size 64 for example.
  And for the T5-11B model for example, the memory can be reduced by 32x because its MHA projection dimension is larger than the embedding dimension.
  See https://github.com/OpenMachine-ai/transformer-tricks for code and more transformer tricks, and https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uVtk3B6YO4Y for this paper's YouTube video.

title: Relatively-Secure LLM-Based Steganography via Constrained Markov Decision Processes for High-Efficiency Embedding
authors: Yu-Shin Huang, Chao Tian, Krishna Narayanan, Lizhong Zheng
abstract: Linguistic steganography aims to conceal information within natural language text without being detected. An effective steganography approach should encode the secret message bits into a minimal number of language tokens while preserving the natural appearance and fluency of the stego-texts. We present a new framework to enhance the embedding efficiency by framing the steganographic embedding procedure as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP), which takes into consideration the long-term dependencies instead of merely the immediate effects. We constrain the solution space such that the discounted expected cumulative total variation between the selected conditional probability distribution and the original one given by the LLM is below a threshold. To find the optimal policy, we first show that the functional optimization problem can be simplified to a convex problem with a finite number of variables. For the binary-state model, we give a full characterization of the optimal policy, including closed-form expressions in several regimes, and show that it displays water-filling-like behavior in certain cases. The solution indicates that states with highly deterministic transition distributions are preferable for adjustment in the binary-state case. For larger state spaces, the optimal solution is more complex and explicit solutions are difficult to obtain, but the optimal policies show similar structural behaviors.

title: A Cross-Country Evaluation of Sentiment Toward Digital Payment Systems in Africa
authors: Isabel Agadagba, Triphonia Kilasara, Takudzwa Tarutira, Noah Shumba, Nicolas Christin, Obigbemi Imoleayo Foyeke, Assane Gueye, Edith Luhanga, Alexander Rusero, Karen Sowon, Giulia Fanti
abstract: Digital payment systems are a cornerstone of African consumer finance, including money transfer applications, mobile money, cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs). While many studies explore how people use digital payment systems (in Africa and beyond), little is known about how people choose and reason about categories of payment systems. We conducted qualitative interviews in three African countries--Nigeria, Tanzania, and Zimbabwe--to understand how and why people use various payment systems. Our study suggests that users navigate accounts and payments on multiple payment systems through a complex selection process based on perceived tradeoffs between utility, privacy, and security. Many users trust government issuers to protect them from scams, but they do not trust those same institutions to build reliable products or prioritize customer satisfaction. Our findings suggest compelling directions for regulators and the research community to design systems that balance users' trust and utility needs.

title: Accelerated Approximate Optimization of Multi-Commodity Flows on Directed Graphs
authors: Li Chen, Andrei Graur, Aaron Sidford
abstract:
We provide $m^{1+o(1)}kε^{-1}$-time algorithms for computing multiplicative $(1 - ε)$-approximate solutions to multi-commodity flow problems with $k$-commodities on $m$-edge directed graphs, including concurrent multi-commodity flow and maximum multi-commodity flow.
  To obtain our results, we provide new optimization tools of potential independent interest. First, we provide an improved optimization method for solving $\ell_{q, p}$-regression problems to high accuracy. This method makes $\tilde{O}_{q, p}(k)$ queries to a high accuracy convex minimization oracle for an individual block, where $\tilde{O}_{q, p}(\cdot)$ hides factors depending only on $q$, $p$, or $\mathrm{poly}(\log m)$, improving upon the $\tilde{O}_{q, p}(k^2)$ bound of [Chen-Ye, ICALP 2024]. As a result, we obtain the first almost-linear time algorithm that solves $\ell_{q, p}$ flows on directed graphs to high accuracy. Second, we present optimization tools to reduce approximately solving composite $\ell_{1, \infty}$-regression problems to solving $m^{o(1)}ε^{-1}$ instances of composite $\ell_{q, p}$-regression problem. The method builds upon recent advances in solving box-simplex games [Jambulapati-Tian, NeurIPS 2023] and the area convex regularizer introduced in [Sherman, STOC 2017] to obtain faster rates for constrained versions of the problem. Carefully combining these techniques yields our directed multi-commodity flow algorithm.

title: GENSTRAT: Toward a Science of Strategic Reasoning in Large Language Models
authors: Vartan Shadarevian, Kia Ghods, Alex Kenich, Anany Kotawala
abstract: Fixed game suites for evaluating strategic reasoning in large language models (LLMs) saturate and are hard to keep free of contamination. We introduce GENSTRAT, a system for evaluating the strategic capabilities of LLMs driven by procedural generation of two-player zero-sum imperfect-information betting games, allowing an evaluator to draw novel, fresh games on demand. Each game is characterized on a scale of five complexity axes (state space, temporal contingency, opponent dependence, private information, precision) and measured by Monte Carlo simulation. Using this generator, we construct a 50-game benchmark and hold a tournament of twelve frontier and open-weight models, gathering data from over 40,000 LLM vs. LLM matches. We further construct a composite complexity axis, and find that, on the eight hardest games, the gap between the best and worst model is 1.7x its value across the whole set of games. Ablations show that a higher thinking budget, disclosing the opponent's strategy, and higher reasoning matched to a game's specific demands (for private information and planning depth) were associated with higher margins for the LLM player.

title: Site Percolation on Multi-dimensional Lattice
authors: Marko Puljic
abstract: Sites in an infinite d-dimensional lattice, open with probability greater or equal to 1/d, form an infinite open path.

title: Denoising Multirobot Trajectories
authors: Yuhao Zhang, Keisuke Okumura, Ajay Shankar, Amanda Prorok
abstract: Multi-robot trajectory planning is a fundamental problem in multi-robot coordination but remains computationally challenging due to its nonconvex, multimodal, and high-dimensional nature. This work builds upon D4orm, a dynamics-aware diffusion-denoising framework, and develops a family of planning architectures for diverse operational requirements. Unlike conventional numerical optimization methods, D4orm employs sampling-based optimization to generate solution trajectories through massively parallel sampling, leveraging modern computing architectures such as GPUs. Its diffusion-denoising structure iteratively optimizes deformations to candidate control trajectories, providing an efficient and versatile paradigm for generating kinodynamically feasible and conflict-free trajectories. Using D4orm as the building block for advanced planners, we present a decoupled planner for improved scalability, an online receding-horizon planner with feedback control, and a distributed planner for resource-constrained settings. Evaluations with differential-drive and holonomic robots in 2D and 3D environments demonstrate that D4orm-based approaches find high-quality solutions faster and more reliably than other sampling-based optimization methods, such as MPPI, as well as a learned diffusion-model-based method. We further demonstrate zero-shot deployment on ten real quadrotors with obstacles, large-scale deconfliction with 100 simulated robots, and fully onboard distributed `lifelong' operation with six ground robots. Overall, these results establish diffusion denoising as a scalable and reliable framework for multi-robot coordination. Code and video: https://github.com/proroklab/d4orm
comment: Accepted to IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO) 2026

title: On kernel Mengerian orientations of line multigraphs
authors: Han Xiao
abstract: A kernel of a digraph is an independent set $K$ such that every vertex outside $K$ has an arc to a vertex in $K$. We present a polyhedral description of kernels in clique-acyclic orientations of line multigraphs. Given a digraph $D$, let $FK(D)$ denote its fractional kernel polytope, and let $σ(D)$ denote the linear system defining $FK(D)$. A digraph $D$ is called kernel perfect if every induced subdigraph has a kernel, called kernel ideal if the fractional kernel polytope of every induced subdigraph is integral, and called kernel Mengerian if the defining system of every induced subdigraph is totally dual integral. We show that a clique-acyclic orientation of a line multigraph is kernel ideal if and only if it is kernel Mengerian. These equivalent properties hold precisely when the orientation is kernel perfect and has no even-cycle obstruction.

zh_title: 关于线多重图的核门格尔定向
translation: 有向图的核是一个独立集 $K$，使得 $K$ 之外的每个顶点都有一条弧指向 $K$ 中的一个顶点。我们提出了线多重图的团无环定向中核的多面体描述。给定一个有向图 $D$，令 $FK(D)$ 表示其分数核多面体，并令 $σ(D)$ 表示定义 $FK(D)$ 的线性系统。一个有向图 $D$ 被称为核完美（kernel perfect），如果其每个导出子有向图都有一个核；被称为核理想（kernel ideal），如果其每个导出子有向图的分数核多面体是整数的；被称为核门格尔（kernel Mengerian），如果其每个导出子有向图的定义系统是完全对偶整数的。我们证明了线多重图的团无环定向是核理想的当且仅当它是核门格尔的。这些等价性质精确地在定向是核完美且没有偶循环障碍时成立。
tldr: 本文描述了线多重图的团无环定向中核的多面体，并证明了对于这类定向，核理想性等价于核门格尔性，且当其核完美且无偶循环障碍时这些性质成立。
ai_comments: 这篇论文通过对线多重图的团无环定向中核的多面体描述，深入探讨了核理想性、核门格尔性和核完美性之间的深刻联系。其创新之处在于揭示了特定图类中这些性质的等价条件，为图论和组合优化领域的理论研究提供了新的见解。
motivation: 研究有向图的核概念及其相关性质，特别是在线多重图的团无环定向背景下，探讨核理想性、核门格尔性和核完美性之间的关系。
method: 提出了线多重图的团无环定向中核的多面体描述。

title: PixelMoE: Scaling Pixel-Space Diffusion with LLM-Style Mixture-of-Experts
authors: Ruixiao Dong, Jianmin Bao, Bozhi Luan, Zijie Meng, Xin Tao, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai, Li Li, Houqiang Li
abstract: Pixel-space diffusion models provide an appealing alternative to latent-space diffusion models by directly modeling raw images without relying on a learned tokenizer. However, scaling pixel-space models has predominantly followed dense strategies, tightly coupling model capacity with active computation. In this work, we show that standard LLM-style Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures can be effectively transferred to pixel-space diffusion. Building on this finding, we introduce PixelMoE, a pixel-space generative framework that sparsely scales model capacity with standard LLM-style MoE, without diffusion-specific routing mechanisms or auxiliary routing objectives. Specifically, PixelMoE combines standard Token-Choice (TC) routing with fine-grained routed experts for input-adaptive sparse computation, a shared expert for capturing common representations, and a bias-based load-balancing strategy. To complement sparse capacity scaling, PixelMoE further introduces Pixel-Space Hierarchical Flow Matching, which varies spatial resolution along the denoising trajectory from global structure formation to fine-grained detail refinement. At comparable active parameter counts, PixelMoE consistently outperforms its dense counterparts across model scales, demonstrating effective sparse capacity scaling in pixel space. On class-conditional ImageNet-1K, PixelMoE achieves FID scores of 1.47 at 256x256 and 1.53 at 512x512 without representation alignment or perceptual losses, comparing favorably with leading pixel-space and latent-space generative models. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/KlingAIResearch/PixelMoE and https://huggingface.co/KlingTeam/PixelMoE, respectively.
zh_title: PixelMoE：结合LLM风格混合专家的像素空间扩散模型扩展
translation: 像素空间扩散模型通过直接对原始图像进行建模而不依赖于学习到的分词器，为潜在空间扩散模型提供了一个引人注目的替代方案。然而，像素空间模型的扩展主要采用稠密策略，将模型容量与主动计算紧密耦合。在这项工作中，我们表明标准的LLM风格混合专家（MoE）架构可以有效地转移到像素空间扩散中。基于这一发现，我们介绍了PixelMoE，一个像素空间生成框架，它利用标准的LLM风格MoE稀疏扩展模型容量，无需扩散特定的路由机制或辅助路由目标。具体来说，PixelMoE将标准的Token-Choice (TC) 路由与输入自适应稀疏计算的细粒度路由专家、用于捕获通用表示的共享专家以及基于偏差的负载均衡策略相结合。为了补充稀疏容量扩展，PixelMoE进一步引入了像素空间分层流匹配，它沿去噪轨迹改变空间分辨率，从全局结构形成到细粒度细节精炼。在可比的主动参数量下，PixelMoE在各个模型尺度上始终优于其稠密对应模型，证明了像素空间中有效的稀疏容量扩展。在类条件ImageNet-1K上，PixelMoE在无需表征对齐或感知损失的情况下，在256x256和512x512分辨率下分别获得了1.47和1.53的FID分数，与领先的像素空间和潜在空间生成模型相比表现优异。代码和预训练模型分别可在https://github.com/KlingAIResearch/PixelMoE和https://huggingface.co/KlingTeam/PixelMoE获取。
tldr: PixelMoE通过引入LLM风格的MoE架构和分层流匹配技术，实现了像素空间扩散模型的高效稀疏扩展，在ImageNet上取得了领先的生成性能。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地将大语言模型中的混合专家（MoE）架构引入到像素空间扩散模型中，通过稀疏扩展模型容量在不显著增加计算开销的同时提升了生成质量，为像素空间生成模型的发展提供了新思路。
motivation: 像素空间扩散模型通常采用稠密计算策略，将模型容量与实际计算紧密耦合。为了实现更高效的扩展，本文旨在探究是否可以将大语言模型（LLM）风格的混合专家（MoE）架构有效地转移并应用于像素空间扩散模型中。
method: 引入了PixelMoE框架，结合了标准Token-Choice (TC) 路由与细粒度专家、用于捕获通用表示的共享专家、基于偏差的负载均衡策略，以及用于沿去噪轨迹改变空间分辨率的像素空间分层流匹配技术。
results: 在同等有效参数量下，PixelMoE在多个模型尺度上持续优于稠密模型。在ImageNet-1K数据集上，无需表征对齐或感知损失，256x256和512x512分辨率下的FID分别达到了1.47和1.53。
conclusion: PixelMoE成功将LLM风格的MoE架构与像素空间扩散模型相结合，通过稀疏容量扩展和分层流匹配技术，在ImageNet-1K上取得了优异的生成效果，证明了像素空间稀疏扩展的巨大潜力。

title: Transport-Free Lower Bounds for Ollivier--Ricci Curvature in Higher-Order Networks: Scope, Tightness, and Computational Applications
authors: Wonwoo Kang, Heehyun Park
abstract: We study how the Bauer--Jost--Liu curvature bound applies to hypergraph Ollivier--Ricci curvature (ORC) and how its accuracy depends on local mass and geometry. An explicit weighted-graph representation shows how the graph theorem applies. A transport construction transfers the bounds to monotone pairwise hyperedge aggregations. We analyze endpoint cancellation under laziness, quantify the exact improvement over the earlier mixture bound, and characterize the extremal geometry at fixed endpoint and overlap statistics. Further results quantify worst-case slack, stability, and exactness on isolated hyperedges. A capacity-constrained short-detour refinement uses additional geometric information and improves monotonically as the query budget increases. As a computational application, a threshold cascade preserves exact transport decisions. Numerical verification and public-hypergraph experiments examine tightness, walk dependence, and aggregation, including evaluations on 42,940 finite pairwise comparisons and 64,620 public-data instances. Together, the results specify the scope, equality mechanisms, and computational uses of BJL-type hypergraph bounds.

title: Discovering contemporaneous and lagged causal relations in autocorrelated nonlinear time series datasets
authors: Jakob Runge
abstract: The paper introduces a novel conditional independence (CI) based method for linear and nonlinear, lagged and contemporaneous causal discovery from observational time series in the causally sufficient case. Existing CI-based methods such as the PC algorithm and also common methods from other frameworks suffer from low recall and partially inflated false positives for strong autocorrelation which is an ubiquitous challenge in time series. The novel method, PCMCI$^+$, extends PCMCI [Runge et al., 2019b] to include discovery of contemporaneous links. PCMCI$^+$ improves the reliability of CI tests by optimizing the choice of conditioning sets and even benefits from autocorrelation. The method is order-independent and consistent in the oracle case. A broad range of numerical experiments demonstrates that PCMCI$^+$ has higher adjacency detection power and especially more contemporaneous orientation recall compared to other methods while better controlling false positives. Optimized conditioning sets also lead to much shorter runtimes than the PC algorithm. PCMCI$^+$ can be of considerable use in many real world application scenarios where often time resolutions are too coarse to resolve time delays and strong autocorrelation is present.
comment: published in the Proceedings of the 36th Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence (UAI), PMLR volume 124, 2020; corrected version (October 2026)
zh_title: 在自相关非线性时间序列数据集中发现同期和滞后因果关系
translation: 本文介绍了一种新颖的基于条件独立性（CI）的方法，用于在因果充分的情况下，从观测时间序列中发现线性、非线性、滞后和同期的因果关系。现有的基于CI的方法，如PC算法，以及其他框架的常见方法，在处理时间序列中普遍存在的强自相关时，存在召回率低和部分误报率高的问题。这种新方法PCMCI$^+$扩展了PCMCI [Runge et al., 2019b]，以包括同期链接的发现。PCMCI$^+$通过优化条件集选择来提高CI测试的可靠性，甚至能从自相关中获益。该方法在理想情况下是顺序无关且一致的。大量的数值实验表明，PCMCI$^+$与其他方法相比，具有更高的邻接检测能力，尤其在同期方向召回率方面表现更优，同时能更好地控制误报。优化的条件集也使得运行时间比PC算法大大缩短。PCMCI$^+$在许多实际应用场景中具有重要价值，这些场景通常时间分辨率过粗以至于无法解决时间延迟，并且存在强自相关。
tldr: 本文介绍了一种名为PCMCI$^+$的新型条件独立性（CI）方法，用于在自相关非线性时间序列中发现同期和滞后因果关系。该方法解决了现有CI方法在强自相关下召回率低和误报高的问题，通过优化条件集提高了检测能力和运行效率。

motivation: 现有基于条件独立性（CI）的方法（如PC算法）以及其他框架的常见方法，在处理时间序列中普遍存在的强自相关时，存在召回率低和部分误报率高的问题。
method: 论文介绍了一种名为PCMCI$^+$的新型条件独立性（CI）方法。该方法扩展了PCMCI算法，以包括同期因果关系的发现，并通过优化条件集选择来提高CI测试的可靠性，甚至能从自相关中获益。PCMCI$^+$适用于线性和非线性、滞后和同期的因果发现，且在理想情况下是顺序无关和一致的。
results: 数值实验表明，PCMCI$^+$与其他方法相比，具有更高的邻接检测能力，尤其在同期方向召回率方面表现更优，同时能更好地控制误报。优化的条件集也使得运行时间比PC算法大大缩短。
conclusion: PCMCI$^+$在许多实际应用场景中具有重要价值，特别是在时间分辨率过粗无法解决时间延迟且存在强自相关的情况下。

title: A First Course in Monte Carlo Methods
authors: Daniel Sanz-Alonso, Omar Al-Ghattas
abstract: This is a concise mathematical introduction to Monte Carlo methods, a rich family of algorithms with far-reaching applications in science and engineering. Monte Carlo methods are an exciting subject for mathematical statisticians and computational and applied mathematicians: the design and analysis of modern algorithms are rooted in a broad mathematical toolbox that includes ergodic theory of Markov chains, Hamiltonian dynamical systems, transport maps, stochastic differential equations, information theory, optimization, Riemannian geometry, and gradient flows, among many others. These lecture notes celebrate the breadth of mathematical ideas that have led to tangible advancements in Monte Carlo methods and their applications. To accommodate a diverse audience, the level of mathematical rigor varies from chapter to chapter, giving only an intuitive treatment to the most technically demanding subjects. The aim is not to be comprehensive or encyclopedic, but rather to illustrate some key principles in the design and analysis of Monte Carlo methods through a carefully-crafted choice of topics that emphasizes timeless over timely ideas. Algorithms are presented in a way that is conducive to conceptual understanding and mathematical analysis -- clarity and intuition are favored over state-of-the-art implementations that are harder to comprehend or rely on ad-hoc heuristics. To help readers navigate the expansive landscape of Monte Carlo methods, each algorithm is accompanied by a summary of its pros and cons, and by a discussion of the type of problems for which they are most useful. The presentation is self-contained, and therefore adequate for self-guided learning or as a teaching resource. Each chapter contains a section with bibliographic remarks that will be useful for those interested in conducting research on Monte Carlo methods and their applications.

title: Learning Maximal Regions of Attraction on Compact Sets using Taylor Lyapunov Networks
authors: Matthieu Barreau, Nicola Bastianello
abstract: We consider the problem of learning maximal Lyapunov functions to compute the maximal region of attraction of nonlinear dynamical systems using neural networks. Two obstacles limit existing neural-network approaches: 1) finite-width approximations can fail to preserve the strict Lyapunov inequalities near the equilibrium, where they become arbitrarily weak, and 2) training is necessarily performed on a bounded computational domain for which the classical Lyapunov and Zubov theorems do not directly apply. To address these issues, first we derive Lyapunov and Zubov theorems directly on a prescribed compact computational domain, characterizing the maximal region of attraction within that domain as the solution of a boundary-value PDE. Second, we introduce the Taylor Lyapunov network, an architecture that prescribes the quadratic leading-order term via the system's linearization and represents the higher-order remainder through a structured cubic factorization, guaranteeing that any network in this class is a valid local Lyapunov function by construction. Finally, we prove that Taylor Lyapunov networks are universal approximators of maximal Lyapunov functions on compact domains, and combine these results into an unsupervised, physics-informed training procedure. Numerical experiments on systems of varying dimensions and stability types show that the proposed architecture is efficient at estimating the maximum region of attraction.

title: Explainable AI-Driven Neural Activity Analysis in Parkinsonian Rats under Electrical Stimulation
authors: Jibum Kim, Hanseul Choi, Gaeun Kim, Sunggu Yang, Eunha Baeg, Donggue Kim, Seongwon Jin, Sangwon Byun
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by motor dysfunction and abnormal neural oscillations. This study combined graphene-based cortical stimulation with an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework to investigate spatial and frequency-related features contributing to pre- and post-stimulation classification in Parkinsonian rats. Electrocorticogram (ECoG) signals were recorded before and after stimulation and classified using EEGNet and DeepConvNet. Layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) and DeepLIFT were applied to identify frequency bands and recording channels contributing to the classification. The anatomical locations of these channels were mapped onto a cortical map. XAI analyses were performed separately for each animal to examine individual attribution patterns. Our XAI analysis revealed frequency-band- and region-specific contributions to pre- and post-stimulation classification in Parkinsonian rats. Our approach provided complementary insights into the features contributing to pre- and post-stimulation ECoG classification alongside PSD-based analyses. These findings highlight the potential of combining graphene-based cortical stimulation with explainable deep learning to identify classification-relevant features across frequency bands and cortical areas in pre- and post-stimulation recordings.

title: NumPSLA -- An experimental research tool for pseudoline arrangements and order types
authors: Günter Rote
abstract: We present a program for enumerating all pseudoline arrangements with a small number of pseudolines and abstract order types of small point sets. This program supports computer experiments with these structures, and it complements the order-type database of Aichholzer, Aurenhammer, and Krasser. This system makes it practical to explore the abstract order types for 12 points, and the pseudoline arrangements of 11 pseudolines.
comment: 27 pages, 16 figures. Full version of a paper that has appeared (without appendices) in the 41st European Workshop on Computational Geometry, Liblice, Czech republic, April 9-11, 2025. Version 2: The entries in the lowest three lines of Table 6 have been corrected

title: Lattice-Based Pruning of Recurrent Neural Networks via Poset Modeling: A Corrected Theory and a Matched-Sparsity Evaluation
authors: Rakesh Sengupta
abstract: Magnitude pruning of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) ignores how information flows between neurons. An earlier version proposed to model RNN dependencies as a partially ordered set (poset) and to retain the meet-irreducible elements of its dependency lattice. By Birkhoff's representation theorem, the meet-irreducible ideals of a finite poset are in bijection with its elements, so retaining them retains everything; the critical-set criterion used earlier selects precisely the elements comparable to all others, of which a dense recurrent layer has none. Condensing a thresholded dependency graph into strongly connected components yields a well-defined dependency order, a graded order score and an acyclic pruning rule; for Cohen-Grossberg networks and LSTMs, acyclic pruning makes local stability decompose over modules. For a 128-unit LSTM pruned at matched sparsity on row-wise and chunked sequential MNIST (three seeds, equal training budgets), the original rules remove every recurrent weight or equal random column pruning; the order score is no better than degree, PageRank or norm; trained weights show little directional bias; and imposing acyclicity from initialisation costs 2.1 and 10.5 percentage points at 50% and 90% sparsity. In the networks studied, order structure must be imposed rather than discovered.
comment: v2: substantially revised. The Transformer extension of v1 is withdrawn. 29 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables

title: Building functional and mechanistic models of cortical computation based on canonical cell type connectivity
authors: Arno Granier, Katharina A Wilmes, Mihai A Petrovici, Walter Senn
abstract: Neuronal circuits of the cerebral cortex are the structural basis of mammalian cognition. The same qualitative components and connectivity motifs are repeated across functionally specialized cortical areas and mammalian species, suggesting a single underlying algorithmic motif. Here, we propose a perspective on current knowledge of the cortical structure, from which we extract two core principles for computational modeling. The first principle is that cortical cell types fulfill distinct computational roles. The second principle is that cortical connectivity can be efficiently characterized by only a few canonical blueprints of connectivity between cell types. Starting with these two foundational principles, we outline a general framework for building functional and mechanistic models of cortical circuits. Finally, we show that the compressed and generative representations of connectivity entailed by this framework are particularly amenable to automatic search through gradient-free optimization, providing a concrete first step towards modelling the evolution of functional neural circuits.

title: Marginal effects for the stochastic actor-oriented model
authors: Daniel Gotthardt, Christian Steglich
abstract: Parameter estimates of stochastic actor-oriented models for network evolution are notoriously hard to interpret. Especially a comparison of parameter estimates is problematic, both between different models for the same data set and between the same model for different data sets. Effect size measures based on the calculation of marginal effects are proposed as an alternative to standardize the scale of interpretation but can and should not universally erase the effects of differences in scale and heterogeneity. Simulation experiments show how an omitted effect displaces coefficients and marginal effects differently, and an analysis of empirical friendship network data finds that reciprocity and triadic closure reinforce one another when ties are created but partially substitute for one another when ties are maintained, a contrast the coefficients do not reveal.
comment: 91 pages (57 pages main text), 9 figures, 4 tables. Comments welcome

title: Advancing Specific Local Wine Identification through Integration of ICP-MS Mineral Wine Profiles and Machine Learning: A Case Study on Discrimination Among the Ten Beaujolais Crus
authors: Yohann Clément, Pierre Lantéri, Agnès Hagège, Bertrand Chatelet, Théodore Tillement, Coraline Duroux, Leticia Sarlo, François Lux, Olivier Tillement
abstract: The Beaujolais vineyard, located in France's Auvergne-Rh{ô}ne-Alpes region, is internationally recognized for its geological diversity and the strong identity of its ten crus. Guaranteeing authenticity of these appellations is essential for producers and regulators, as mislabeling and fraud can undermine both economic value and consumer trust. In this study, we introduce the Mineral Wine Profile (MWP), a high-throughput ICP-MS protocol enabling the semi-quantitative analysis of more than 40 mineral elements. A total of 1288 Gamay wines from the 2022 and 2023 vintages, collected across the ten Beaujolais crus, were analyzed. Multivariate statistical methods and machine learning were applied to assess their discriminatory power. Principal Component Analysis clearly separated vintages, while Random Forest models achieved 98% accuracy for vintage classification. Mixture Discriminant Analysis further differentiated the ten crus with an average accuracy of 92%. Misclassifications mostly occurred between geographically neighboring crus, reflecting overlapping soil structures and terroir continuity. Element-soil correlations (e.g., Fe enriched in clay-rich soils, Mn in sandy soils, Cs in silty soils) provided mechanistic insights into terroir differentiation. These results confirm that wine mineral fingerprints can act as reliable chemical memories of origin. By combining elemental profiling with Machine Learning, this work demonstrates a robust, reproducible, and scalable approach for intra-regional wine authentication. Beyond its scientific contribution, the MWP approach offers practical applications for the valorization of terroirs, protection of Appellations d'Origine Contr{ô}l{é}e (AOC), and fraud prevention in the wine industry.

title: Value of Adding AI Weather Model Ensembles to a Multi-model Probabilistic Blend
authors: Harris Sop Nkuiate, Gavin Evans, Christopher A. T. Ferro, Frank Kwasniok, Caroline Bain, Stefan Siegert
abstract: Many weather forecasting organizations use a multi-model blend of ensemble members from different prediction systems to obtain a more accurate forecast. Recent studies have shown that blending deterministic AI-based models alongside physics-based models improves the overall forecast skill. However, the incorporation of an ensemble AI-based model into a multi-model blend is yet to be investigated. This study explores the value of blending the ensemble version of the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS-CRPS) with the Met Office's convection permitting physics-based ensemble, MOGREPS-UK. We show that blending site temperature (and wind speed) forecasts over the United Kingdom from both ensemble physics-based and ensemble AI-based models leads to an increase in overall forecast skill spatially, across lead times and across exceedance thresholds, especially when the models have different error characteristics. By decomposing the continuous ranked probability score of the blend into component means and diversity terms, we show that a more accurate blend can be achieved by assigning more weight to more skillful models and using models with complementary errors. For example, we show that a blend of MOGREPS-UK with either AIFS-CRPS or the physics-based Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) is better than a blend of IFS and AIFS-CRPS which are not very diverse. This has implications for the importance of weather model diversity and may lend weight to different model development approaches being pursued in tandem. We also demonstrate that calibrating AIFS-CRPS forecasts yields an increase in forecast skill comparable to calibrated ensemble physics-based forecasts, and calibrating the source forecasts before blending and the blended forecast after blending improves the overall forecast accuracy.
